interpretation_gold: People should not presume to lay claim to things or functions that are far beyond their station.
deepseek_translation: When did the leopard's skin become a mat for a child?
claude_translation: When did the leopard's spots become a toy for children?
gemini_translation: When did the leopard's pouch become a counting game for children?
mistral_translation: When did the leopard's sack turn into a child's plaything?
llama_translation: When does the leopard's cub become a tortoise's child?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against disrespecting or undervaluing something or someone of great importance or dignity.
claude_interpretation: Some things are inherently dangerous and should never be treated casually or as harmless playthings.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb warns against underestimating or trivializing a dangerous situation or person.
mistral_interpretation: One should not underestimate or treat dangerous things as harmless or trivial.
llama_interpretation: It highlights the impossibility of changing one's inherent nature or identity.

yoruba: “Ng óò gba owó-ò mi lára ṣòkòtò yìí”; ìdí làgbàlagbà ńṣí sílẹ̀.
english_literal: “I will get my money's worth out of these trousers”; the grown man only winds up exposing his bare buttocks to the world.
interpretation_gold: One should not insist on squeezing every last once of use out of a perishable article.
deepseek_translation: “I will not take my money out of this pit”; the elder’s wisdom is being revealed.
claude_translation: I will not take my money from these trousers; it is the buttocks that the elder is exposing to the ground
gemini_translation: “I will collect my money from this pair of trousers”; the elder opens his buttocks.
mistral_translation: I will not take my money from this trouser pocket; it is the elders who leave reasons behind
llama_translation: My money is in this pocket; the owner of the cloth is the one who knows the inside
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the value of patience and trust in the wisdom of elders when facing difficult situations.
claude_interpretation: When someone refuses to fulfill their obligations or contribute their fair share, they end up exposing themselves to shame and embarrassment.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the foolishness of making empty threats or boasting about actions that are impossible or self-defeating.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the wisdom of elders in providing explanations or justifications for their actions, which younger people should respect and learn from.
llama_interpretation: Only the person directly involved in a situation truly understands its intricacies.

yoruba: Nígbàtí à ńto ọkà a ò to ti ẹmọ́ si.
english_literal: When we were stacking the corn we did not stack some for the brown rat.
interpretation_gold: People should keep their hands off other people's property unless they have been asked to help themselves.
deepseek_translation: When we are measuring corn, we do not measure that of the squirrel.
claude_translation: When we are planting corn, we do not plant it together with grass.
gemini_translation: When we are counting corn, we do not count the chaff with it.
mistral_translation: When we are soaking cornmeal, we do not yet have the vegetable soup ready.
llama_translation: When it is raining, the frog does not get wet.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should not interfere in matters that do not concern them.
claude_interpretation: One should not mix good things with bad things or associate with negative influences when pursuing worthwhile goals.
gemini_interpretation: It is important to distinguish between what is valuable and what is worthless, and to focus on the former.
mistral_interpretation: Do not count on something that has not yet happened or assume success before completing necessary steps.
llama_interpretation: One who is prepared or has a natural advantage will not be affected by challenges that others face.

yoruba: Nígbàtí o mọ̀-ọ́ gùn, ẹṣin ẹ-ẹ́ ṣe ṣẹ́ orókún?
english_literal: Since you claim to be a seasoned rider, how come your horse has gone lame?
interpretation_gold: An expert does not produce flawed goods.
deepseek_translation: When you knew it was long, did you not see the horse's tail dragging on the ground?
claude_translation: When you know how to climb, did your horse develop a swollen neck?
gemini_translation: When you know how to ride, will the horse refuse to kneel?
mistral_translation: When you do not know how to mount, does the horse refuse to bend its knee?
llama_translation: When you know the depth of the river, how many times will you test the river?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb criticizes willful ignorance or pretending not to notice obvious signs of a problem.
claude_interpretation: Don't blame external factors or make excuses when you have the skills and ability to handle a situation yourself.
gemini_interpretation: Skill and expertise can overcome resistance or make difficult tasks easier.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb teaches that one should take initiative and learn rather than expecting others or circumstances to adjust to their ignorance.
llama_interpretation: One should not repeatedly test or provoke a situation once its danger or depth is known.

yoruba: Ó yẹ ẹni gbogbo kó dínwó aró, kò yẹ atọ̀ọ́lé.
english_literal: It is fitting for everybody to bargain to reduce the cost of dyeing clothes, but not the bed wetter.
interpretation_gold: The person in desperate need of a thing cannot afford to be finicky.
deepseek_translation: It is proper for everyone to reduce the dyeing vat, it is not proper for the dyer.
claude_translation: It is fitting for everyone to contribute to the dye pot, it is not fitting for the lazy person.
gemini_translation: It is proper for everyone to reduce the price of indigo dye, it is not proper for the one who just arrived.
mistral_translation: It is proper for everyone to reduce their indigo dye, but it is not proper for the dyer.
llama_translation: It is not everyone that will buy a cloth, but it is not everyone that will wear it.
deepseek_interpretation: Everyone should contribute to solving a problem, but the expert (dyer) should not be excluded.
claude_interpretation: Everyone should contribute to communal efforts and responsibilities, except those who are unwilling to work.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate for a newcomer to dictate terms or prices, as they lack the established authority or understanding of the community.
mistral_interpretation: One should not abandon their specialized skills or responsibilities even when others are cutting back.
llama_interpretation: Not everyone who has access to something will be able to utilize it effectively.

yoruba: Olóbìnrin kan kì í pagbo ìja.
english_literal: A person who has only  one wife does not form a circle for a fight.
interpretation_gold: A person who does not have enough helping hands should not embark on ventures that are too ambitious.
deepseek_translation: A woman does not provoke a fight.
claude_translation: One woman cannot break up a fight.
gemini_translation: One woman does not break up a fight.
mistral_translation: A certain woman does not join in the crowd to fight
llama_translation: One woman cannot make a fight
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the value of peace and the expectation for women to avoid conflict.
claude_interpretation: Some tasks require collective effort and cannot be accomplished by a single person alone.
gemini_interpretation: A single individual, especially when outnumbered, may not be able to resolve a conflict or overcome a challenge alone.
mistral_interpretation: It advises against blindly following others into conflict or trouble without considering one's own values or safety
llama_interpretation: A single person cannot cause conflict or chaos.

yoruba: Ohun tí eèrá bá lè gbé ní ńpè ní ìgànnìkó.
english_literal: Whatever the ant is able to carry is what it says is its full measure.
interpretation_gold: One should match one's desires to what one can afford.
deepseek_translation: What the ant can carry is called a load.
claude_translation: What an ant can carry is what it calls a heavy load.
gemini_translation: What the ant can carry, it calls a burden.
mistral_translation: What the ant can carry is called a mere trifle
llama_translation: What the wind can carry is called a kite.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that one should only take on responsibilities or tasks they are capable of handling.
claude_interpretation: People should only take on responsibilities or challenges that match their capabilities and capacity.
gemini_interpretation: One should only take on responsibilities or tasks that are within their capacity.
mistral_interpretation: What may seem insignificant to one person can be a great burden or achievement for another
llama_interpretation: One's abilities or circumstances can determine their limitations or potential.

yoruba: Ó bọ́ lọ́wọ́ iyọ̀ ó dòbu.
english_literal: Salt loses its good quality and becomes like saltpeter.
interpretation_gold: A person who has been written off loses all regard.
deepseek_translation: It slipped from the hand and fell into the mortar.
claude_translation: It slipped from the hands of salt and fell into the pit.
gemini_translation: It escaped from the salt, it became tasteless.
mistral_translation: He who wraps his hand with salt will lick it
llama_translation: The one who is dancing is the one who is being beaten
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that carelessness can lead to loss or unintended consequences.
claude_interpretation: Something valuable was carelessly lost due to negligence or lack of proper handling.
gemini_interpretation: Something that avoids a beneficial influence may lose its essential quality or purpose.
mistral_interpretation: One who creates a problem for themselves will inevitably suffer the consequences
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the idea that those who engage in reckless or foolish behavior will ultimately suffer the consequences.

yoruba: O dájú dánu, o ò mọ ẹ̀sán mẹ́sàn-án.
english_literal: Your eyes flinch not and your mouth is unstoppable, but you do not know nine times nine.
interpretation_gold: Too much mouth often indicates too little substance.
deepseek_translation: You swear falsely, you do not know the nine hundred and ninety-nine.
claude_translation: You are certain of waste/loss, you don't know revenge/retaliation threefold.
gemini_translation: You threw away the eye, you don't know the nine nines.
mistral_translation: It is too certain to be lost, yet you do not know its nine times nine (81) benefits.
llama_translation: It is sweet to be alive, but it is not known how many days one has.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against dishonesty, implying that deceitful actions will eventually lead to unforeseen consequences.
claude_interpretation: When you carelessly cause harm or loss to others, you don't realize that the consequences or retaliation you'll face will be much greater than what you inflicted.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that one cannot truly understand or appreciate something without first having a foundational understanding or experience of it.
mistral_interpretation: Overconfidence in something valuable can blind one to its full potential or hidden advantages.
llama_interpretation: One should appreciate life while it lasts, because its duration is uncertain.

yoruba: Olówó ní ḿbá ọlọ́rọ̀-ọ́ rìn; ẹgbẹ́ ní ḿbá ẹgbẹ́ ṣeré.
english_literal: It is a rich person that keeps company with a wealthy person; only people of equal standing play together.
interpretation_gold: One should associate with one's equals.
deepseek_translation: The rich walk with the rich; the poor play with the poor.
claude_translation: The wealthy person walks with the wealthy person; peers play with peers
gemini_translation: The rich associate with the rich; peers play with peers.
mistral_translation: A rich person walks with a poor person; a peer walks with a peer to play
llama_translation: Money is what the rich use to play; the poor use their poor group to play.
deepseek_interpretation: People tend to associate with others of similar social or economic status.
claude_interpretation: People naturally associate and form relationships with others of similar social status, wealth, or circumstances.
gemini_interpretation: People tend to associate with others of similar social standing or background.
mistral_interpretation: People tend to associate with those who share similar status or circumstances as themselves.
llama_interpretation: Wealthy people use their money to have fun, while the less privileged rely on community and friendship for enjoyment.

yoruba: Ohun tí wèré fi ńse ara ẹ̀, ó pọ̀ ju ohun tó fi ńṣẹ ọmọ ẹlòmíràn lọ.
english_literal: What the imbecile does to himself is far worse than what he does to others.
interpretation_gold: Said what a person intending to injure others in fact does himself or herself greater injury.
deepseek_translation: What the mad person uses on himself is more than what he uses on another person's child.
claude_translation: What a mad person does to himself is more than what he does to another person's child.
gemini_translation: What a mad person does to themselves is more than what they do to another person's child.
mistral_translation: What a madman uses to harm himself is more than what he uses to harm another person's child.
llama_translation: What a madman uses to take care of himself is more than what is used to take care of another person's child
deepseek_interpretation: People often prioritize their own well-being over that of others.
claude_interpretation: A person harms themselves more through their own foolish actions than they could ever harm others.
gemini_interpretation: People often inflict more harm or trouble upon themselves than they do upon others.
mistral_interpretation: People often cause more harm to themselves through their own reckless actions than they do to others.
llama_interpretation: One's own needs and priorities should take precedence over the needs of others.

yoruba: Oúnjẹ ọmọ kékeré a máa wọ àgbà nínú; òrùka ọmọ kékeré ni kì í wọ ágbá lọ́wọ́.
english_literal: A youth's food can enter the stomach of an elder; it is only a youth's ring that cannot slip unto an elder's finger.
interpretation_gold: An elder may take advantage of the youth in certain respects, but in some others an elder must respect his status.
deepseek_translation: The food of a small child will enter an elder's belly; the ring of a small child will not enter an elder's hand.
claude_translation: A small child's food can enter an adult's stomach; a small child's ring cannot fit on an adult's finger.
gemini_translation: The food of a small child enters an elder; the ring of a small child does not fit an elder's hand.
mistral_translation: The food of a small child will enter an elder's stomach; the ring of a small child does not go onto an elder's hand
llama_translation: The food of a small child is not put in the mouth of an elder; the load of a small child is not carried by an elder.
deepseek_interpretation: Children's possessions may be taken by elders, but some things (like rings) are too personal or small to be appropriated.
claude_interpretation: Some things can be shared across generations while others are specifically suited to particular stages of life.
gemini_interpretation: While elders can partake in the simple provisions of the young, they cannot adopt their roles or responsibilities, which are often too small or inappropriate for their experience and status.
mistral_interpretation: Children's resources or possessions are often used or controlled by elders, but certain boundaries or respect must still be maintained.
llama_interpretation: Responsibilities should be matched to one's capabilities and age.

yoruba: Ó bọ́ lọ́wọ́ oṣù ó dàràn-mọ́jú.
english_literal: The moon loses its esteem and shines all night long.
interpretation_gold: A person who overstays his/her welcome ceases to be valued.
deepseek_translation: It exceeds the month's money, it becomes debt.
claude_translation: It fell from the hand of the moon and became a shooting star
gemini_translation: It escaped the hand of the moon, it committed a crime in the dark.
mistral_translation: He who lends money to the moon will have his eyes spoiled (from staring).
llama_translation: He who is in the market does not know the day is dark
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against spending beyond one's means, as it leads to debt.
claude_interpretation: Something that was once stable and elevated has fallen and become fleeting or transient.
gemini_interpretation: Something that avoids scrutiny in the light of day will inevitably reveal its true, negative nature in the cover of darkness.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against futile efforts or investments that are doomed to fail, as recovery is impossible.
llama_interpretation: One who is deeply involved in a situation may not be aware of its true nature.

yoruba: Ohun méjì ló yẹ Ẹ̀ṣọ́: Ẹ̀ṣọ́ jà, ó lé ogun; Ẹ̀ṣọ́ jà ó kú sógun.
english_literal: Only two things are proper for a warrior: the warrior goes to war and drives the enemy off; the warrior goes to war and dies in battle.
interpretation_gold: One should not act in a way that is not proper or becoming.
deepseek_translation: Two things are proper for a warrior: the warrior fights and conquers in war; the warrior fights and dies in war.
claude_translation: Two things befit Esho: Esho fights and drives away war; Esho fights and dies in war.
gemini_translation: Two things befit Eṣọ: Eṣọ fought, he won the war; Eṣọ fought, he died in the war.
mistral_translation: There are two things that suit the warrior: the warrior fights, he wins the war; the warrior fights, he dies in war.
llama_translation: Two things are expected of the horse: the horse runs, it wins the war; the horse runs, it dies in the war.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that a warrior must accept both victory and death as possible outcomes of battle.
claude_interpretation: A warrior's honor lies in either achieving victory or dying with dignity in battle.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights that in any significant endeavor, there are only two possible outcomes: success or failure.
mistral_interpretation: A true warrior must be prepared for either victory or death in battle, as both outcomes are honorable.
llama_interpretation: One's actions can lead to either success or failure, highlighting the duality of risk and reward.

yoruba: Olójúkan kì í tàkìtì òró.
english_literal: A one-eyed person does not attempt standing somersaults.
interpretation_gold: One should limit one's ambition to one's capability.
deepseek_translation: A person with eyes does not stumble over words.
claude_translation: A one-eyed person does not wink playfully at secrets.
gemini_translation: A one-eyed person does not wrestle in the dark.
mistral_translation: A person with one eye does not sell kola-nut gossip.
llama_translation: The one who is not present does not get a share of the discussion.
deepseek_interpretation: A wise or observant person avoids unnecessary conflicts or mistakes.
claude_interpretation: Someone with limited resources or abilities cannot afford to be careless or wasteful with what they have.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to engage in activities where one's disadvantages are amplified, as it leads to certain failure.
mistral_interpretation: Those who lack full understanding or perspective should avoid spreading unverified information.
llama_interpretation: Those who are absent or not involved in a situation cannot expect to benefit from it.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká fàbúrò ẹni ṣaya.
english_literal: One should not become so desperate that one takes one's younger sister as wife.
interpretation_gold: Desperation should not preempt propriety.
deepseek_translation: The eye does not become so swollen that it prevents one from seeing.
claude_translation: The eye does not deceive one to the extent that one mistakes another person for one's wife
gemini_translation: One does not suffer hardship and then marry one's younger sibling.
mistral_translation: The eye does not become swollen enough to marry one's younger sibling
llama_translation: The eye does not see the back of the head of the person who is going
deepseek_interpretation: No matter how severe a problem may seem, it should not stop one from finding a solution or moving forward.
claude_interpretation: Some things are so familiar and important to us that we cannot be mistaken about them, no matter the circumstances.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate to seek comfort or solutions from those who are meant to be protected or supported by you, especially in times of difficulty.
mistral_interpretation: Excessive anger or jealousy should not lead one to harm or disrespect their own family members.
llama_interpretation: One cannot know what the future holds for another person.

yoruba: Olówó ní ńjẹ iyán ẹgbàá.
english_literal: It is a rich person that eats pounded yams worth two thousand cowries.
interpretation_gold: One's level of consumption is a reflection of the depth of one's pocket.
deepseek_translation: The rich man eats pounded yam two hundred times.
claude_translation: The rich person is the one eating pounded yam worth a thousand.
gemini_translation: It is the rich person who eats pounded yam worth two thousand cowries.
mistral_translation: It is the rich person who eats pounded yam worth a hundred cowries
llama_translation: Money is eating pounded yam in the market
deepseek_interpretation: Wealth affords one the luxury of abundance and repeated indulgence.
claude_interpretation: Wealth is demonstrated through one's ability to afford expensive or luxurious things.
gemini_interpretation: Only those with ample resources can afford extravagant things.
mistral_interpretation: Wealth affords luxuries and privileges that the poor cannot access, highlighting economic disparity.
llama_interpretation: Wealth and prosperity are being enjoyed by others in public.

yoruba: O kò mọ ẹ̀wà lóńjẹ à-jẹ-sùn.
english_literal: You do not know what black eyed peas are like for dinner.
interpretation_gold: Addressed to a person who is not mindful of the repercussions of his/her behavior.
deepseek_translation: He does not know beauty eats sleep.
claude_translation: He does not know the beauty that is being eaten while sleeping
gemini_translation: You do not know the beauty in food that is eaten and slept on.
mistral_translation: He does not know beans who eats the 'sleep-eater'.
llama_translation: He does not know character, he eats and sleeps
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that obsession with superficial beauty can lead to neglect of essential needs like rest.
claude_interpretation: One fails to appreciate or recognize the good things they are enjoying effortlessly or unconsciously.
gemini_interpretation: One often fails to appreciate the value or benefit of something until it is fully experienced or utilized.
mistral_interpretation: One who lacks wisdom or discernment may unknowingly engage in harmful or self-destructive actions.
llama_interpretation: One's true nature is revealed in their daily habits and behavior.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká pọ́n léhín.
english_literal: One's circumstances do not so deteriorate that one becomes red in teeth.
interpretation_gold: Adverse circumstances should not keep one from attending to essential matters.
deepseek_translation: The eye does not cost more than the back of the head.
claude_translation: The eye does not deceive one to be deceived from behind.
gemini_translation: The eye does not suffer hardship and then suffer hardship again at the back.
mistral_translation: The eyes do not meet each other to meet behind
llama_translation: The eyes do not see the back of the head
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should not prioritize superficial appearances over deeper, more important matters.
claude_interpretation: What you can see clearly with your own eyes cannot mislead you like things happening behind your back.
gemini_interpretation: One should not experience hardship in one area only to face it again in another, implying that problems should be resolved or not compounded.
mistral_interpretation: One should not scheme or plot against someone who is not present or unaware.
llama_interpretation: One cannot know everything about oneself or one's own situation.

yoruba: Ohun tó yẹni ló yẹni; okùn ọrùn ò yẹ adìẹ.
english_literal: Whatever is becoming for a person is what is becoming; a noose is not becoming for a chicken.
interpretation_gold: One should always confine one's actions to those that are proper and becoming.
deepseek_translation: What fits a person is what fits them; a rope does not fit a chicken.
claude_translation: What suits one suits one; a neck chain does not suit a chicken.
gemini_translation: What suits one is what suits one; a necklace does not suit a chicken.
mistral_translation: What suits one is suitable for one; a neck rope does not suit a chicken
llama_translation: What is mine is mine; the sea does not own a chicken
deepseek_interpretation: Each person has what suits them best, and what works for one may not work for another.
claude_interpretation: Different things are appropriate for different people based on their nature and circumstances.
gemini_interpretation: One should only aspire to or accept things that are appropriate and beneficial for their nature or situation.
mistral_interpretation: What is appropriate for one person or situation may not be suitable for another
llama_interpretation: One should not covet or take what belongs to another.

yoruba: Owó ẹ̀yẹ ò sú ẹni-í san; tọ̀ràn ni ò súnwọ̀n.
english_literal: People have no difficulty paying the money for glorious events; it is the money for trouble that is unpleasant to pay.
interpretation_gold: The trouble one goes into for honorable purposes are really a pleasure, not so the trouble to extricate oneself from problems.
deepseek_translation: The money of the guinea fowl does not make one rich; it is the advice that is valuable.
claude_translation: A bird's feathers do not make one pay; it is debt that is not pleasant.
gemini_translation: The bird's money is not what is difficult to pay; it is the matter (the problem) that is not good.
mistral_translation: A bird's money does not satisfy its owner; it is advice that is truly valuable.
llama_translation: Money of the bird does not sleep with its owner; it is shared among the nest.
deepseek_interpretation: Material wealth is fleeting, but wise counsel endures and brings true prosperity.
claude_interpretation: Natural gifts or talents are freely given, but obligations and debts create burdens and discomfort.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb suggests that the cost of something is often not the real issue, but rather the underlying problem or circumstance that makes it difficult to afford or resolve.
mistral_interpretation: Material wealth alone is insufficient without wisdom or guidance to use it wisely.
llama_interpretation: Wealth should be shared with family and community, not hoarded by one person.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọnni ká fàkísà bora.
english_literal: One should never be so benighted that one covers oneself in rags.
interpretation_gold: Despite adverse circumstances, one should strive to maintain one's dignity.
deepseek_translation: The eye does not swell to the point of covering the body with a cloth.
claude_translation: The eye does not deceive one to cover oneself with rags
gemini_translation: The eye does not suffer hardship and then cover itself with rags.
mistral_translation: The eye does not deceive someone to the extent of tearing a rag to shreds
llama_translation: The eyes do not meet to make a needle
deepseek_interpretation: One should not exaggerate or overreact to minor issues.
claude_interpretation: What you can clearly see with your own eyes should guide your decisions rather than relying on false appearances or deception.
gemini_interpretation: One should not add to their troubles or neglect their appearance even in difficult times.
mistral_interpretation: One should not act recklessly based on mere appearances without proper verification or understanding
llama_interpretation: Collaboration and collective effort are necessary to achieve a complex task.

yoruba: Ojú iná kọ́ lewùrà ńhurun.
english_literal: It is not in the presence of the flame that water-yam grows hair.
interpretation_gold: One dares not strut when one's bane is around.
deepseek_translation: The eye of fire cannot see gold.
claude_translation: It is not the face of fire that makes the salt cry.
gemini_translation: The face of the fire does not grow hair on the ewura (yam).
mistral_translation: The eye of fire cannot wear a gold necklace on its neck
llama_translation: The eyes of fire do not see the smoke
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that anger or haste can blind one to valuable opportunities or truths.
claude_interpretation: External appearances or threats are not always the true cause of one's problems or distress.
gemini_interpretation: Direct confrontation or harshness is not conducive to growth or positive outcomes.
mistral_interpretation: One cannot adorn or beautify something inherently dangerous or destructive
llama_interpretation: One who is passionate or angry may not notice the consequences of their actions.

yoruba: Olóyè kékeré kì í ṣe fáàárí níwájú ọba.
english_literal: A minor chief should not act garrulously in the presence of a king.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's station and act accordingly.
deepseek_translation: A small chief does not make a proclamation in front of the king.
claude_translation: A minor chief does not boast in front of the king.
gemini_translation: A small chief does not boast in the presence of a king.
mistral_translation: A minor chief does not announce the king's arrival in the king's presence
llama_translation: A small chief does not make a loud noise in the presence of a king.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not overstep their authority or position in the presence of a superior.
claude_interpretation: One should show respect and humility when in the presence of those in higher authority or status.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate for someone of lesser status or authority to show off or act arrogantly in the presence of a superior.
mistral_interpretation: It is inappropriate for a person of lower status to take on the role or authority of someone superior in their presence
llama_interpretation: One should show humility and respect in the presence of a superior or someone of higher authority.

yoruba: Ó yẹ ẹni gbogbo kó sọ pé “Ọlọ́run a-ṣèkan-má-kù,” kò yẹ akúkó.
english_literal: Everyone can justifiably say, “God, who has left nothing undone,” but not a eunuch.
interpretation_gold: People should not act as though they are unaware of their flaws.
deepseek_translation: It is proper for everyone to say 'God the one who creates and does not lack,' it is not proper for the rooster.
claude_translation: It is fitting for everyone to say 'God who does one thing and does not die,' it is not fitting for a rooster.
gemini_translation: It is fitting for everyone to say 'God who does not leave anything undone,' but it is not fitting for the rooster.
mistral_translation: It is proper for everyone to say 'God is the one who creates and never runs short,' but it is not proper for a rooster
llama_translation: It is not everyone that you tell that “God is not asleep,” it is not a chicken.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes humility and the recognition of divine providence, contrasting human gratitude with the rooster's natural behavior.
claude_interpretation: Humans can praise God's eternal nature and power, but creatures like roosters should not presume to make such declarations about divinity.
gemini_interpretation: It is appropriate for humans to acknowledge God's perfection and completeness, but not for a rooster, as it lacks the capacity for such understanding.
mistral_interpretation: One should not boast or claim credit for what only God can provide.
llama_interpretation: Not everyone can be trusted with sensitive information.

yoruba: Onígẹ̀gẹ́ fìlẹ̀kẹ̀ dọ́pọ̀; onílẹ̀kẹ̀ ìbá gbowo, ko rọ́rùn fìlẹ̀kẹ̀ so.
english_literal: The person with goitre offers a ridiculously low price for beads; were the beads seller to accept her offer she would have no neck to string the beads around.
interpretation_gold: One can always find a ruse to get one out of embarrassing situations.
deepseek_translation: The lazy person's hoe is heavy; the hardworking person's hoe is light.
claude_translation: The owner of ginger mixed it with pepper; if the owner of pepper had money, it wouldn't be easy to mix pepper.
gemini_translation: The one who wears beads on their neck is in a high position; if the bead-wearer were to collect money, it would be easy to wear beads.
mistral_translation: The bead-stringer leaves beads scattered; the bead-wearer, if they had money, would not find it easy to string beads.
llama_translation: The weaver's wife has a wrapper; the owner of the house has a cloth, but the weaver's wife's wrapper is not as good as the owner of the house's cloth.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that laziness makes tasks seem difficult, while diligence makes them easier.
claude_interpretation: Those who have valuable things often undervalue them, while those who lack such things understand their true worth.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights that positions of honor or status often come with responsibilities and expectations that are not always easy to fulfill, despite the outward appearance of ease or privilege.
mistral_interpretation: Those who neglect their responsibilities often create difficulties for others who must then take on the burden.
llama_interpretation: One's own possessions are often less valued than those of others.

yoruba: Ò ńjàgbọ̀nrín èṣín lọ́bẹ̀, o ní o ti tó tán.
english_literal: You are reduced to eating last year's antelope in your stew, and yet you claim to have attained the height of good fortune.
interpretation_gold: A hard-up person who claims to be prosperous deceives him/herself.
deepseek_translation: The horse is galloping in the forest, you say it has finished running.
claude_translation: You are not taking the horse to the river, yet you say you have watered it enough.
gemini_translation: You are struggling to find a deer in the soup, and you say you are full.
mistral_translation: You are cutting the tail of a horse with a razor, and you say it is not yet finished
llama_translation: The one who is riding a horse is on the road, he says he has arrived.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against premature conclusions or underestimating someone's potential based on initial observations.
claude_interpretation: You cannot claim to have completed a task or fulfilled a responsibility when you haven't even begun the necessary work.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the absurdity of claiming satisfaction or completion when a crucial and expected element is missing or yet to be found.
mistral_interpretation: It highlights the futility of an endless or overly meticulous task that yields no meaningful progress
llama_interpretation: One should not claim to have achieved a goal until the journey is actually completed.

yoruba: Olómele kì í sọ pé igi yó dàá lóde lọ́la.
english_literal: The omele drummer does not vow that there will be an earth-shaking performance on the morrow.
interpretation_gold: If one has no say, one should avoid making projections or promises.
deepseek_translation: The woodcarver does not say that the wood will fall tomorrow.
claude_translation: The honey gatherer does not say that wood will be scarce in the forest tomorrow
gemini_translation: The drummer does not say that the tree will fall outside tomorrow.
mistral_translation: The owner of the farm does not say that the tree will fall outside tomorrow
llama_translation: The one who climbs the tree does not say that the tree is tall on the ground
deepseek_interpretation: One should not make assumptions about uncertain future events.
claude_interpretation: An expert in their field does not worry about the availability of their basic tools or resources.
gemini_interpretation: One should not postpone or delay important tasks, especially those that are time-sensitive or require immediate attention.
mistral_interpretation: One should not make assumptions about future events or outcomes beyond their control
llama_interpretation: One should not underestimate a challenge until they have experienced it firsthand.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́n baálé ilé kó fọwọ́ gbálẹ̀ ilé ẹ̀.
english_literal: A head of a household is never so hard up that he sweeps his compound with his bare hands.
interpretation_gold: However desperate one might be, there are certain things one must not stoop to do.
deepseek_translation: The eye does not get tired of looking at the ceiling until it falls.
claude_translation: The eye does not pain the head of the house for him to wash his hands of his house.
gemini_translation: The head of the household does not become poor and then sweep his house with his hand.
mistral_translation: The eyes do not gather the owner of the house to sweep the house for him
llama_translation: The eyes do not meet the owner of the house to go and steal the owner of the house's property.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against overconfidence or neglecting vigilance, as even the seemingly stable can fail unexpectedly.
claude_interpretation: A leader should not abandon their responsibilities or give up on their domain because of minor troubles or irritations.
gemini_interpretation: A person in a position of authority or responsibility should not resort to undignified or desperate measures, even in times of hardship.
mistral_interpretation: One should not expect others to take responsibility for their own duties or problems.
llama_interpretation: One should not take advantage of someone's trust or hospitality to exploit them.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́n ẹdun kó dẹni ilẹ̀; ìṣẹ́ kì í ṣẹ́ igún kó di ojúgbà adìẹ.
english_literal: The colobus monkey is never so reduced in circumstances that it becomes a land-hugging creature; the vulture is never so badly off that it becomes the equal of a chicken.
interpretation_gold: No matter one's misfortune one should maintain one's dignity.
deepseek_translation: The eye does not swell from tears to become the owner of the land; labor does not labor like the vulture to become the equal of the chicken.
claude_translation: The eye does not deceive the monkey so it falls to the ground; work does not fail the vulture so it becomes a chicken's gathering place.
gemini_translation: The face of a monkey does not become red and then it becomes a ground dweller; a vulture does not become poor and then it becomes a peer of the chicken.
mistral_translation: The eye does not gather firewood to become a baboon; hard work does not turn a vulture into a chicken's peer.
llama_translation: The eyes do not meet the festival and reach the house; the work does not meet the vulture and become the vulture's share.
deepseek_interpretation: Hard work alone does not guarantee success or elevate one's status.
claude_interpretation: Those who are naturally skilled or experienced in their domain rarely fail due to their inherent abilities and diligent effort.
gemini_interpretation: One's inherent nature or status does not change due to temporary hardship or circumstances.
mistral_interpretation: Natural limitations and inherent traits cannot be overcome by effort alone, as one's true nature remains unchanged.
llama_interpretation: One should not expect to reap the benefits of a situation without putting in the necessary effort or contribution.

yoruba: “Òru ò molówó” nIfá tí à ńdá fún “Ìwọ ta nìyẹn?”
english_literal: “The dark of night knows not who is a wealthy person” is the oracle one delivers to “Who might that be?”
interpretation_gold: Night-time wanderers should be prepared for indignities.
deepseek_translation: "Darkness is not wealth" Ifa that we are casting for "Who are you?"
claude_translation: Night does not know the wealthy person is the Ifa divination cast for Who are you?
gemini_translation: “Night does not know the wealthy” is the Ifa divination cast for “Who are you?”
mistral_translation: “The night does not have money” is the Ifá verse recited for “You who are selling that?”
llama_translation: The night does not befriend the thief, Ifá says to him 'What do you want here?'
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that obscurity or lack of clarity (symbolized by darkness) holds no value and questions one's true identity or purpose.
claude_interpretation: Death and misfortune do not discriminate based on wealth or social status, treating all people equally regardless of their material possessions.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights that in the darkness of night, social status and identity become irrelevant, emphasizing the equality of all people when stripped of their outward distinctions.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb warns against engaging in suspicious or dubious transactions, especially at odd hours when trust is low.
llama_interpretation: One's misdeeds will ultimately expose and condemn them.

yoruba: Òkété pẹ̀lú ọmọ ẹ̀-ẹ́ di ọgbọọgba sínú ihò; nígba tí ìyá ńfehín pàkùrọ́, ọmọ náà ńfehín pa pẹ̀lú.
english_literal: The giant bush rat and its child become equals in their hole; the mother cracks palm-nuts with its teeth, and the child does the same thing.
interpretation_gold: Too much familiarity makes comrades of people who are quite distant from each other in standing.
deepseek_translation: The rat digs a hole with its child; when the mother is removing dirt, the child is also removing dirt.
claude_translation: The giant rat and its child become numerous in the hole; when the mother is backing to dig, the child is also backing to dig along.
gemini_translation: The giant rat and its young do not enter the hole equally; while the mother is cracking palm kernels, the young one is also cracking with its teeth.
mistral_translation: The giant rat with its young becomes trapped in a hole; when the mother tries to escape, the young one also tries to escape with it.
llama_translation: The hen's chick is a chick in the bush; when the mother is scratching the ground, the chick is also scratching the ground.
deepseek_interpretation: Children learn by imitating their parents' actions and behaviors.
claude_interpretation: Children naturally imitate and learn from their parents' behaviors and actions.
gemini_interpretation: Children learn and imitate the behaviors and habits of their parents, even when those behaviors are not explicitly taught.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb warns that one's actions or misfortunes can inadvertently affect those dependent on them, especially in times of crisis.
llama_interpretation: Children often imitate the actions of their parents or elders.

yoruba: Odò kékeré lalákàn-án ti lè fọ́ epo; bó bá di àgàdàm̀gbá tán, odò a gbé alákàn lọ.
english_literal: It is only in a small stream that the crab can make its oil; when it becomes huge and swift the river sweeps the crab away.
interpretation_gold: When times are easy there is little one cannot attempt.
deepseek_translation: A small river can carry palm oil; when it becomes a mighty river, the river will carry the palm oil seller away.
claude_translation: A small river can break the palm oil seller's calabash; when it becomes a great flood, the river will carry the palm oil seller away.
gemini_translation: It is in a small river that a crab can break palm kernels; if it becomes a raging torrent, the river will carry the crab away.
mistral_translation: It is the small river that the crab can jump over; when it becomes a big river, the crab will be carried away by the river.
llama_translation: A small stream can carry away a snail shell; but when it becomes a mighty river, it carries away a canoe.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that small beginnings can lead to uncontrollable consequences if not managed wisely.
claude_interpretation: Small problems that are ignored can grow into much larger ones that become overwhelming and destructive.
gemini_interpretation: It is wise to address challenges and seize opportunities when they are manageable, as waiting until they become overwhelming can lead to failure.
mistral_interpretation: Small challenges can be overcome easily, but as they grow, they may become too difficult to handle.
llama_interpretation: Even the smallest and seemingly insignificant can have a profound impact when given the opportunity to grow and develop.

yoruba: Ojú ò ti oníṣègùn, ó ní àna òun ńkú lọ.
english_literal: The medicine man lacks all shame, he announces that his parent-in-law is dying.
interpretation_gold: If one cannot do what is expected of one, one should at least not broadcast one's shame.
deepseek_translation: The patient's eyes are not on the herbalist, he says his relative is dying.
claude_translation: The medicine man's eyes are not yet open, he says his mother-in-law is dying away.
gemini_translation: The herbalist is not ashamed, he says his in-law is dying.
mistral_translation: The eye that belongs to the healer says its neighbor is dying
llama_translation: The eye that is not treated, says it is going to die
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against neglecting immediate help in favor of distant or unavailable solutions.
claude_interpretation: A person who cannot solve their own problems should not be trusted to solve others' problems.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights hypocrisy or a lack of shame when someone prioritizes personal gain or convenience over their professional duty or the well-being of others.
mistral_interpretation: People often overlook their own flaws while criticizing others.
llama_interpretation: One who refuses to seek help or advice will ultimately suffer the consequences.

yoruba: Orí awọ là ḿbágbà.
english_literal: It is on the hide that one finds the elder.
interpretation_gold: One should always live up to what others expect of one.
deepseek_translation: The head and the neck are together.
claude_translation: It is the head of the plate that we break first
gemini_translation: It is with a tough head that one meets old age.
mistral_translation: It is the head of the leopard that I am greeting.
llama_translation: The head that is adorned is the one that is revered.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the inseparable relationship between two entities, often used to describe close bonds or dependencies between people or things.
claude_interpretation: Leadership or those in prominent positions bear the greatest risk and face consequences first when trouble comes.
gemini_interpretation: One needs resilience and strength to endure the challenges and difficulties that come with aging and life.
mistral_interpretation: One should acknowledge and respect those in positions of authority or strength.
llama_interpretation: Respect and recognition are earned through one's accomplishments and good character.

yoruba: Orí àgbà-á níyì, ó sàn ju orí àgbà-á fọ́ lọ.
english_literal: The-elderly-person's-head-deserves-respect is better than The-elderly-person's-head-is-damaged.
interpretation_gold: An elder who enjoys respect is better off than one who is insulted by others.
deepseek_translation: The head of an elder is respected, it is better than the head of an elder that has fallen.
claude_translation: The head of an elder is honorable, it is better than the head of an elder being broken.
gemini_translation: The head of an elder has dignity, it is better than the head of an elder breaking.
mistral_translation: The head of an elder is honorable, it is better than the head of an elder that is bald
llama_translation: The elder's head is wise, it surpasses the elder's head in wisdom.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the value of respecting and honoring elders while they are alive, as their wisdom and guidance are irreparable once they are gone.
claude_interpretation: It is better to respect and preserve the dignity of elders than to cause them harm or disgrace.
gemini_interpretation: It is better to respect and preserve the wisdom and authority of elders than to disregard or destroy it.
mistral_interpretation: Respect for elders is more valuable than their physical appearance or shortcomings.
llama_interpretation: Experience and wisdom are not solely the preserve of the elderly, as younger ones can also possess great wisdom.

yoruba: O ru ládugbó ò ńrerá; kí ni ká sọ fẹ́ni tó ru Òrìṣà-a Yemọja?
english_literal: Because you are carrying a huge pot you strut; what would one say to the person carrying the divinity Yemoja?
interpretation_gold: Never assume to be more important than you are, especially when there are really more important people around.
deepseek_translation: He who carries a load at the crossroads does not stagger; what can we say of someone who carries the load of the goddess Yemoja?
claude_translation: He carries a load in the neighborhood and is not sweating; what shall we say about one who carries the deity Yemoja?
gemini_translation: You carry a neighbor and boast; what should we say to someone who carries the Òrìṣà Yemọja?
mistral_translation: The one who carries a mortar on the street does not run; why should we say the one who carries the deity Yemọja is in love?
llama_translation: The one who is at the riverbank does not wash; what will one who is at the riverbank of the goddess Yemọja do?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb highlights the strength and resilience of those who bear greater responsibilities or burdens, comparing them to the divine endurance of Yemoja's devotees.
claude_interpretation: If someone can handle a lesser task with ease, imagine how much more capable they would be with a greater responsibility or challenge.
gemini_interpretation: One should not boast about small achievements when others have accomplished much greater feats.
mistral_interpretation: One should not judge or assume the intentions of others based on their burdens or responsibilities.
llama_interpretation: One who is close to a source of power or knowledge should take advantage of it.

yoruba: Òní, ẹtú jìnfìn, ọ̀la, ẹtú jìnfìn; ẹtu nìkan lẹran tó wà nígbó?
english_literal: Today, the antelope falls into the ditch; tomorrow, the antelope falls into the ditch; is the antelope the only animal in the forest?
interpretation_gold: If a person is the only one misfortune always visits, there is probably something the person is doing to invite it.
deepseek_translation: Today, the duiker is lean, tomorrow, the duiker is lean; is the duiker the only animal in the forest?
claude_translation: Today, we eat guinea fowl, tomorrow, we eat guinea fowl; is guinea fowl the only meat in the forest?
gemini_translation: Today, the antelope is hunted, tomorrow, the antelope is hunted; is the antelope the only animal in the forest?
mistral_translation: Today, the partridge is plentiful, tomorrow, the partridge is plentiful; is it only the partridge that is meat in the forest?
llama_translation: Today, the cloth is torn, tomorrow, the cloth is torn; is it only the cloth that is troublesome in the world?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises patience and persistence, suggesting that opportunities are not limited to a single option.
claude_interpretation: One should not limit themselves to only one option when many alternatives are available.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to repeatedly exploit or burden the same individual or resource when other options are available.
mistral_interpretation: Do not rely on a single option or resource, as there are always alternatives.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the idea that problems and troubles are a normal part of life.

yoruba: Ogun tí olójúméjìí rí sá ni olójúkan-án ní òún ńlọ jà.
english_literal: The war that the two-eyed person saw and fled is the same the one-eyed person vows he will join.
interpretation_gold: A comment on overreaching people who attempt feats that have defeated their betters.
deepseek_translation: The war that a person with two eyes sees and runs away from is the one a one-eyed person is going to fight.
claude_translation: The war that the two-eyed person ran away from is what the one-eyed person says he is going to fight.
gemini_translation: The war that a two-eyed person saw and fled, a one-eyed person says he is going to fight.
mistral_translation: The war that two-eyed people see as a mere chase is being fought seriously by the one-eyed person.
llama_translation: The god of iron that two people see is the one that the one-eyed person is going to fight
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against underestimating challenges that others have wisely avoided.
claude_interpretation: Those with less ability or experience often boast about tackling challenges that even more capable people have wisely avoided.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to attempt a task that someone with more experience or ability has already deemed impossible or too dangerous.
mistral_interpretation: What may seem trivial or insignificant to some can be a matter of great importance or survival to others.
llama_interpretation: A person with a disability or limitation can still achieve their goals and overcome challenges.

yoruba: Ohun tí kò tó okòó kì í jẹ àgbà níyà.
english_literal: A thing that is not worth the least amount of money should not prove a hardship for an elder.
interpretation_gold: One should not be defeated by insignificant problems.
deepseek_translation: What is not enough for a boat does not trouble an elder.
claude_translation: What is not worth a penny does not cause an elder suffering
gemini_translation: What is not worth twenty cowries does not trouble an elder.
mistral_translation: What is not enough for a hoe does not become food for an elder
llama_translation: Something that is not up to the farm cannot be eaten as a yam.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not worry about insignificant matters that do not concern you.
claude_interpretation: Wise and experienced people do not let trivial or worthless matters cause them distress or worry.
gemini_interpretation: An elder or a wise person does not concern themselves with trivial matters.
mistral_interpretation: One should not take on responsibilities or burdens beyond their capacity, as it may lead to failure or disgrace.
llama_interpretation: One must not expect to reap benefits from something that has not been properly invested in or nurtured.

yoruba: Ojú àlejò la ti ńjẹ gbèsè; ẹ̀hìn-in ẹ̀ là ńsan án.
english_literal: It is in a visitor's presence that one gets into debt; it is in her absence that one repays the debt.
interpretation_gold: One does not estimate how much hospitality is costing one until the visitor has departed.
deepseek_translation: It is in the visitor's presence that we eat the gbese; it is behind them that we repay it.
claude_translation: It is in the presence of a guest that we incur debt; it is behind them that we pay it
gemini_translation: It is in the presence of a stranger that one incurs debt; it is in their absence that one repays it.
mistral_translation: It is the face of a visitor that eats debt; it is the back of the host that bears the burden
llama_translation: The eyes of a stranger are eating debt; his back is paying for it.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against pretending to be generous or hospitable only when others are watching, while being stingy or neglectful in private.
claude_interpretation: We often overspend or make promises to impress visitors, but must deal with the consequences after they leave.
gemini_interpretation: People often act differently or make commitments when observed by others, and fulfill those commitments later when no longer under scrutiny.
mistral_interpretation: Guests often incur expenses or obligations, but the host ultimately bears the responsibility and consequences
llama_interpretation: A person who borrows or takes things without permission will eventually face the consequences.

yoruba: Orogún ìyá ẹ-ẹ́ dáṣọ fún ọ o ní kò balẹ̀; mélòó nìyá ẹ-ẹ́ dá fún ọ tó fi kú?
english_literal: Your mother's co-wife made a garment for you and you complain that it is not long enough; how many did your mother make for you before she died?
interpretation_gold: People dependent on charity should rather be grateful than difficult to please.
deepseek_translation: Your mother's enemy who gave you clothes did not prostrate; how many did your mother give you that you died?
claude_translation: Your mother's twenty medicines that she prepared for you, you said they were not effective; how many did your mother prepare for you that caused you to die?
gemini_translation: Your mother's rival gave you clothes and you said they didn't touch the ground; how many did your mother give you that you wore until they tore?
mistral_translation: The debt of a mother is not enough to clothe you; how many mothers' debts did you collect before you died?
llama_translation: The mother's curse is not a curse that one can escape; how many curses of the mother can one bear?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against ingratitude and emphasizes valuing the sacrifices of those who truly care for you.
claude_interpretation: One should not dismiss or complain about a mother's care and remedies, as her intentions are always for healing and protection, never harm.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the ingratitude of someone who criticizes a gift from an outsider while overlooking the greater generosity and sacrifice of a close relation.
mistral_interpretation: One should not rely excessively on the sacrifices of others, especially parents, as no amount of gratitude can fully repay their efforts.
llama_interpretation: A mother's curse is considered particularly potent and inescapable in Yoruba culture.

yoruba: Oǹpè ní ńfa ọlá; òjípè kì í fa ọlá.
english_literal: It is the person who does the summoning that assumes airs; the person subject to summons does not assume airs.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's place, especially in the company of more illustrious people.
deepseek_translation: The one who is called does not bring wealth; the one who calls does not bring wealth.
claude_translation: Patience attracts honor; impatience does not attract honor.
gemini_translation: The one who calls (invites) brings honor; the one who answers a call does not bring honor.
mistral_translation: The palm-wine tapper draws wealth; the one who taps too late does not draw wealth.
llama_translation: The one who is patient gets wealth; the impatient one does not get wealth.
deepseek_interpretation: Wealth is not determined by titles or names, but by one's actions and efforts.
claude_interpretation: Those who are patient and wait for the right time will gain respect and success, while those who are hasty will not achieve lasting honor.
gemini_interpretation: It is more prestigious to be the one who extends an invitation or initiates an action than to be the one who merely responds to it.
mistral_interpretation: Timing and effort are crucial to achieving success or prosperity.
llama_interpretation: Patience is a necessary virtue for achieving success and prosperity.

yoruba: Ó di ọjọ́ alẹ́ kábuké tó mọ̀ pé iké kì í ṣọmọ.
english_literal: It will not be until the end of days before the humpback realizes that a hump is not a child.
interpretation_gold: People seldom learn wisdom until it is too late.
deepseek_translation: It became the evening of the day Kabuke realized that strength does not belong to a child.
claude_translation: It was evening before the hunchback knew that a hump does not bear children
gemini_translation: It is on the evening of the hunchback that he knows that the hump is not a child.
mistral_translation: It has become evening for the hunchback who thought a knot could not have a child.
llama_translation: It is the night that reveals the true nature of a hen that we know it does not crow
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that wisdom and experience, not mere physical strength, are the true marks of maturity.
claude_interpretation: Some people only realize their limitations or the futility of their expectations when it's too late to make meaningful changes.
gemini_interpretation: One only realizes the true nature or burden of a situation when it becomes critical or too late.
mistral_interpretation: One should not underestimate others or assume their limitations, as unexpected outcomes can challenge such assumptions.
llama_interpretation: One's true character is revealed in times of crisis or adversity.

yoruba: Ojú baba ara; awọ́n bí ojú; aṣòró dà bí àgbà.
english_literal: The eye, father of the body; nothing is as valuable as the eye; nothing is as difficult to achieve as the status of elder.
interpretation_gold: The status of elder is most precious, and most difficult to achieve.
deepseek_translation: The father's eye; they resemble the eye; the young resembles the elder.
claude_translation: The eye of the father is the body; children are like eyes; it is difficult to be like an elder.
gemini_translation: The father's eye is the body; they are like the eye; a difficult person is like an elder.
mistral_translation: The father's face is a mirror; the faces of the young resemble it; the elder's speech is profound like an elder's.
llama_translation: The father's eyes are many; the children are like the eyes; the cloth is as wide as the elder.
deepseek_interpretation: Children often inherit the traits or behaviors of their parents.
claude_interpretation: A father's watchful care over his children is as essential as eyes are to the body, and achieving the wisdom and responsibility of true eldership is challenging.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of respecting elders and those in authority, as their wisdom and guidance, even if seemingly strict, are crucial for well-being and societal order.
mistral_interpretation: Children often inherit and reflect the traits, behaviors, or wisdom of their parents or elders.
llama_interpretation: A community's collective wisdom and experience are more valuable than individual perspectives.

yoruba: Onífunra àlejò tí ńtètè ṣe onílé pẹ̀lẹ́.
english_literal: The excessively attentive visitor “who” extends hospitality greetings to the host.
interpretation_gold: One should not assume other people's functions.
deepseek_translation: The landlord who hastily builds a house for a visitor will soon become a tenant.
claude_translation: A selfish guest who quickly greets the host.
gemini_translation: A suspicious guest who quickly greets the host.
mistral_translation: The hasty guest who acts like the owner of the house greets the real owner carelessly.
llama_translation: The stranger who is always visiting is not a tenant of a small house.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against making hasty decisions that may lead to one's own detriment.
claude_interpretation: Someone who appears polite and respectful on the surface but is actually self-serving and manipulative in their intentions.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes a person who, despite being a guest, acts with an unusual and perhaps insincere eagerness to please, suggesting ulterior motives or a lack of genuine respect.
mistral_interpretation: Overstepping one's bounds or acting presumptuously in unfamiliar situations can lead to embarrassment or disrespect.
llama_interpretation: Frequent visitors should not be mistaken for permanent residents.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́n òkú ọ̀run kó ní kí ará ayé gba òun.
english_literal: A dead person cannot be so desperate as to appeal to a living person for deliverance.
interpretation_gold: However bad one's circumstances might be, one should use good sense in determining where one can turn for help.
deepseek_translation: The eye does not swell at the death of a person in heaven so that the earthly people can mourn him.
claude_translation: The eye does not wink at a dead person in heaven for the living on earth to accept them
gemini_translation: The eyes of a dead person in the afterlife do not become red and ask the people of the world to help them.
mistral_translation: The eyes do not gather the corpse of heaven to ask the people of the world to receive it
llama_translation: The eye does not see the death of heaven, yet the world says it has happened.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should not grieve excessively for those who have lived a good life and passed on honorably, as their transition to the afterlife is a natural and dignified process.
claude_interpretation: One cannot claim divine approval or heavenly endorsement without proper evidence or authority that others can verify.
gemini_interpretation: One should not expect help from those who are no longer in a position to offer it, especially after their passing.
mistral_interpretation: One should not interfere in matters that are beyond their control or responsibility, especially those that belong to the divine or spiritual realm.
llama_interpretation: One should not claim to know or judge something beyond one's knowledge or experience.

yoruba: Òtòlò-ó jẹ, òtòlò-ó mu, òtòlò-ó fẹsẹ̀ wé ẹsẹ̀ erin.
english_literal: The water-buck ate, the water-buck drank, the water-buck compared its limbs to an elephant's.
interpretation_gold: Satiation leads to excess.
deepseek_translation: The mushroom eats, the mushroom drinks, the mushroom attempts to wipe the feet of the elephant.
claude_translation: The mudfish eats, the mudfish drinks, the mudfish rubs its feet against the elephant's feet.
gemini_translation: The guinea fowl eats, the guinea fowl drinks, the guinea fowl compares its leg to the elephant's leg.
mistral_translation: The otolo (a small bird) eats, the otolo drinks, the otolo uses its legs to wash the elephant's legs
llama_translation: The tortoise eats, the tortoise drinks, the tortoise throws away the foot of the elephant.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against overestimating one's abilities or attempting tasks beyond one's capacity.
claude_interpretation: Even the smallest or most humble creature can find ways to benefit from or associate with the mighty and powerful.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish and dangerous to compare oneself to someone far superior in power or status.
mistral_interpretation: A small or seemingly insignificant person can unexpectedly perform a great or important task.
llama_interpretation: One should not waste or reject something that is valuable or useful to others.

yoruba: Ohun tí à ńtà là ńjẹ; kì í ṣe ọ̀rọ̀ oní-kẹrosíìnì.
english_literal: What one sells is what one eats; that does not apply to the kerosene seller.
interpretation_gold: One should be mindful of the peculiarities of one's situation.
deepseek_translation: What we sell is what we eat; it is not the matter of the kerosene seller.
claude_translation: What we are selling is what we are eating; it is not the matter of the kerosene seller.
gemini_translation: What is being sold is what is eaten; it is not the concern of the kerosene seller.
mistral_translation: It is what we sell that we eat; it is not the business of the one who merely watches.
llama_translation: What we are looking for is what we are eating; it is not the talk of the kerosene seller.
deepseek_interpretation: One should focus on their own affairs and not meddle in others' business.
claude_interpretation: People should focus on their own business and livelihood rather than interfering in matters that don't concern them.
gemini_interpretation: People should focus on their own affairs and not meddle in the business of others.
mistral_interpretation: One benefits only from their own efforts and not from merely observing others.
llama_interpretation: One should focus on solving the problem at hand rather than just talking about it.

yoruba: Oníbàjẹ́ ò mọra; oníbàjẹ́ ńlọ sóko olè ó mú obìnrin lọ; ọkọ́ kó akọṣu, ìyàwó kó ewùrà.
english_literal: The shameless person does not know what is fitting; the shameless person is off to raid a farm, and he takes his wife along; the husband steals staple yams, the wife steals wateryams.
interpretation_gold: A man who involves his family in his questionable ventures has sunk to the lowest depths.
deepseek_translation: The spoilt child does not know himself; the spoilt child goes to the farm, the thief takes the woman; the husband gathers firewood, the wife gathers locust beans.
claude_translation: The destroyer does not know himself; the destroyer goes to the lazy man's farm and takes a woman along; the husband carries a hoe, the wife carries a goat.
gemini_translation: The one who spoils things doesn't know themselves; the one who spoils things goes to the thief's farm and takes a woman along; the husband takes yams, the wife takes water yams.
mistral_translation: The debauchee does not know the way; the debauchee goes to the thief's farm and takes another man's wife; the husband gathers thorns, the wife gathers okra.
llama_translation: The debtor doesn't know; the debtor is going to the farm, the debtor takes the wife; the husband takes the hoe, the wife takes the basket.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that lack of discipline and indulgence can lead to recklessness and undesirable consequences in life.
claude_interpretation: A troublemaker lacks self-awareness and involves others in questionable ventures where roles and responsibilities become confused or inappropriate.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes the self-destructive and often oblivious nature of someone who causes trouble, highlighting how their actions can lead to further complications and even involve others in their wrongdoing.
mistral_interpretation: A reckless or immoral person brings trouble upon themselves and others through their thoughtless actions.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of cooperation and division of labor in a marriage.

yoruba: Oòrùn, kó tìẹ wọ̀ ká má bàá Ọlọ́jọ́ wí.
english_literal: Sun, go set so one does not blame the owner of the day.
interpretation_gold: Subordinates should not behave in a manner that would bring their superior to disrepute.
deepseek_translation: Sun, do not shine so we can see the rainbow.
claude_translation: Sun, let it not set so we don't have to speak with the Owner of the Day
gemini_translation: Sun, do not set so that we do not blame God.
mistral_translation: The sun, may it not set for us to be caught speaking ill of the owner of the day
llama_translation: The sky, do not look at it and think it is far from the sun
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that sometimes we must endure temporary discomfort or sacrifice to achieve greater beauty or rewards.
claude_interpretation: It's better to avoid confrontation or difficult conversations with those in authority by preventing situations that would necessitate such encounters.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb expresses a desire for a favorable situation to continue, implying that its cessation would lead to hardship or regret.
mistral_interpretation: It is unwise to speak ill of someone in a position of power or authority while still under their influence or jurisdiction.
llama_interpretation: Do not underestimate the power or influence of someone just because they seem distant or uninvolved.

yoruba: Olówó jẹun jẹ́jẹ́; òtòṣì jẹun tìpà-tìjàn; òtòṣì tí ḿbá ọlọ́rọ̀ rìn, akọ ojú ló ńyá.
english_literal: The rich man eats slowly and at leisure; the poor person eats fast and with anxiety; the poor man who keeps company with a wealthy man is exceeding his station.
interpretation_gold: One should keep to comrades whose station is similar to one's.
deepseek_translation: The rich eat leisurely; the poor eat hurriedly; the poor who walks with the rich, his eyes are wide open.
claude_translation: The rich person eats food gently; the poor person eats food hurriedly and roughly; the poor person who walks with the wealthy is only putting on appearances.
gemini_translation: The rich eats gently; the poor eats with struggle and fight; the poor who walks with the rich, it is a borrowed face he uses.
mistral_translation: The rich person eats gently; the poor person eats hurriedly; the poor person who walks with a rich person, it is the corner of the eye that is tearing up.
llama_translation: The rich man eats well; the poor man eats hastily; the poor man who runs after the rich man, it is the rich man's dog that chases him.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb highlights the disparity in lifestyles between the rich and the poor, and how the poor may become more aware of their struggles when associating with the wealthy.
claude_interpretation: People often pretend to have wealth or status they don't possess when associating with those of higher social standing.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb highlights the disparity in ease and dignity between the rich and the poor, suggesting that the poor often have to compromise their self-respect or appear to be something they are not when associating with the wealthy.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb illustrates how the poor often feel pressured or ashamed when associating with the wealthy, leading to discomfort or envy.
llama_interpretation: One should focus on their own struggles rather than trying to keep up with someone more privileged.

yoruba: Pẹ̀lẹ́ larẹwà ńrìn; jẹ́jẹ́ lọmọ ọlọ́jà ńyan.
interpretation_gold: Gently and carefully is the best manner to take life.
deepseek_translation: The snail moves slowly; the child of the market walks hastily.
claude_translation: Gently is how a beautiful woman walks; quietly is how a merchant's child behaves.
gemini_translation: Gently the beautiful one walks; softly the child of the market owner strolls.
mistral_translation: Gentleness is the beauty of walking; calmness is how the child of the market owner eats
llama_translation: The one who is gentle walks alone; the one who is stubborn is the child of the market woman.
deepseek_interpretation: Different people have different paces and approaches to life based on their circumstances.
claude_interpretation: Grace, composure, and proper conduct are the hallmarks of those from good upbringing and social standing.
gemini_interpretation: Those who are privileged or possess inherent value often move with a calm and unhurried demeanor, reflecting their secure position.
mistral_interpretation: Patience and composure are virtues that bring success and respect in life.
llama_interpretation: Stubbornness can lead to isolation and loneliness.

yoruba: Pátápátá alágbẹ̀dẹ ò ju ilé àrọ lọ.
english_literal: The most one can expect of the blacksmith is confined to the smithy.
interpretation_gold: There is a limit to a person's bragging.
deepseek_translation: The blacksmith's hammer is not heavier than the anvil.
claude_translation: The blacksmith's workshop is not bigger than the dye pit house.
gemini_translation: The blacksmith's utmost is not beyond the forge.
mistral_translation: The blacksmith's anvil is never better than the forge house.
llama_translation: A small axe is not superior to a house of hoes
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that no matter how strong or powerful someone may seem, there is always a greater force or authority.
claude_interpretation: No matter how skilled or important someone becomes, they should not consider themselves superior to their origins or community.
gemini_interpretation: A person's capabilities and influence are often limited to their area of expertise or immediate environment.
mistral_interpretation: One's tools or resources are only as effective as the environment or foundation that supports them.
llama_interpretation: A small but effective tool can be more valuable than a large collection of useless ones.

yoruba: Pamí-nkú obìnrín ṣorí bẹmbẹ sọ́kọ.
english_literal: A masochistic woman hardens her head against her husband.
interpretation_gold: Obstinacy only invites harsh punishment.
deepseek_translation: The death of a woman is like the breaking of a calabash.
claude_translation: A woman who kills and eats speaks sweetly to her husband
gemini_translation: The woman who dies and has a flat head marries a husband.
mistral_translation: The woman who is always crying 'I am dying' climbs the palm tree to tap wine for her husband
llama_translation: A woman's death is on a mortar
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the fragility and irreplaceable value of a woman's life in the community.
claude_interpretation: People who are capable of harmful acts can still present themselves as gentle and loving to those closest to them.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb is a playful and somewhat nonsensical saying, often used to express that some things are inherently contradictory or impossible, or to highlight the absurdity of certain situations.
mistral_interpretation: People who constantly complain or exaggerate their struggles may still perform their duties despite their grievances
llama_interpretation: A woman's greatest sorrow is the loss of her child.

yoruba: Pẹ̀lẹ́-pẹ̀lẹ́ nijó àgbà; ara gbogbo ló di àkísà tán.
english_literal: An elderly person's manner of dancing must be very gentle, because the whole body has become worn to a rag.
interpretation_gold: Elderly people should not over-exert themselves.
deepseek_translation: Slowly-slowly in the elder's day; the whole body has become completely lean.
claude_translation: Gently-gently is the dance of the elder; the whole body has become stiff.
gemini_translation: Slowly, slowly is the dance of the elder; the whole body becomes rags.
mistral_translation: Slowly-slowly is the way of the elder; the whole body has become rags completely.
llama_translation: Slowly-slowly is the dance of the elderly; the whole body becomes a walking stick.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that patience and moderation lead to better outcomes, as rushing can result in exhaustion or loss.
claude_interpretation: Elders move carefully and deliberately because age has made their bodies less flexible, teaching us to respect the natural limitations that come with aging.
gemini_interpretation: Elders, due to their age and wisdom, approach tasks with caution and deliberation, which may appear slow but is a result of their accumulated experience and the physical toll of life.
mistral_interpretation: Patience and carefulness are virtues of wisdom, as rushing leads to ruin or loss of dignity.
llama_interpretation: With age, one's pace and strength naturally decline.

yoruba: San là ńrìn; ajé ní ḿmúni pá kọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: Straight and upright is the way one would walk; it is money that forces one to sneak about.
interpretation_gold: When one is in debt, one's freedom of movement is compromised.
deepseek_translation: Wealth walks; poverty holds it by the leg.
claude_translation: Slowly one walks; it is wealth that makes one kill a leopard.
gemini_translation: It is with health that we walk; wealth makes one walk with a stoop.
mistral_translation: We walk gently; it is witchcraft that makes one walk arrogantly
llama_translation: The road is long; the hawk is crying, let us not be slow.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb highlights how poverty hinders progress and keeps one from achieving wealth.
