deepseek_interpretation: Over-reliance on others can lead to personal weakness or failure.
claude_interpretation: A person who is indecisive or constantly changing their mind cannot make progress or achieve stability.
gemini_interpretation: A person who is actively engaged in a task or expressing themselves will not remain idle or unnoticed.
mistral_interpretation: A person who seeks benefit or advantage must take action rather than remain idle.
llama_interpretation: One who is not part of a situation or community cannot fully understand its complexities.

yoruba: Àjẹ́gbà ni ti kọ̀ǹkọ̀.
english_literal: Croaking-in-relays is the mark of frogs.
interpretation_gold: It is in the nature of sheep to follow and to lack initiative.
deepseek_translation: The witch is the one who does not confess.
claude_translation: The elderly person's own is the grasshopper's
gemini_translation: Receiving a beating is for the frog.
mistral_translation: The witch who refuses to cackle (laugh loudly).
llama_translation: It is the one who is not present that is not counted.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that those who hide their true intentions or actions are often the most dangerous.
claude_interpretation: What belongs to an elder will eventually be inherited by the younger generation, just as grasshoppers benefit from what older ones leave behind.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb suggests that some individuals or situations are inherently prone to negative outcomes or consequences.
mistral_interpretation: A person who conceals their true intentions or abilities will not be easily exposed or understood.
llama_interpretation: One must be present to be recognized or considered.

yoruba: Ara kì í tu ẹni káká, kí ara ó roni koko, ká má leè jíkàkà dÍfá.
english_literal: One cannot be so much at ease, or so much in pain, that one cannot wake early to consult the oracle.
interpretation_gold: Whatever one's condition, one does what one must do.
deepseek_translation: The body does not deceive someone excessively, so the body can become the head, and we cannot deceive the Ifa.
claude_translation: The body does not trouble one severely, and the body afflicts one with illness, that one cannot wake up early to consult Ifa
gemini_translation: One does not feel very relaxed, with a body that is very stiff, and still be able to consult Ifa properly.
mistral_translation: One's body does not swell to the extent that it bursts; rather, it swells gradually until it reaches the navel, so we should not be overly stubborn in divination.
llama_translation: The body does not get tired of someone's stubbornness, until the body gets tired, then it can be stubborn with Ifá
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that honesty and integrity are essential, as deceit will ultimately be revealed, especially in matters of divination like Ifa.
claude_interpretation: No matter how sick or troubled you are, you should still make effort to seek spiritual guidance and solutions to your problems.
gemini_interpretation: One cannot perform complex or important tasks effectively when one is not in a state of physical or mental ease.
mistral_interpretation: Patience and moderation are essential—excessive stubbornness or pride can lead to failure, just as over-swelling can harm the body.
llama_interpretation: One should not be too quick to judge or react to someone's stubbornness, as patience and endurance can ultimately lead to a more effective response.

yoruba: A kì í pa igún, a kì í jẹ igún, a kì í fi igún bọrí.
english_literal: One does not kill the vulture; one does not eat the vulture; one does not offer the vulture as a sacrifice to one's head.
interpretation_gold: Certain behaviors are beyond the pale.
deepseek_translation: We do not kill the vulture, we do not eat the vulture, we do not use the vulture for sacrifice.
claude_translation: We do not kill the vulture, we do not eat the vulture, we do not use the vulture for sacrifice.
gemini_translation: One does not kill a vulture, one does not eat a vulture, one does not use a vulture for sacrifice.
mistral_translation: One does not kill a vulture, one does not eat a vulture, one does not use a vulture to win a bet
llama_translation: We do not kill vulture, we do not eat vulture, we do not use vulture for sacrifice.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that some things, though seemingly useless or undesirable, have their own sacred or protected place in the natural order.
claude_interpretation: Some things are considered so sacred, taboo, or spiritually significant that they must be completely avoided and left untouched.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the sacred and untouchable nature of certain entities or individuals within the Yoruba belief system, implying they are not to be harmed, consumed, or used for ritual purposes.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb advises against associating with or exploiting things or people that are widely considered unworthy or harmful.
llama_interpretation: One should not harm or take advantage of something that is of no use or benefit to them.

yoruba: A-sọ́-ẹ̀hìnkùlé ba araa rẹ̀ nínú jẹ́; ohun tó wuni là ńṣe nílé ẹni.
english_literal: He-who-spies-on-others-from-behind-their-walls upsets himself; one does as one pleases in one's home.
interpretation_gold: What one does in the privacy of one's home is nobody's business.
deepseek_translation: The lizard that jumps from the high iroko tree lands on the ground; what pleases one is what one does at home.
claude_translation: The backbiter harms himself; what brings shame is what one does in their own home
gemini_translation: One who gossips behind one's back spoils their own inside; one does what one likes in one's own house.
mistral_translation: The back-yard wrapper causes one to sweat inside; it is what is available that one uses at home.
llama_translation: The one who is lazy at home will be working hard in another person's house; what he does not do at home is what he is doing in another person's house.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes personal freedom and the right to do what makes one happy in their own space.
claude_interpretation: Those who gossip or speak ill of others ultimately damage themselves, as shameful behavior originates from one's own actions at home.
gemini_interpretation: Gossiping about others' private affairs is self-destructive, as people are entitled to their own choices within their personal space.
mistral_interpretation: One must make do with what is available, even if it is not ideal, rather than complain or seek unnecessary alternatives.
llama_interpretation: One who is idle and refuses to take care of their responsibilities will eventually have to work harder to achieve the same goals elsewhere.

yoruba: Ahun-ún wọnú orù, ó ku àtiyọ.
english_literal: Tortoise has entered into a narrow-necked pot; now, getting out is a problem.
interpretation_gold: One should consider the possible consequences of one's actions before one acts.
deepseek_translation: The tortoise is in the pit, it remains to see the dawn.
claude_translation: The miser enters the grave, leaving behind regret
gemini_translation: The tortoise entered the pot, it remains for it to come out.
mistral_translation: The tortoise inside the mortar died of starvation
llama_translation: The tortoise's noise is in the night, it dies in the morning.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that even in difficult situations, one should remain hopeful for a better future.
claude_interpretation: A greedy or stingy person dies with nothing but remorse for not enjoying or sharing their wealth while alive.
gemini_interpretation: It is easier to get into trouble than to get out of it.
mistral_interpretation: Being surrounded by resources does not guarantee benefit if one lacks the means or wisdom to utilize them
llama_interpretation: A person's actions may seem harmless at first, but they can ultimately lead to their downfall.

yoruba: Àyangbẹ ẹjá dùn; ṣùgbọ́n kí la ó jẹ kẹ́já tó yan?
english_literal: Dry smoked fish is delicious, but what is one to eat before the fish is smoked?
interpretation_gold: While one must look to the future, one must also take care of the present.
deepseek_translation: The fish trap catches fish well; but how do we eat the fish that is caught?
claude_translation: Selecting fish is sweet/pleasant; but what shall we eat before the fish is selected?
gemini_translation: Dried fish is delicious; but what will we eat before the fish dries?
mistral_translation: The fish seller's stew is tasty; but who will eat the fish bones that are chosen?
llama_translation: The fish is delicious; but what of the fish that has been swallowed?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb highlights the irony of effort without benefit, questioning the purpose of success if one cannot enjoy its fruits.
claude_interpretation: Being too choosy or taking too long to make decisions can leave you with nothing while you wait for the perfect option.
gemini_interpretation: It is important to consider immediate needs and challenges while pursuing long-term goals.
mistral_interpretation: One should be cautious of enticing offers that may come with hidden or unpleasant consequences.
llama_interpretation: One should consider the consequences of their actions before taking them.

yoruba: Àlùsì ẹsẹ̀ tí ńfa koríko wọ̀lú.
english_literal: Disaster-causing legs that drag weeds into town.
interpretation_gold: It is a person who will bring disaster on others who behaves like the wayward foot that drags weeds into town.
deepseek_translation: The lame foot that causes the grass to bend.
claude_translation: The foot scraper that pulls grass into the town
gemini_translation: The secret of the foot that pulls grass into the town.
mistral_translation: The footprint that is searching for grass to enter the town
llama_translation: A lazy person's leg is long for a festival
deepseek_interpretation: Even the weak can have a significant impact on their surroundings.
claude_interpretation: Someone who brings problems or trouble from outside into a peaceful community.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb refers to the hidden or subtle ways in which problems or negative influences are introduced into a community.
mistral_interpretation: A person who is overly curious or meddlesome may unknowingly invite trouble upon themselves.
llama_interpretation: One is more energetic and motivated when it comes to leisure activities than when it comes to work or responsibilities.

yoruba: À-gbà-bọ́ ò di tẹni.
english_literal: A foster child does not become one's own child.
interpretation_gold: There is nothing like having one's own.
deepseek_translation: An old monkey does not become one's own.
claude_translation: What is received and brought back does not become one's own
gemini_translation: That which is received is not yet yours.
mistral_translation: The shield does not become the owner
llama_translation: The one who is not at home does not know
deepseek_interpretation: One cannot easily change or control someone who is set in their ways.
claude_interpretation: Borrowed or temporarily held items must be returned to their rightful owner and cannot be claimed as personal property.
gemini_interpretation: Something given or received is not truly owned until it is fully integrated or secured by the recipient.
mistral_interpretation: A borrowed or temporary tool does not confer permanent status or ownership.
llama_interpretation: Absence can lead to ignorance or lack of awareness about what is happening.

yoruba: À ńsọ̀rọ̀ elégédé, obìnrín ḿbèrè ohun tí à ńsọ, a ní ọ̀rọ̀ ọkùnrin ni; bí a bá kó elégédé jọ, ta ni yó sè é?
english_literal: We are discussing pumpkins, a woman asks what we are discussing, and we respond that it is men's talk; after we have gathered the pumpkins, who will cook them?
interpretation_gold: The woman, certainly. There is no point in excluding her from a matter that will eventually involve her anyway.
deepseek_translation: While discussing the pumpkin, a woman asks what we are talking about, we say it is a man's matter; if we gather the pumpkin together, who will cook it?
claude_translation: We are talking about plantain, a woman asks what we are discussing, we say it is men's talk; if we gather plantains together, who will cook them?
gemini_translation: We are talking about pumpkins, a woman asks what we are talking about, we say it's a man's talk; if we gather pumpkins, who will cook them?
mistral_translation: We are discussing the pumpkin, and a woman asks what we are saying, and we say it is men's talk; if we gather the pumpkin together, who will cook it?
llama_translation: We are searching for the lizard, the woman is searching for what we are searching for, we say it is the voice of a man; if we catch the lizard, who will hold it?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb highlights the exclusion of women from certain discussions or decisions, questioning the practicality of such exclusion when their contributions are essential.
claude_interpretation: Men and women need each other and should not exclude one another from important discussions, as both have essential roles to play.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the irony of excluding someone from a discussion only to realize their essential role is needed to complete the task being discussed.
mistral_interpretation: It highlights the irony of excluding women from discussions on matters they are essential to, emphasizing their indispensable role.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of cooperation and division of labor in achieving a common goal.

yoruba: Abẹ́rẹ́ ò ṣéé gúnyán.
english_literal: A needle cannot be used to make pounded yams.
interpretation_gold: Some tools are inadequate for some tasks.
deepseek_translation: A needle cannot roast yam.
claude_translation: A needle cannot pound yam
gemini_translation: A needle cannot be used to pound yam.
mistral_translation: A needle cannot swallow yam.
llama_translation: The calabash does not make a gourd
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that certain tools are not suited for specific tasks, emphasizing the importance of using the right means for the right ends.
claude_interpretation: One should use the right tool for the job, as using inadequate resources for a task will lead to failure.
gemini_interpretation: One should use the appropriate tools or methods for a task.
mistral_interpretation: One should not attempt tasks beyond their capacity or status.
llama_interpretation: One cannot produce what is beyond their capacity or nature.

yoruba: Àjànàkú ò ṣéé rù.
english_literal: The elephant is impossible to carry.
interpretation_gold: Some tasks are impossible to accomplish.
deepseek_translation: The elephant does not get tired of carrying its load.
claude_translation: An elephant cannot be carried
gemini_translation: The elephant is not something that can be carried.
mistral_translation: An elephant cannot carry a load.
llama_translation: The elephant does not get tired of its own weight.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should embrace responsibilities with strength and endurance, just as the elephant carries its weight without complaint.
claude_interpretation: Some people or things are too important, powerful, or significant to be easily handled or controlled by others.
gemini_interpretation: Some tasks or burdens are too great for a single individual to handle alone.
mistral_interpretation: There are limits to what even the strongest or most capable can handle, emphasizing the importance of recognizing one's boundaries.
llama_interpretation: One should not be overwhelmed by their own responsibilities or burdens.

yoruba: Àbá alágẹmọ lòrìṣà ńgbà.
english_literal: The gods heed what chameleon proposes.
interpretation_gold: One should heed the advice of trusted friends and advisers.
deepseek_translation: The deity accepts the sacrifice at the base of the palm tree.
claude_translation: The god accepts the offering of the chameleon owner
gemini_translation: The chameleon's wish is what the deity accepts.
mistral_translation: It is the owner of the chameleon that the deity punishes.
llama_translation: The palm tree is not a climbing tree for the gods.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that blessings come to those who are patient and persistent in their efforts.
claude_interpretation: Patience and adaptability are valued qualities that bring divine favor and acceptance.
gemini_interpretation: One's destiny or fate is often determined by their own intentions or desires.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb warns that those who cause trouble or deception will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
llama_interpretation: Some things are not meant for everyone, regardless of status or power.

yoruba: A-tọrọ-ohun-gbogbo-lọ́wọ́-Ọlọ́run kì í kánjú.
english_literal: The-seeker-of-all-things-from-God does not yield to impatience.
interpretation_gold: The supplicant must be patient for an answer.
deepseek_translation: He who asks for everything from God does not lack.
claude_translation: One who asks God for everything does not hurry
gemini_translation: One who asks for everything from God does not rush.
mistral_translation: It is all pleas (or requests) that are in the hands of God, He does not rush
llama_translation: One who has everything in the world is not greater than God
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that relying on God for all needs ensures provision and discourages greed.
claude_interpretation: Those who trust in God's provision remain patient and do not act with desperate haste.
gemini_interpretation: Those who trust in divine providence for all their needs are patient and do not act hastily.
mistral_interpretation: God attends to all prayers in His own time, so one should be patient and trust in His timing.
llama_interpretation: No matter how wealthy or powerful one is, they are still subordinate to a higher power.

yoruba: Àgbàdo kì í ṣe èèyàn;ta ní ńrí ọmọ lẹ́hìn eèsún?
english_literal: The maize plant is not a human being; who ever saw children on the back of elephant grass?
interpretation_gold: One should not overestimate the value of things.
deepseek_translation: Corn is not a person; who then sees the child behind the cornstalk?
claude_translation: Corn is not a human being; how can it have children behind the cob?
gemini_translation: Corn is not a human being; who sees a child behind a stump?
mistral_translation: Corn does not act like a person; who is eating the child behind the chaff?
llama_translation: The old man is not a person; who sees a child behind the corn?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against underestimating or overlooking someone or something based on appearances.
claude_interpretation: Things should be understood according to their true nature, not attributed with qualities or capabilities they don't possess.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to expect a non-living thing to behave like a living one, just as it is impossible for a stump to bear offspring.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against neglecting one's responsibilities or failing to protect those who depend on you.
llama_interpretation: Experience and age are essential for wisdom and insight.

yoruba: A kì í pé kí òṣìkà ṣe é ká wò ó.
english_literal: One does not dare a wicked person to do his worst.
interpretation_gold: Never tempt evil people to do their evil.
deepseek_translation: We do not wait for a wicked person to do something before we watch them.
claude_translation: We do not say let the left hand do it so we can watch it.
gemini_translation: One does not wait for a wicked person to do it so that one can watch it.
mistral_translation: We do not wait for a wicked person to do it before we look at him.
llama_translation: We don't ask a lazy person to test the depth of a river
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against trusting or waiting for evil individuals to act before taking precautions.
claude_interpretation: One should not deliberately create problems or allow incompetence just to observe the outcome.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to allow a wicked person to act, expecting to merely observe the consequences.
mistral_interpretation: One should be cautious and observant of potentially harmful people without waiting for them to act first.
llama_interpretation: One should not entrust a critical task to someone who is not capable or willing to put in the necessary effort.

yoruba: À-jókòó-àì-fẹ̀hìntì, bí ẹní nàró ni.
english_literal: Sitting-without-leaning-the-back-against-something is like standing.
interpretation_gold: Never do things by half measures.
deepseek_translation: One who sits without shifting, like a roasted corn seller.
claude_translation: Sitting without leaning back is like standing
gemini_translation: Sitting without leaning back is like standing.
mistral_translation: Sitting without support, one becomes like a person with a stiff neck
llama_translation: We do not learn to be wise, it is how one is born
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against stubbornness or inflexibility, comparing it to the stationary posture of a corn seller who does not move.
claude_interpretation: Half-hearted commitment or effort is essentially the same as not committing at all.
gemini_interpretation: Even when seemingly at rest, a lack of proper support can be as tiring and demanding as being active.
mistral_interpretation: Relying solely on oneself without seeking help or advice can lead to unnecessary struggle or discomfort.
llama_interpretation: Wisdom is innate and cannot be acquired through learning or external means.

yoruba: A rí i lójú, a mọ̀ ọ́ lẹ́nu; òṣòwò oṣẹ kì í pọ́n-wọ́-lá.
english_literal: One can tell by looking, and one can tell by taste; a soap seller does not lick her fingers.
interpretation_gold: Soap is recognizable as soap, and anyone who has ever tasted it knows that one does not lick fingers caked with soap. Each trade has its don'ts.
deepseek_translation: We see it with our eyes, we know it with our mouth; the soap seller's trade does not make him rich.
claude_translation: We see it with our eyes, we know it with our mouth; a soap seller does not wash hands carelessly.
gemini_translation: We see it in the face, we know it in the mouth; a soap seller does not go bankrupt.
mistral_translation: We see it with the eyes, we know it in the mouth; a soap trader does not wash with palm oil
llama_translation: We see with the eyes, we know with the mouth; the market of the night is not as crowded as the daytime market.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that mere familiarity or knowledge of something does not necessarily lead to success or profit.
claude_interpretation: People who deal with valuable things regularly handle them with extra care and expertise.
gemini_interpretation: One's true character or intentions are often revealed through their words and actions, and a skilled or essential trade is unlikely to fail.
mistral_interpretation: One should not neglect the tools or resources of their own trade while seeking alternatives.
llama_interpretation: Secrets and hidden matters are often more numerous and complex than open and obvious ones.

yoruba: A kì í fi oníjà sílẹ̀ ká gbájúmọ́ alápẹpẹ.
english_literal: One does not leave the person one has a quarrel with and face his lackey.
interpretation_gold: Focus rather on your main problem, not a side-show.
deepseek_translation: We do not abandon the owner of the fight and embrace the coward.
claude_translation: One does not leave aside the fighter to rely on the flatterer
gemini_translation: One does not abandon the quarrelsome person to embrace the one who has a flat nose.
mistral_translation: We do not leave the trader behind to chase after the one who is merely boasting.
llama_translation: We don't use a razor to shave a tortoise's head
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches loyalty and the importance of standing by those who defend or support us.
claude_interpretation: It is unwise to abandon those who are genuinely strong and capable in favor of those who only offer sweet words but lack substance.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to leave a known problem for an unknown or potentially worse one.
mistral_interpretation: It is wiser to stick with a reliable person or opportunity rather than abandoning it for an uncertain or boastful alternative.
llama_interpretation: One should not use excessive or inappropriate force to achieve a goal.

yoruba: À ńkì í, à ńsà á, ó ní òun ò mọ ẹni tó kú; ó ńgbọ́, “Ikú mẹ́rù, Ọ̀pàgá, a-biṣu-ú-ta-bí-òdòdó, a-lábà-ọkà, a-roko-fẹ́yẹ-jẹ”; ó ní, “Àgbẹ̀ ló kú, tàbí ọ̀nájà?”
english_literal: We recite someone's praise names, we intone his attributes, and a person says he does not know who died; he hears, “Death takes a renowned man, a titled man, whose yams spread like petals, who possesses barns of corn, whose fields are a bounty for birds,” and he asks, “Is the dead man a farmer or a trader?”
interpretation_gold: This is a variant of the preceding entry.
deepseek_translation: We greet him, we salute him, he says he does not know who died; he hears, "Death is fearful, Opaga, the-one-who-sows-seeds-like-flowers, the-one-who-has-a-farm-full-of-corn, the-one-who-farms-for-birds-to-eat"; he says, "Is it the farmer who died, or the trader?"
claude_translation: We greet him, we run to him, he says he doesn't know who died; he hears, 'Death has taken Meru, Opaga, who-plants-yam-and-sells-like-flowers, who-has-corn-barn, who-farms-and-eats-vegetables-fresh'; he says, 'Is it a farmer who died, or a trader?'
gemini_translation: We are mourning, we are wailing, he says he doesn't know who died; he hears, "Death is heavy, Ọ̀pàgá, one who sells yams like flowers, one with a corn barn, one who farms for birds to eat"; he says, "Is it a farmer who died, or a market path?"
mistral_translation: We greet, we ask, he says he does not know who died; he hears, 'Death is fearful, Opaga, the one who sneezes and spits like a flower, the one who carries a cornstalk basket, the one who farms for birds to eat'; he says, 'Was it the farmer who died, or the trader?'
llama_translation: The one who is crying, the one who is wailing, he says he doesn't know the person who died; he is crying, 'My mother has died, my father has died, the one who gives birth to me, the one who takes care of me, the one who makes me happy'; he says, 'Is it the farmer who died or the hunter?'
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes those who feign ignorance or indifference to avoid responsibility or involvement in communal matters.
claude_interpretation: This proverb mocks someone who pretends ignorance despite hearing detailed information that clearly answers their question.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb highlights the importance of paying attention to details and understanding the context of a situation, as the detailed description of the deceased clearly indicates it was a farmer, yet the person still asks for clarification.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb illustrates how people often pretend ignorance when they actually know the truth, especially in matters affecting them.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the hypocrisy of people who pretend to be deeply affected by the death of someone they don't really know or care about.

yoruba: 337. Àgbàlagbàá ṣenú kẹrẹndẹn; èyí tó máa ṣe ḿbẹ níkùn-un rẹ̀.
english_literal: An elder shows a smooth belly to the world; but what he will do is known to him.
interpretation_gold: Be a person of thought and action, not of words.
deepseek_translation: The elder spoke foolishly; what he would do is in his belly.
claude_translation: The elderly person speaks with a trembling voice; what he will do is already in his mind.
gemini_translation: An elder has a small stomach; what he will do is in his belly.
mistral_translation: An elder opens his mouth wide; the one who will act does so in his belly
llama_translation: The elderly person is a repository of knowledge; that is why he is always sought after for advice.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that even elders can speak thoughtlessly, and their true intentions or wisdom may not always be evident in their words.
claude_interpretation: An experienced elder's words may seem weak or shaky, but their intentions and plans are already well-formed in their thoughts.
gemini_interpretation: An elder's seemingly small or insignificant actions are often the result of careful and deliberate thought and planning.
mistral_interpretation: Wise or experienced people may speak openly, but true action or intention remains hidden until executed.
llama_interpretation: Experience and age are valuable sources of wisdom and guidance.

yoruba: Arúgbó oǹdágbèsè, ó ní mélòó ni òun óò dúró san níbẹ̀?
english_literal: The old person who incurs debt, he says how much of it will he be around to pay?
interpretation_gold: A person whose days are numbered can afford to freely take on long-term obligations.
deepseek_translation: The old debtor asks, how much longer will he stand there to pay?
claude_translation: The old debtor says how long will he not stand there to pay?
gemini_translation: An old person who is in debt asks, 'How much will I be able to pay back there?'
mistral_translation: An old debtor says, 'How many times will I stand and pay there?'
llama_translation: The old man who is a master of the Ifá divination, does he ask for directions when he is lost?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against procrastination and the consequences of delaying responsibilities.
claude_interpretation: An elderly person in debt questions how much longer they must endure the burden of repaying what they owe.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the burden of accumulated responsibilities or debts that become overwhelming with age, suggesting that one should address issues promptly rather than letting them pile up.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the reluctance of someone who repeatedly avoids settling their debts, often due to shame or procrastination.
llama_interpretation: Experience and expertise can guide one through uncertain situations.

yoruba: Àfòmọ́ ńṣe ara-a rẹ̀, ó ní òún ńṣe igi.
english_literal: The creeper is destroying itself, but it thinks it is destroying its host.
interpretation_gold: The host's death will be the parasite's death.
deepseek_translation: The millipede is doing its own thing, it says it is doing wood.
claude_translation: The chameleon is changing itself, it says it is changing the tree.
gemini_translation: The parasitic plant is harming itself, it says it is harming the tree.
mistral_translation: The child of a monkey is working on itself, it says it is working on a tree.
llama_translation: The axe is cutting its own body, it says it is cutting a tree.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb criticizes those who boast about their actions or abilities beyond what they are actually capable of.
claude_interpretation: People often blame external circumstances for changes that are actually happening within themselves.
gemini_interpretation: One who harms others often harms themselves more in the process.
mistral_interpretation: People often attribute their own faults or actions to others rather than acknowledging their own responsibilities.
llama_interpretation: One's actions can ultimately harm oneself, despite initial intentions to harm others.

yoruba: A ní kọ́mọ má kùú, o ní kò jọ bàbá kò jọ ìyá.
english_literal: We strive to keep a child from dying, and you say he resembles neither the father nor the mother.
interpretation_gold: The person addressed has his or her priorities reversed.
deepseek_translation: We say the child should not die, you say it does not resemble the father nor the mother.
claude_translation: We say teach the child not to die, you say it doesn't resemble the father nor the mother
gemini_translation: We said the child should not die, you said he doesn't resemble the father, he doesn't resemble the mother.
mistral_translation: You say the child should not cry, you say it does not resemble the father, it does not resemble the mother
llama_translation: He says the child is not dead, he says he is neither father nor mother.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes valuing life over superficial traits or comparisons.
claude_interpretation: When given good advice for improvement, some people reject it by making excuses or claiming it goes against their nature or family traits.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb criticizes those who prioritize superficial resemblances over the fundamental well-being or survival of something important.
mistral_interpretation: It is unfair to expect someone to behave perfectly when they lack proper guidance or good examples from their parents.
llama_interpretation: One should not claim authority or expertise in a matter that is not their responsibility.

yoruba: A kì í fi ara ẹni ṣe oògun alọ̀kúnná.
english_literal: One does not use oneself as an ingredient in a medicine requiring that the ingredients be pulverized.
interpretation_gold: Self-preservation is a compulsory project for all.
deepseek_translation: One does not use one's own body as medicine for a headache.
claude_translation: One does not use oneself as medicine for a mad person
gemini_translation: One does not use oneself to make medicine for a chronic illness.
mistral_translation: One does not use oneself as an ingredient for a fire-extinguishing charm.
llama_translation: One does not use one's body to make a shield for a madman.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against self-harm or sacrificing oneself to solve problems that require wiser solutions.
claude_interpretation: You should not sacrifice yourself or put yourself in danger to help someone who is destructive or beyond reason.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to sacrifice oneself or one's well-being in an attempt to solve a problem that is inherently difficult or long-standing.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against self-sabotage or harming oneself in an attempt to solve a problem.
llama_interpretation: Do not put yourself in harm's way to protect someone who is reckless or irresponsible.

yoruba: Àgbà òṣìkà ńgbin ìyà sílẹ̀ de ọmọọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: A wicked elder sows suffering for his children.
interpretation_gold: One's character often affects the fortunes of one's children.
deepseek_translation: A wicked elder plants suffering for his child.
claude_translation: A wicked elder plants suffering on the ground for his child
gemini_translation: An old wicked person plants suffering on the ground for their child.
mistral_translation: A wicked elder plants suffering that will reach his own child.
llama_translation: An elderly person who is a thief will teach his child to steal
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that harmful actions by elders will ultimately bring suffering to their own descendants.
claude_interpretation: The harmful actions of parents or elders create consequences that their children will inevitably face.
gemini_interpretation: The negative actions of elders can have detrimental consequences that affect future generations.
mistral_interpretation: The harm one causes to others will eventually affect one's own family or descendants.
llama_interpretation: Parents' behavior influences their children's actions.

yoruba: Aláàjàá gbé e sókè, o ní, “Kó ṣẹ!”; o mọ̀ bí ibi lówí tàbí ire?
english_literal: The wielder of the incantation rattle lifts it, and you respond, “May it be so!”; do you know if he has invoked good or evil?
interpretation_gold: One should be certain about what is happening before one intervenes or becomes involved.
deepseek_translation: The bat flew up, saying, 'Let it happen!'; does it know whether it is bad or good?
claude_translation: The dog lifted it up and said 'Let it not happen!'; does it know whether evil or good is being spoken?
gemini_translation: The one who lifts it up says, 'Let it break!'; do you know if it's evil or good that he speaks?
mistral_translation: The one who carries the load upwards says, 'Let it burn!'; does he know whether the place of descent is good or bad?
llama_translation: The lazy person climbs up and says, 'Don't go!'; does he know whether the place is bad or good?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against reckless actions without considering the consequences.
claude_interpretation: One should not reject or oppose something without understanding whether it will bring harm or benefit.
gemini_interpretation: One should be cautious and discerning about the intentions behind seemingly simple or ambiguous statements, as they may carry hidden meanings, whether positive or negative.
mistral_interpretation: One should not act recklessly without considering the consequences of their actions.
llama_interpretation: One should not advise others based on assumptions or ignorance.

yoruba: A-sọ-aré-dìjà ní ńjẹ̀bi ẹjọ́.
english_literal: One-who-turns-play-into-a-fight is always guilty.
interpretation_gold: One should take a jest in the spirit of jest.
deepseek_translation: The one who dances too much is the one who spoils the gathering.
claude_translation: The one who speaks and causes conflict is the one who bears the guilt of the case
gemini_translation: One who turns a joke into a quarrel is guilty of the case.
mistral_translation: The one who dresses to run in a fight is the one who bears the blame of the dispute
llama_translation: One who is not at home is not aware of the fight
deepseek_interpretation: Excessiveness can ruin what would otherwise be enjoyable or beneficial.
claude_interpretation: Those who instigate disputes through their words are responsible for the consequences that follow.
gemini_interpretation: Those who escalate playful interactions into serious conflicts are responsible for the resulting problems.
mistral_interpretation: The person who prepares for conflict or provocation is often the one held responsible for escalating the situation
llama_interpretation: Absence can make one unaware of problems or conflicts at home.

yoruba: A kì í pa asínwín ilé, nítorí ọjọ́ tí tòde yó bàá wá sílé.
english_literal: One does not kill the imbecile within one's home, because of the day when the one from outside might visit one.
interpretation_gold: One should cultivate one's own madness; one might need it to combat others' madness.
deepseek_translation: We do not kill the housefly at home, because of the rain that will come from outside into the house.
claude_translation: One does not kill the house lizard because of the day when the outdoor one will come home
gemini_translation: One does not kill the mad person of the house, because of the day the one from outside will come into the house.
mistral_translation: We do not kill the house lizard because of the day rain will come from outside into the house
llama_translation: We don't kill the lizard in the house, because the rain that will bring it back home is yet to come.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb advises against destroying small conveniences, as they may be needed in future hardships.
claude_interpretation: You should not harm those close to you because of potential future threats from outsiders.
gemini_interpretation: It is wise to tolerate and care for one's own problematic family members, as they may be the only ones available to help when external troubles arise.
mistral_interpretation: Do not destroy what is currently harmless or useful, as it may become valuable in the future
llama_interpretation: One should not destroy or harm something that can still be useful or beneficial in the future.

yoruba: Àgádágodo ò finú han ara-a wọn.
english_literal: Padlocks do not share their secrets with one another.
interpretation_gold: Some secrets one should not divulge to others.
deepseek_translation: The crabs do not reveal their insides to each other.
claude_translation: Chameleons do not show their hearts to each other.
gemini_translation: Padlocks do not reveal their insides to each other.
mistral_translation: The large, broad leaf does not reveal what is inside them.
llama_translation: The tortoise does not cover its own body with its shell
deepseek_interpretation: People often hide their true intentions or vulnerabilities from others.
claude_interpretation: Even those who are similar or from the same group may not trust each other completely or reveal their true intentions.
gemini_interpretation: People often keep their secrets and true intentions hidden from others, even those similar to them.
mistral_interpretation: Outward appearances do not always reflect true intentions or inner qualities.
llama_interpretation: One cannot hide one's own flaws or weaknesses.

yoruba: A kì í ka ilé òrìṣà kún ìlú.
english_literal: One does not count a god's grove as part of the town.
interpretation_gold: Do not list questionable items as part of your wealth.
deepseek_translation: We do not count the houses of the gods to fill the town.
claude_translation: One does not count shrines to fill up a town
gemini_translation: One does not count the house of a deity as part of the town.
mistral_translation: One does not fill a town with the house of a deity.
llama_translation: We do not count the house of the deity as part of the town
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that sacred or spiritual matters should not be exploited for material or selfish gains.
claude_interpretation: Quality and substance matter more than quantity when building or developing something meaningful.
gemini_interpretation: Sacred or special places, though within a community's bounds, are distinct and not to be treated as ordinary parts of it.
mistral_interpretation: Excessive focus on one aspect or individual can disrupt the balance and harmony of the whole community.
llama_interpretation: One should not underestimate or belittle something or someone based on appearance or size.

yoruba: Àpàkòmọ̀rà, tí ńgẹṣin lórí àpáta.
english_literal: A-shiftless-person-who-knows-not-what-things-cost rides a horse on rocks.
interpretation_gold: A person who has no part in paying for a thing is seldom careful in using it.
deepseek_translation: The horse rider, who rides a horse on a rock.
claude_translation: The bald-headed one who is riding a horse on top of a rock
gemini_translation: The one who carves a horse on a rock.
mistral_translation: The lizard that rides a horse on a rock
llama_translation: The child of a dwarf, who is climbing on the back of a tortoise.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against engaging in risky or impractical endeavors.
claude_interpretation: Someone who is attempting something extremely difficult or dangerous without proper preparation or protection is bound to fail.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes someone who undertakes a difficult or impossible task with great determination and skill.
mistral_interpretation: It describes someone who takes on a task or position far beyond their capability, leading to inevitable failure.
llama_interpretation: A person who is already disadvantaged is making things worse by taking unnecessary risks.

yoruba: Àkámọ́ ẹkùn-ún níyọnu.
english_literal: A cornered leopard poses problems.
interpretation_gold: One should be wary of what prey to stalk.
deepseek_translation: The cry of a leopard is sweet.
claude_translation: The leopard's spots are its beauty.
gemini_translation: To embrace a leopard is trouble.
mistral_translation: The chameleon's tears are deceptive.
llama_translation: The leopard's spots are inside
deepseek_interpretation: Appearances can be deceiving, as danger often comes disguised as something pleasant.
claude_interpretation: One's natural characteristics or inherent qualities are what make them beautiful and should be embraced rather than changed.
gemini_interpretation: Engaging with a dangerous situation or person will inevitably lead to problems.
mistral_interpretation: Outward displays of emotion or distress may be insincere or manipulative.
llama_interpretation: A person's true nature is often hidden from view.

yoruba: Abiyamọ kì í rìn kó ṣánwọ́ ahá.
english_literal: A nursing mother does not venture away from home without a cup.
interpretation_gold: She must be prepared to nurse the baby.
deepseek_translation: A child does not walk and crack palm nuts.
claude_translation: A nursing mother does not walk and swing her arms carelessly.
gemini_translation: A mother does not walk and then her calabash of money breaks.
mistral_translation: A pregnant woman does not walk about just to show off her pregnancy
llama_translation: A pregnant woman does not walk and then look back
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that certain tasks require maturity and experience.
claude_interpretation: Those with responsibilities must act with care and consideration for what they are entrusted with.
gemini_interpretation: A mother is always prepared and resourceful, especially when it comes to her children's needs.
mistral_interpretation: One should not engage in actions merely for show or without a meaningful purpose.
llama_interpretation: One should focus on the present and future, rather than dwelling on the past.

yoruba: À-wí-ìgbọ́, àfọ̀-ọ̀-gbọ́ tí ńfi àjèjé ọwọ́ mumi.
english_literal: He-who-will-not-listen-to-talk, he-who-will-not-listen-to-counsel, who drinks water with the bare hand.
interpretation_gold: The obstinate child drinks with the bare hand.
deepseek_translation: The one who says 'I will go to the farm', the one who says 'I will not go to the farm', they both use their hands to drink water.
claude_translation: The one who speaks in the forest, the one who whispers and is heard, who uses the palm of the hand to drink blood
gemini_translation: The one who is told but does not hear, the one who is spoken to but does not understand, is the one who drinks water with cupped hands.
mistral_translation: What the forest says, the river that uses a gentle hand to drink hears
llama_translation: The one who knows the forest, it is the one who knows the way to the forest that is leading the blind person.
deepseek_interpretation: Regardless of one's intentions or claims, actions reveal the truth.
claude_interpretation: This refers to someone who practices secret or mystical arts, suggesting that hidden knowledge and power often involve dangerous or forbidden practices.
gemini_interpretation: Stubbornness and refusal to heed advice will ultimately lead to self-inflicted difficulties and a lack of proper guidance.
mistral_interpretation: Those who listen carefully and act with patience will understand and benefit from wise advice.
llama_interpretation: A leader or guide should be knowledgeable and experienced in the area they are leading others.

yoruba: A bímọ kò gbọ́n, a ní kó má ṣàá kú; kí ní ńpa ọmọ bí àìgbọ́n?
english_literal: A child lacks wisdom, and some say that what is important is that the child does not die; what kills more surely than lack of wisdom?
interpretation_gold: A foolish child is not much better than a dead child.
deepseek_translation: A child is not wise, we tell them not to die; what is killing a child like foolishness?
claude_translation: We give birth to a child who is not wise, we say let him not die; what kills a child like lack of wisdom?
gemini_translation: One gives birth to a child who is not wise, one says let him just not die; what kills a child like foolishness?
mistral_translation: If a child is not wise, we say let them not die young; what then kills a child born without wisdom?
llama_translation: We don't hear the cry of the child, we say it won't die; what kills a child that doesn't cry?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that foolishness can lead to dire consequences, even death, emphasizing the importance of wisdom.
claude_interpretation: Parents may wish to protect their unwise children from harm, but lack of wisdom itself is the greatest danger that can destroy them.
gemini_interpretation: Foolishness is a greater threat to a child's well-being than physical death, as it leads to self-destructive behavior.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the importance of wisdom and good judgment in ensuring a long and successful life.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of expressing one's problems or needs, as silence can lead to unresolved issues.

yoruba: A kì í rí adìẹ nílẹ̀ ká da àgbàdo fún ajá.
english_literal: One does not see chickens about and throw one's corn to the dog.
interpretation_gold: Always direct help where it will be appreciated and where it will do some good.
deepseek_translation: We do not see a chicken on the ground and give corn to a dog.
claude_translation: One does not see a chicken on the ground and pour corn for a dog
gemini_translation: One does not see a chicken on the ground and give corn to a dog.
mistral_translation: We do not see a chicken on the ground and give corn to a dog
llama_translation: We do not eat chicken at home and then go to the farm to give corn to the dog.
deepseek_interpretation: One should prioritize and give resources to those who can truly benefit from them.
claude_interpretation: Don't waste resources on the wrong recipient when the right one is available and present.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to misdirect resources or efforts when the intended recipient or problem is clearly present.
mistral_interpretation: Do not waste resources on those who cannot appreciate or make use of them.
llama_interpretation: One should prioritize and take care of their own before attending to outsiders or others.

yoruba: A kì í léku méjì ká má pòfo.
english_literal: One does not chase two rats and avoid coming up with nothing.
interpretation_gold: Never try to go in two directions at once.
deepseek_translation: One does not chase two rats and not miss one.
claude_translation: One cannot have two rats without one getting spoiled
gemini_translation: One does not chase two rats without losing one.
mistral_translation: We do not chase two rats at the same time and miss both
llama_translation: We do not use two hoes to cultivate one farm
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against trying to do too many things at once, as it may lead to failure in all.
claude_interpretation: When you have multiple options or opportunities, you risk losing some if you don't act decisively.
gemini_interpretation: Attempting to pursue multiple goals simultaneously often results in failure to achieve any of them effectively.
mistral_interpretation: Focus on one task at a time to avoid failure in all endeavors
llama_interpretation: One should not use multiple methods or resources to achieve a single goal.

yoruba: A leper must not wait for a bearer of abrasive leaves (eépín
interpretation_gold: Know your weaknesses.
deepseek_translation: A leper must not wait for a bearer of abrasive leaves
claude_translation: A leper must not wait for a bearer of abrasive leaves
gemini_translation: A leper must not wait for a bearer of abrasive leaves (eépín)
mistral_translation: A leper must not wait for someone carrying rough leaves (eépín)
llama_translation: A leper must not wait for a bearer of abrasive leaves
deepseek_interpretation: One should not delay addressing urgent needs by waiting for external help that may never come.
claude_interpretation: One should not depend on others for help with personal problems that require immediate self-action.
gemini_interpretation: One should not rely on others to provide what is essential for their well-being, especially when facing a critical need.
mistral_interpretation: One should not rely on those who will worsen their suffering or condition.
llama_interpretation: One should not wait for someone else to take action when they have the power to do so themselves.

yoruba: A-ṣòwò-ọṣẹ kì í pa owó ńla.
english_literal: A trader in soap does not make big money.
interpretation_gold: One's success cannot exceed one's enterprise.
deepseek_translation: A seller of soap does not kill big money.
claude_translation: A small-scale trader does not kill big money
gemini_translation: A soap seller does not make big money.
mistral_translation: One who trades in soap does not kill big money
llama_translation: The one who buys on credit does not pay with a big stone.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that engaging in honest, modest work (like selling soap) may not bring great wealth, but it sustains one honorably.
claude_interpretation: Small business ventures cannot generate large profits or significant wealth.
gemini_interpretation: Some professions or ventures, while necessary, are not typically associated with generating significant wealth.
mistral_interpretation: Small or modest ventures may not yield great wealth, but they provide steady and reliable sustenance.
llama_interpretation: One should not promise to pay a debt with something of little value or no value at all.

yoruba: A kì í ṣe fáàárí ẹ̀ṣẹ́ dídì sọ́mọ adẹ́tẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not flaunt one's ability to make a fist in the face of a leper's child.
interpretation_gold: Never make fun of people because of their affliction.
deepseek_translation: One does not use a dirty rag to clean a king's crown.
claude_translation: One does not boast about the tight knots of sin to a crown prince.
gemini_translation: One does not boast about tying a knot for the child of a leper.
mistral_translation: We do not use a razor blade to shave the head of a leper
llama_translation: We do not use the left hand to point at the right hand of a child
deepseek_interpretation: You should not use improper or unworthy means to handle something of great value or importance.
claude_interpretation: It is inappropriate to brag about wrongdoing or shameful acts to someone of high moral standing or noble character.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate to boast about helping someone who is already disadvantaged or in a difficult situation.
mistral_interpretation: One should avoid unnecessary risks or actions that could worsen an already difficult situation.
llama_interpretation: One should not publicly criticize or shame a younger person.

yoruba: Ayé ò ṣé-é bá lérí; wọ́n lè ṣeni léṣe.
english_literal: The world is not a thing to exchange threats with; it can inflict disaster on one.
interpretation_gold: Be wary in dealing with the world.
deepseek_translation: The world cannot be trusted with an oath; they can accuse an innocent person.
claude_translation: The world cannot be trusted to be reliable; they can deceive a person
gemini_translation: The world is not to be trusted; they can harm one.
mistral_translation: The world does not agree to be led by the head; some may be led by the feet
llama_translation: The world does not spoil for the one who is wise; they will spoil it for themselves.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against blind trust in others, as people may falsely accuse even the innocent.
claude_interpretation: Life is unpredictable and people can be deceptive, so one must be cautious and not trust blindly.
gemini_interpretation: One should be cautious and not place complete trust in others, as they have the capacity to cause harm.
mistral_interpretation: Not everyone will follow your guidance or leadership, so adapt to different people's ways
llama_interpretation: Wisdom and self-control are essential for navigating life's challenges.

yoruba: Adìẹ ò lè ti ìwòyí sunkún ehín.
english_literal: Chicken cannot at this late date bemoan its lack of teeth.
interpretation_gold: Everything at its proper time.
deepseek_translation: The chicken cannot cry for the missing teeth of the dog.
claude_translation: A chicken cannot cry backwards.
gemini_translation: A chicken cannot cry for teeth from this time (onwards).
mistral_translation: A chicken cannot cry tears for a hawk's death.
llama_translation: The chicken does not enter the nest of the vulture.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not worry about problems that do not concern them.
claude_interpretation: One cannot undo what has already been done or change the past.
gemini_interpretation: It is futile to lament over something that was never possessed or is naturally impossible.
mistral_interpretation: One should not grieve or show sympathy for the misfortune of those who would harm them.
llama_interpretation: One should not put oneself in a situation where one is vulnerable to the influence or control of a more powerful or unscrupulous person.

yoruba: A kì í bọ́ sínú omi tán ká máa sá fún òtútù.
english_literal: One does not enter into the water and then run from the cold.
interpretation_gold: Precautions are useful only before the event.
deepseek_translation: One does not dive into water and then run away from cold.
claude_translation: One does not jump into water and then run from cold.
gemini_translation: One does not dive into water and then run away from the cold.
mistral_translation: We do not dive completely into water and then run away from the cold
llama_translation: We don't dip our hands into the water and then ask who will fetch for the deaf
deepseek_interpretation: Once you commit to a task, you must endure its challenges.
claude_interpretation: You cannot seek the benefits of something while trying to avoid its natural consequences or challenges.
gemini_interpretation: Once committed to a situation, one must accept its inherent challenges and consequences.
mistral_interpretation: One should not commit fully to a course of action and then abandon it due to minor discomfort or challenges
llama_interpretation: One should not initiate a problem and then expect others to solve it.

yoruba: A kì í peni lólè ká máa gbé ọmọ ẹran jó.
english_literal: One does not suffer the reputation of being a thief and yet go seeking to dance with kids (baby goats).
interpretation_gold: It is foolish to behave in ways that will confirm people's evil opinion of one.
deepseek_translation: One does not steal from someone and still dance with their child.
claude_translation: One does not call someone a thief and still dance with their livestock
gemini_translation: One does not call someone a thief and then carry a young animal to dance.
mistral_translation: We do not wait for a thief at night to start dancing with a piece of meat
llama_translation: We don't sell the house and still carry the child of the house on our back
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against betraying trust while pretending to maintain a friendly relationship.
claude_interpretation: You cannot accuse someone of wrongdoing and then continue to associate with or benefit from them as if nothing happened.
gemini_interpretation: It is hypocritical to accuse someone of a crime while engaging in similar or questionable behavior yourself.
mistral_interpretation: One should prepare for potential problems or dangers in advance rather than waiting until they arise.
llama_interpretation: One cannot abandon one's responsibilities and still expect to retain the benefits.

yoruba: Aṣiwèrè èèyàn lòjò ìgboro ńpa.
english_literal: It is an imbecile who is soaked in the rain in the middle of a town.
interpretation_gold: Only an imbecile ignores a refuge when one is available.
deepseek_translation: A mad person is the one the rain beats in the city.
claude_translation: It is the foolish person that rain catches in the marketplace
gemini_translation: It is a foolish person that the rain in the town square beats.
mistral_translation: It is a mad person that people in the town beat every day
llama_translation: A madman's words are not taken seriously in the marketplace.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights how society often neglects or mistreats those who are vulnerable or different.
claude_interpretation: Those who lack foresight or fail to prepare adequately will suffer consequences that could have been avoided.
gemini_interpretation: A wise person anticipates and prepares for foreseeable challenges, unlike a foolish one who is caught off guard.
mistral_interpretation: Repeated misfortune or suffering often reveals an underlying flaw or persistent problem in a person's behavior or situation.
llama_interpretation: One's words or actions are judged based on their character and reputation.

yoruba: Àì-mọwọ́-ọ́-wẹ̀ ni àì-bágbà-jẹ; ọmọ tó mọwọ́-ọ́ wẹ̀ á bágbà jẹ.
english_literal: Not-knowing-how-to-wash-one's-hands is not-eating-with-elders; a person who knows how to wash his hands will eat with elders.
interpretation_gold: To qualify to live in society, one must learn the social graces.
deepseek_translation: Not knowing how to wash hands is not knowing how to eat with elders; a child who knows how to wash hands will eat with elders.
claude_translation: Not knowing how to wash hands is not growing old; a child who knows how to wash hands will grow old.
gemini_translation: Not knowing how to wash one's hands is not eating with elders; a child who knows how to wash their hands will eat with elders.
mistral_translation: Not knowing how to wash hands is why one does not eat with elders; a child who knows how to wash hands will eat with elders.
llama_translation: Not knowing how to greet is not being respectful; a child who knows how to greet will be respected.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of learning proper etiquette and cultural norms to gain acceptance and opportunities in society.
claude_interpretation: Good hygiene and cleanliness are essential for longevity and survival.
gemini_interpretation: Respect and proper conduct are essential for gaining acceptance and opportunities from those in authority or with more experience.
mistral_interpretation: Proper conduct and knowledge of etiquette grant one access to respected company and opportunities.
llama_interpretation: Showing respect through proper greetings is essential for earning respect in return.

yoruba: Awo aláwo la kì í dá lẹ́ẹ̀mejì.
english_literal: It is another person's divination that one does not repeat.
interpretation_gold: One might not put oneself out for others, but one will for oneself.
deepseek_translation: The diviner's divination is not done twice.
claude_translation: We do not break a plate that has a plate design twice
gemini_translation: One does not consult a diviner twice for the same matter.
mistral_translation: It is only a diviner's tray that does not have two faces
llama_translation: It is the secret of the diviner that does not exceed two people.
deepseek_interpretation: One should trust and act on the first advice or solution given without seeking repeated confirmations.
claude_interpretation: A person who has already learned from a mistake should not repeat the same error.
gemini_interpretation: It is unnecessary and unproductive to repeatedly seek advice or solutions for an issue that has already been addressed.
mistral_interpretation: Every situation or person has multiple perspectives or sides that should be considered.
llama_interpretation: Confidential information should be shared with only a trusted few.

yoruba: Asínwín ní òun ó ti iná bọlé; wọ́n ní kó má ti iná bọlé; ó ní òun ó sáà ti iná bọlé; wọ́n ní bó bá tiná bọlé àwọn ó sọ ọ́ si; ó ní ìyẹn kẹ̀ ìkan.
english_literal: The imbecile said he would torch the house; he was asked not to torch the house; he said he certainly would torch the house; he was told that if he torched the house he would be thrown in it; he said, “That casts the matter in a different light.”
interpretation_gold: Even an imbecile becomes sane when his life is at stake.
deepseek_translation: The blind man says he will carry fire home; they tell him not to carry fire home; he says he will quickly carry fire home; they say if he carries fire home they will chase him away; he says that is nothing.
claude_translation: The foolish person says he will bring fire home; they tell him not to bring fire home; he says he will still bring fire home; they say if he brings fire home they will report him; he says that is the least of his concerns.
gemini_translation: The madman said he would set the house on fire; they told him not to set the house on fire; he said he would still set the house on fire; they said if he sets the house on fire, they would throw him into it; he said, 'That's another matter.'
mistral_translation: The bat said it would set the house on fire; they told it not to set the house on fire; it said it would only fan the fire; they said if it fans the fire, they will blame it; it said that is one more thing.
llama_translation: The gourd said it was the one that was burning in the fire; they said no, it was not the one burning in the fire; it said it was the one burning in the fire; they said if it was the one burning in the fire, they would have heard its sound; it said that was its own voice.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against stubbornness and ignoring wise advice, as it can lead to rejection or consequences.
claude_interpretation: A stubborn fool will persist in dangerous behavior despite warnings and threats of consequences, dismissing all concerns as trivial.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb illustrates the foolishness of someone who persists in a destructive path despite warnings, only to be surprised by the inevitable consequences of their actions.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb illustrates how someone persistently seeks ways to cause trouble despite warnings, showing defiance and disregard for consequences.
llama_interpretation: One should not claim to have experienced something one has not gone through.

yoruba: Adẹ́tẹ̀-ẹ́ ní òún sẹ́ ọ̀ràn kan de àwọn ará ilé òun; ó ní bí òún bá lọ sídàálẹ̀, wọn ò jẹ́ fi kàn-ìn-kàn-ìn òun wẹ̀.
english_literal: The leper says that he trusts his relatives on a certain matter; he says when he goes on a journey, they would not dare use his sponge to wash themselves.
interpretation_gold: People have a knack for skirting dangerous or distasteful situations.
deepseek_translation: Adete is the one who said he has no problem with his household members; he said if he goes to the grave, they will not allow him to rest in peace.
claude_translation: Adẹ́tẹ̀ says he has committed an offense against his family members; he says if he goes to prostrate before them, they will not allow him to wash away his shame bit by bit.
gemini_translation: The leper said he has caused a problem for his family; he said that if he goes to the toilet, they will not wash his anus with a sponge.
mistral_translation: The king says he has a matter to discuss with his household members; he says if he goes to the battlefield, they should not feed him with mere glances.
llama_translation: The crown is what makes one's town people know one's house; if the crown goes to a distant town, they will not know one's house.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that unresolved conflicts within a family can lead to lasting discord, even after death.
claude_interpretation: Some offenses are so serious that even sincere apologies and gradual efforts at reconciliation may not be accepted by those who were wronged.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the social stigma and isolation faced by individuals with certain conditions, as their affliction can lead to their ostracization even by their own family.
mistral_interpretation: A leader expects full attention and support from their people, not just superficial or dismissive gestures.
llama_interpretation: A person's status or achievement is what brings recognition and respect to their family or community.

yoruba: Adánilóró fagbára kọ́ni.
english_literal: He who disappoints one teaches one to be more resourceful.
interpretation_gold: Once disappointed or injured, one learns to be self-reliant.
deepseek_translation: The wealthy person who lacks patience has no one.
claude_translation: The one who asks for advice uses strength to teach oneself.
gemini_translation: The one who causes pain teaches with force.
mistral_translation: The one who eats alone does not grow strong.
llama_translation: The one who has a lot to say does not have a basket
deepseek_interpretation: Wealth without patience leads to loneliness and loss of respect.
claude_interpretation: Seeking advice and guidance from others is a form of self-empowerment and wisdom.
gemini_interpretation: Experiences of suffering or hardship often impart valuable and lasting lessons.
mistral_interpretation: Strength and success come from communal effort and sharing, not isolation.
llama_interpretation: One who talks excessively often lacks substance or resources.

yoruba: A-bayé-jẹ́ kò ṣéé fìdí ọ̀ràn hàn.
english_literal: A treacherous person is not someone to tell profound matters to.
interpretation_gold: One should keep one's secrets from treacherous people.
deepseek_translation: One who has not experienced suffering cannot explain trouble.
claude_translation: One who spoils life cannot be trusted to reveal the truth of a matter
gemini_translation: One who spoils the world cannot be shown the root of a matter.
mistral_translation: The one who spoils the world cannot use a mere pretext to reveal a matter
llama_translation: The one who eats at home does not know the bitterness of the road.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that only those who have endured hardship can truly understand and articulate its nature.
claude_interpretation: A person with a destructive character lacks the credibility to serve as a reliable witness or judge of situations.
gemini_interpretation: It is futile to explain the truth or details of a situation to someone who is inherently destructive or malicious, as they will only twist or misuse the information.
mistral_interpretation: A person who causes trouble should not try to justify their actions or shift blame onto others.
llama_interpretation: Those who have not experienced hardship or struggle cannot truly understand its difficulties.

yoruba: Àpèmọ́ra là ńpe Tèmídire.
english_literal: It is in furtherance of one's own fortune that one calls the name Temidire.
interpretation_gold: Each person must advance his or her own interests.
deepseek_translation: It is gradually that we call Tèmídire.
claude_translation: We call Temidire 'the one who knows how to pamper oneself'
gemini_translation: It is by calling 'Àpèmọ́ra' that Tèmídire is called.
mistral_translation: It is the one who is about to fall that we call 'Hold-on-tight.'
llama_translation: The one who is not present is being called by Temidire
deepseek_interpretation: Patience and persistence are necessary to achieve meaningful results.
claude_interpretation: Self-care and knowing how to treat oneself well is a virtue worthy of recognition and praise.
gemini_interpretation: One's true identity or nature is revealed through their actions or the circumstances surrounding them.
mistral_interpretation: People often seek help or support only when they are already in trouble or facing failure.
llama_interpretation: One's absence can lead to being summoned or sought after, implying that being present and available is important.

yoruba: Àjòjí lójú, ṣùgbọ́n kò fi ríran.
english_literal: A stranger has eyes, but they do not see.
interpretation_gold: A stranger's eyes are blind to the intricacies of his new surroundings.
deepseek_translation: A stranger is in sight, but does not have eyesight.
claude_translation: The stranger has eyes, but cannot see clearly
gemini_translation: A stranger has eyes, but cannot see with them.
mistral_translation: A stranger in the eyes, but he does not blink
llama_translation: The dawn has broken, but it has not brought light.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against trusting outsiders who may not understand or respect local customs and values.
claude_interpretation: A newcomer or outsider may observe situations but lacks the deep understanding that comes from familiarity and experience within that environment.
gemini_interpretation: A newcomer may observe a situation but lacks the understanding or insight to truly comprehend it.
mistral_interpretation: Someone may appear unfamiliar or distant, but they are not necessarily untrustworthy or deceitful.
llama_interpretation: Good intentions or beginnings do not necessarily guarantee success or positive outcomes.

yoruba: Abiyamọ́ ṣọwọ́ kòtò lu ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: A nursing mother cups her palm to strike her child.
interpretation_gold: Discretion is the better part of discipline.
deepseek_translation: The mother who washes her hands in muddy water harms her child.
claude_translation: A mother washes her hands clean before beating her child.
gemini_translation: A mother does not use a hoe to hit her child.
mistral_translation: A mother hen pecks the ground to hit her own chick
llama_translation: The mother's wealth is not hidden from her child.
deepseek_interpretation: A parent's irresponsible actions negatively affect their children.
claude_interpretation: A parent must ensure they are morally clean and justified before disciplining their child.
gemini_interpretation: A mother's love and care for her child are inherent, and she would never intentionally harm them.
mistral_interpretation: Sometimes those who care for us may unintentionally cause us harm while trying to protect or correct us
llama_interpretation: A mother knows her child's true nature and character.

yoruba: Atipo ò mọ erèé; ó ní, “Bàbá, mo réwé funfun lóko.”
english_literal: Atipo does not recognize beans, he says, “Father, I saw white leaves on the farm.”
interpretation_gold: Ignorance is a curse.
deepseek_translation: The cripple does not know how to crawl; he says, "Father, I harvested white leaves in the farm."
claude_translation: The dwarf does not know the taboo; he says, 'Father, I have plucked white leaves in the farm.'
gemini_translation: A stranger does not know okra; he says, “Father, I saw white leaves in the farm.”
mistral_translation: The partridge does not know the game; it says, 'Father, I am bringing white leaves from the farm.'
llama_translation: The tortoise does not know play; he says, “Father, I am farming white cloth.”
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb criticizes someone who makes excuses or boasts about impossible achievements.
claude_interpretation: Ignorance of cultural rules and taboos can lead one to unknowingly commit serious offenses.
gemini_interpretation: Ignorance or unfamiliarity can lead to misidentification or misunderstanding of common things.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights ignorance or arrogance in claiming credit for something one does not truly understand or contribute to meaningfully.
llama_interpretation: One should not pretend to be what they are not or claim expertise in something they know nothing about.

yoruba: Bí ọkùnrín réjò, tóbìrín pa á, à ní kéjò má ṣáà lọ.
english_literal: If a man sees a snake, and a woman kills it, what matters is that the snake does not escape.
interpretation_gold: One should not be a stickler about roles.
deepseek_translation: If a man escapes a snake, and a woman kills it, they say the snake should not have gone away.
claude_translation: If a man sees a snake and a woman kills it, we tell the snake not to run away.
gemini_translation: If a man sees a snake, and a woman kills it, they say the snake should not escape.
mistral_translation: If a man turns into a snake and a woman kills him, they will say the snake should not have gone out
llama_translation: When a man is walking, a child follows him, and he says the child should not go far
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes the tendency to undermine or dismiss someone's efforts, especially when they succeed where others have failed.
claude_interpretation: This proverb highlights the irony of giving advice or commands that are pointless because the situation has already been resolved by someone else's action.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that the effectiveness of a task is more important than who performs it, encouraging collaboration and focusing on the outcome.
mistral_interpretation: One should avoid unnecessary risks or provocations that could lead to blame or misfortune, even if the outcome seems justified.
llama_interpretation: A leader should be mindful of the followers and ensure they are not left behind or lost.

yoruba: Bí ojú ọmọdé ò tó ìtàn, a bá àwígbọ́.
english_literal: If a youth's eyes do not witness a story, they should be good for hearsay.
interpretation_gold: If one does not witness something, one learns from those who did.
deepseek_translation: If a child's eye does not reach the ceiling, they meet the wall.
claude_translation: If a child's eyes cannot reach the shelf, they join the listeners
gemini_translation: If a child's eyes are not enough for a story, they will meet with a hear-and-tell.
mistral_translation: If a child's eyes are not enough for the story, we add the elders' wrinkles
llama_translation: If a child's eyes have not seen history, we show him the forest.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should adjust their expectations according to their capabilities or circumstances.
claude_interpretation: When you lack the ability or experience to participate directly in something, you should observe and learn from others.
gemini_interpretation: A child who is too young to understand a story fully will rely on others to explain or retell it.
mistral_interpretation: When a child lacks the experience to understand something fully, the wisdom of elders is needed to provide clarity.
llama_interpretation: Experience and history are essential for a child's growth and understanding of the world.

yoruba: Bí iṣẹ́ kò pẹ́ ẹni, a kì í pẹ́ iṣẹ́.
english_literal: If a task does not delay one, one does not drag it out.
interpretation_gold: Tasks that are easy should be finished promptly.
deepseek_translation: If work does not reach a person, one does not reach work.
claude_translation: If work does not kill a person, one does not kill work.
gemini_translation: If work does not call for one, one does not call for work.
mistral_translation: If work does not call someone, one does not call work
llama_translation: If work does not call you, you do not call work
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that if opportunities do not come to you, you must actively seek them out.
claude_interpretation: As long as you are alive and capable, you should continue working and not abandon your responsibilities.
gemini_interpretation: One should not interfere or get involved in matters that do not concern them.
mistral_interpretation: One should not force opportunities or responsibilities that are not naturally available or meant for them.
llama_interpretation: One should not force or rush into a task or responsibility that is not yet ready or suitable.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá torí iṣu jẹ epo, à torí epo jẹṣu.
english_literal: If one does not eat oil because of yams, one will eat yams because of oil.
interpretation_gold: If one does not perform a duty because one likes it, one performs it because it is the right thing to do.
deepseek_translation: If we do not eat oil because of yam, we will eat yam because of oil.
claude_translation: If we don't eat palm oil because of yam, we eat yam because of palm oil
gemini_translation: If we don't eat yam because of palm oil, we will eat palm oil because of yam.
mistral_translation: If we do not eat yam because of palm oil, we eat palm oil because of yam
llama_translation: If we do not use the head to eat yam, we use the head to eat palm oil.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes adaptability and making the best out of any situation.
claude_interpretation: Things that complement each other are mutually beneficial and interdependent.
