claude_interpretation: Gradual persistence and patience lead to achieving significant goals over time.
gemini_interpretation: Small, seemingly insignificant intrusions can gradually lead to greater damage or a complete takeover.
mistral_interpretation: Consistent small efforts over time lead to significant achievements.
llama_interpretation: Smallness or humility can be a virtue that leads to productivity and success.

yoruba: Dúró o kíkà; bí o ò dúró kíkà, ìkà a ba tìrẹ jẹ́.
english_literal: Stop and say hello to the wicked; if you do not say hello to the wicked, the wicked will find problems for you.
interpretation_gold: One's best defence against the wicked is ingratiation.
deepseek_translation: Stand and be wicked; if you do not stand to be wicked, wickedness will consume you.
claude_translation: Wait, don't be wicked; if you don't wait and avoid wickedness, wickedness will destroy yours too
gemini_translation: Wait, you wicked one; if you do not wait, wickedness will spoil yours.
mistral_translation: Stand still and read; if you do not stand still to read, wickedness will befall you
llama_translation: Stay and be patient; if you don't stay and be patient, patience will come and meet you.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that failing to confront or resist evil may lead to being overcome by it.
claude_interpretation: Those who practice wickedness will eventually have their own possessions or loved ones destroyed by the same evil they perpetrate.
gemini_interpretation: One should be patient and avoid acting wickedly, as impatience and wickedness can lead to negative consequences for oneself.
mistral_interpretation: Patience and careful attention are necessary to avoid mistakes or misfortune in life
llama_interpretation: Patience is inevitable, so it's better to cultivate it willingly rather than being forced to do so.

yoruba: Dídì ní ḿmú abẹ mú.
english_literal: It is wrapping that makes a knife sharp.
interpretation_gold: Only by taking great care of them does one keep one's possessions in good shape.
deepseek_translation: The beard is what makes the razor sharp.
claude_translation: Tightness is what makes a razor sharp.
gemini_translation: Binding is what makes a razor sharp.
mistral_translation: It is stubbornness that makes the razor hold on to the armpit
llama_translation: The head is what the load carries
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that challenges or opposition can bring out one's best qualities or sharpen one's abilities.
claude_interpretation: Discipline and restraint are what give strength and effectiveness to one's abilities.
gemini_interpretation: Consistent effort and practice are essential for developing and maintaining skills or abilities.
mistral_interpretation: Stubbornness or persistence in a harmful action will only lead to self-inflicted suffering.
llama_interpretation: The leader or person in charge bears the ultimate responsibility for the actions of their group or organization.

yoruba: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must needs speak Ẹ̀gbá.
interpretation_gold: One should speak to others in a manner that befits one, and that will facilitate one's business with them.
deepseek_translation: The Egbá masquerader must speak Egbá.
claude_translation: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must needs speak Ẹ̀gbá.
gemini_translation: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must needs speak Ẹ̀gbá.
mistral_translation: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must speak Ẹ̀gbá
llama_translation: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must needs speak Ẹ̀gbá
deepseek_interpretation: One must adhere to the customs and traditions of their role or community.
claude_interpretation: One must stay true to their origins and cultural identity regardless of the role they play.
gemini_interpretation: One should always act in accordance with their true identity or origin.
mistral_interpretation: One should communicate or behave in a way that reflects their true identity or origin
llama_interpretation: One must act in accordance with one's role or identity.

yoruba: Ebi ńpa mí ọlọ́ṣẹ ńkiri; ìgbà tí ng ò wẹnú ng ó ṣe wẹ̀de?
english_literal: I am hungry and the soap seller hawks her wares; when I have not washed my inside, how can I wash my outside?
interpretation_gold: One must order one's priorities sensibly.
deepseek_translation: I am hungry and the soap is moving around; when I don't have saliva, how will I foam?
claude_translation: Hunger is killing me, the lazy one is wandering about; when I don't enter inside, how will I do entering?
gemini_translation: I am hungry, and the soap seller is hawking; when I have not eaten, how will I bathe?
mistral_translation: Hunger is killing me while the soap owner is bathing; when I don't bathe, how will I be clean?
llama_translation: Hunger is killing me, the hunter is crying; when I have not entered the forest, how can I bring game?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the futility of pursuing trivial matters when basic needs (like hunger) are unmet.
claude_interpretation: One cannot expect to satisfy their needs or achieve success without taking action and making an effort to pursue opportunities.
gemini_interpretation: One must address fundamental needs before attending to less urgent matters.
mistral_interpretation: It highlights the frustration of lacking resources while others have them in abundance, emphasizing the need to address one's own needs first.
llama_interpretation: One must take action and face challenges to achieve success.

yoruba: Ejò-ó rí ihò tó há ó kó wọ̀ ọ́; ìyá-a rẹ̀-ẹ́ lọ́wọ́ àti fà á yọ?
english_literal: A snake sees a tight hole and crawls into it; has its mother hands to pull it out?
interpretation_gold: One had better be certain that one would be able to extricate oneself before one ventures into tight spots.
deepseek_translation: The snake saw a hole and entered it; did its mother hold its hand and pull it out?
claude_translation: A snake finds a hole and enters it; is it its mother who will pull it out?
gemini_translation: The snake saw a hole that was too narrow and did not enter it; does its mother have hands to pull it out?
mistral_translation: Will the snake see a hole big enough to enter and not go in; is it its mother that has hands to pull it out?
llama_translation: The lizard sees the wall it will climb and asks its mother if the wall is climbable
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes personal responsibility and the consequences of one's own actions.
claude_interpretation: People must take responsibility for the consequences of their own actions and decisions.
gemini_interpretation: One should avoid situations that are difficult to escape from, as there may be no one to help.
mistral_interpretation: One should avoid dangerous situations rather than relying on others to rescue them later.
llama_interpretation: One should seek advice from experienced elders before embarking on a challenging task.

yoruba: Èmi-ò-níí-fẹ́-obìnrin-tẹ́nìkan-ńfẹ́, olúwarẹ̀ ò níí fẹ́ obìnrin ni.
english_literal: I-will-court-no-woman-being-courted-by-another-man will court no woman at all.
interpretation_gold: A person who wants exclusive rights to a woman (or anything) will look for a long time and in vain.
deepseek_translation: I do not want the woman that someone else wants, the owner of the house does not want a woman.
claude_translation: I-will-not-love-the-woman-that-someone-else-loves, her owner will not love the woman.
gemini_translation: I will not love a woman that someone else is loving, that person will not love a woman.
mistral_translation: I will not love a woman who loves only one person, the owner of the town will not love a woman either
llama_translation: I don't love a woman who is always at home, the one I love is the one who is not at home
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against desiring what others value, as it may lead to unnecessary conflict or trouble.
claude_interpretation: When you pursue someone else's romantic partner, even the original partner may lose interest, showing that interference in relationships often destroys them entirely.
gemini_interpretation: One should not be possessive or dictate another's choices, as such an attitude can lead to isolation.
mistral_interpretation: This proverb warns against selfish or one-sided relationships, emphasizing that no one, not even a leader, tolerates a partner who is disloyal or self-serving.
llama_interpretation: A partner who is industrious and independent is more desirable than one who is idle and dependent.

yoruba: Eégún tí yó gbeni là ńdáṣọ fún; òrìṣà tí yó gbeni là ńsìn; bi igí bá gbè mí mà kó obì mà bọ igi.
english_literal: It is the masquerader that succors one that one makes shrouds for; it is the god that succors one that one worships; if a tree succors me, I will take kolanuts and worship the tree.
interpretation_gold: One should confine one's efforts to profitable ventures, and one's service to appreciative people.
deepseek_translation: It is the masquerade that will carry one that we sew clothes for; it is the deity that will carry one that we serve; if a tree should carry me, let it carry kola nuts to the tree.
claude_translation: It is the masquerade that will save us that we dress for; it is the deity that will save us that we worship; if a tree supports me, let me not take kola nut to worship the tree.
gemini_translation: It is the masquerade that will support one that we sew clothes for; it is the deity that will support one that we worship; if a tree supports me, I will gather kola nuts and offer them to the tree.
mistral_translation: We sew clothes for the masquerade that will carry us; we worship the deity that will carry us; if a tree is going to fell me, let it at least bear kola nuts so I can offer it.
llama_translation: The masquerade that is revered is the one that dances well; the deity that is revered is the one that is worshipped; if a tree falls on me and I use it to make a canoe to sail on the tree.
deepseek_interpretation: One should invest time and resources only in those who will reciprocate or bring benefit.
claude_interpretation: We should be grateful and show respect to those who help and support us in our time of need.
gemini_interpretation: One should show gratitude and devotion to those who provide support and assistance.
mistral_interpretation: One should engage with things or people that will ultimately support or benefit them in the future.
llama_interpretation: One's abilities and actions determine the respect and recognition they receive.

yoruba: Ebi ò pàmọ̀le ó ní òun ò jẹ àáyá; ebí pa Súlè ó jọ̀bọ.
english_literal: The muslim is not hungry and he vows he will not eat a red Colobus monkey; hunger gripped Suleiman and he ate a monkey.
interpretation_gold: A desperate person is seldom finicky.
deepseek_translation: Hunger did not kill the lizard, yet it claims it does not eat termites; hunger killed Sule, he bowed down.
claude_translation: Hunger does not spare the learned one claiming it does not eat scholars; hunger killed Sule and he fell down.
gemini_translation: Hunger did not kill the rich man, he said he would not eat bat; hunger killed Sule, he ate a bat.
mistral_translation: Hunger does not hide behind the door and say it won't eat beans; hunger killed Sule and he was buried
llama_translation: Hunger does not kill the child of a noble; hunger kills the child of a poor man.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against pride and false claims, emphasizing that humility and truthfulness are essential for survival.
claude_interpretation: No one is exempt from life's basic needs and hardships, regardless of their education or social status.
gemini_interpretation: When faced with extreme hardship, one may be forced to abandon their principles or preferences.
mistral_interpretation: Hardship or necessity will force people to do what they initially resist or deny, no matter their objections.
llama_interpretation: Poverty and lack of resources can exacerbate the effects of hardship.

yoruba: Èrò kì í mọ ibùsọ̀ kọ́rùn ó wọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: A wayfarer does not know the location of the rest stop and yet have his neck crushed from the weight of a heavy load.
interpretation_gold: One measures one's exertions to suit one's capacity.
deepseek_translation: The ant does not know the palm oil will drown it.
claude_translation: A passenger does not know where to sleep until evening comes upon them
gemini_translation: A thought does not know a resting place and enter it.
mistral_translation: A thought does not know the depth of the river before it dives in with its neck.
llama_translation: A traveler does not know the depth of a river until he wades into it
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against underestimating dangers due to ignorance or overconfidence.
claude_interpretation: One cannot fully prepare for or understand a situation until they are actually experiencing it.
gemini_interpretation: One must act on an idea or plan for it to materialize and be effective.
mistral_interpretation: One should not act hastily without first assessing the risks or challenges involved.
llama_interpretation: One must experience a situation firsthand to truly understand its challenges.

yoruba: Èyí tó yẹ ará iwájú, èrò ẹ̀hìn fiyè sílẹ̀.
english_literal: (To) what turned out favorably for those going ahead, you coming behind, pay close attention.
interpretation_gold: Learn from the examples of others.
deepseek_translation: What is proper for those in front, the followers neglect.
claude_translation: What is suitable for those in front, those behind should let it pass by
gemini_translation: That which befits those in front, those behind should pay attention to it.
mistral_translation: What is good for those ahead, the ones behind leave it behind.
llama_translation: What is put in front is the face, the back is what is put behind
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against disregarding the wisdom or examples set by predecessors.
claude_interpretation: People should recognize their position and not interfere with matters that are meant for those who are ahead of them in rank, age, or status.
gemini_interpretation: One should learn from the experiences and actions of those who have gone before them.
mistral_interpretation: People often abandon what has already benefited others, assuming it no longer holds value for them.
llama_interpretation: One's true nature is often revealed by their actions when they think no one is watching.

yoruba: Èmi-ò-níí-ṣu-imí-le-imí, olúwarẹ̀ ó rìn jìnnà ààtàn.
english_literal: I-will-not-defecate-on-existing-excrement will walk a good distance into the bush.
interpretation_gold: People who are too finicky will pay in effort and delay for their habits.
deepseek_translation: I do not defecate on excrement, the owner of the farm walks far to the dung heap.
claude_translation: I-will-not-cook-yam-for-you-to-eat, your master will walk far in the evening
gemini_translation: I will not defecate on feces, the person will walk far from the dump.
mistral_translation: I will not sniff the scent of a fart, let the owner of the fart walk far away from the refuse dump
llama_translation: The one who does not know how to swim, the king's servant will lead to the riverbank.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches the importance of respecting others' property and not taking advantage of their kindness or resources.
claude_interpretation: When you refuse to help someone or show kindness, they will seek assistance elsewhere, often going to great lengths to find what you denied them.
gemini_interpretation: It is wise to avoid repeating past mistakes or engaging in futile actions, as doing so only prolongs the problem or effort.
mistral_interpretation: Avoid unnecessary involvement in others' shameful or unpleasant situations, allowing them to bear their own consequences
llama_interpretation: A leader should guide and support those who are inexperienced or lack knowledge in a particular area.

yoruba: Èpè la fi ńwo èpè sàn.
english_literal: Curses are the antidote for curses.
interpretation_gold: One matches the remedy to the affliction.
deepseek_translation: It is with a curse that we watch a curse heal.
claude_translation: It is with a curse that we use to heal a curse.
gemini_translation: It is with a curse that a curse is healed.
mistral_translation: It is with curses that one counts curses as being plentiful.
llama_translation: It is with curse that one looks at a curse.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that sometimes the solution to a problem comes from the same source that caused it.
claude_interpretation: Sometimes you must use the same method or approach that created a problem to solve it.
gemini_interpretation: Sometimes, a problem or negative situation can only be resolved by using a similar or equally strong measure.
mistral_interpretation: People often focus on and amplify negativity, making problems seem worse than they are.
llama_interpretation: One should not respond to evil with evil.

yoruba: Epo lojú ọbẹ̀.
english_literal: Palm-oil is the countenance of stew.
interpretation_gold: One should be particularly attentive to that one ingredient or thing whose absence mars the entire project.
deepseek_translation: Palm oil is in the eye of the soup.
claude_translation: Oil is the eye of soup.
gemini_translation: Palm oil is the eye of the soup.
mistral_translation: Palm oil is in the soup.
llama_translation: Palm oil is on the stew
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against greed or excess, as too much palm oil (a key ingredient) can ruin a dish just as excess can spoil any situation.
claude_interpretation: The most essential or valuable element gives life and beauty to the whole, just as oil makes soup appetizing and complete.
gemini_interpretation: Palm oil is an essential ingredient that gives soup its characteristic color and appeal, symbolizing that some elements are crucial for the completeness or identity of something.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the obvious presence or involvement of something or someone essential in a situation.
llama_interpretation: Good things are about to happen or a pleasant surprise is coming.

yoruba: Elékuru kì í kiri lóko.
english_literal: The seller of steamed ground beans does not hawk her wares on a farm.
interpretation_gold: One wastes one's time attempting to sell things to those who produce them.
deepseek_translation: The guinea fowl does not roam the farm.
claude_translation: The corn seller does not wander around in the farm.
gemini_translation: The seller of ekuru does not hawk in the farm.
mistral_translation: The cassava meal does not go around the farm.
llama_translation: The elephant does not sleep in the farm
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against meddling in affairs that do not concern you.
claude_interpretation: People should focus on their own area of expertise rather than interfering in matters outside their profession or knowledge.
gemini_interpretation: One should not offer goods or services where there is no demand or appropriate audience.
mistral_interpretation: One should not waste limited resources on unnecessary or overly ambitious tasks.
llama_interpretation: One should not take advantage of a situation or place where they are a guest or have been given permission to stay.

yoruba: Ewúrẹ́ ò ṣe-e fiṣu ṣọ́.
english_literal: A goat is not a wise choice as the guard over yams.
interpretation_gold: Do not entrust your affairs to your enemy.
deepseek_translation: A goat does not use its beard to cover itself.
claude_translation: A goat cannot be trusted to guard yam
gemini_translation: A goat cannot be used to guard yam. (Or, A goat cannot be used to watch over yams.)
mistral_translation: The goat does not use yam to tie a knot.
llama_translation: Goat does not use its horn to kill itself
deepseek_interpretation: One should not rely on insignificant things for important matters.
claude_interpretation: You should not put someone in charge of something they are naturally inclined to destroy or consume.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to entrust something valuable to someone or something that has a natural inclination to destroy or consume it.
mistral_interpretation: One should not attempt a task beyond their capability or use unsuitable tools for a purpose.
llama_interpretation: One should not use one's own strength or abilities to harm oneself.

yoruba: Èló là ńra adìẹ òkókó, tí à ńgba ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀ sìn?
english_literal: How much does a hen cost that one would contract to raise chicks for the owner?
interpretation_gold: Certain obligations are not worth the trouble.
deepseek_translation: How much are we buying the rooster, that we are taking its chick for free?
claude_translation: How much do we buy a hen for, that we would accept its chick in return?
gemini_translation: How much does one buy a mature hen, that one would take its chick as a gift?
mistral_translation: How much is the price of a hen that lays eggs, when one is raising its chicks?
llama_translation: The elephant is eating the okoko tree, and you are asking for its child?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb criticizes unfairness or illogical actions, especially when someone takes advantage of a situation without proper compensation.
claude_interpretation: One should not accept something of lesser value as compensation for something of greater worth.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb questions the logic of accepting a small, insignificant gift when the main, more valuable item is already acquired or expected.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the immeasurable value of something or someone that brings continuous benefits or blessings.
llama_interpretation: One should not ask for something that is not yet available or not yet born.

yoruba: Ètò lòfin kìn-ín-ní lóde ọ̀run.
english_literal: Order is the first law in heaven.
interpretation_gold: Whatever one does, one must be orderly.
deepseek_translation: Order is the law that governs heaven.
claude_translation: Order is the law that exists in heaven.
gemini_translation: Order is the first law in heaven.
mistral_translation: Order is the everlasting law outside in heaven
llama_translation: Customs are what make the world thick
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of order and structure in all aspects of life, as even the heavens are governed by it.
claude_interpretation: Divine order and proper organization are fundamental principles that should guide all aspects of life.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the fundamental importance of order and structure, suggesting that even in the divine realm, organization is paramount.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that divine or natural order governs all things, and humans should follow established rules or systems.
llama_interpretation: Cultural practices and traditions are what give life depth and richness.

yoruba: Ète lẹ̀gbọ́n; ìmọ̀ràn làbúrò; bí-a-ó-ti-ṣe lẹ̀kẹta wọn.
english_literal: Intention is the eldest, contemplation is the next, and plan of action is the third.
interpretation_gold: First there is the goal, next a contemplation of it, and finally a plan for attaining it.
deepseek_translation: Deceit is the elder; wisdom is the younger; how-we-do-it is their third sibling.
claude_translation: Cunning is the first; wisdom is the second; how-we-will-do-it is the third of them.
gemini_translation: Thought is the elder sibling; advice is the younger sibling; how-it-will-be-done is their third.
mistral_translation: The elder is a chair; the wise one is a bag; what shall we do with the third one?
llama_translation: The partridge is in the bush; the hunter is outside; if they do not meet, they will not fight.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that deceit may appear superior, but true wisdom and proper conduct ultimately prevail.
claude_interpretation: Success requires three elements: cleverness to identify opportunities, wisdom to make good decisions, and practical planning to execute effectively.
gemini_interpretation: Careful planning and consideration (thought) precede seeking counsel (advice), and both are essential before taking action (how-it-will-be-done).
mistral_interpretation: Respect for elders and wisdom are essential, but the third person's role or value must also be carefully considered.
llama_interpretation: Avoiding a confrontation can prevent conflict.

yoruba: Epo ló ṣeé jẹṣu; àkàsọ̀ ló ṣeé gun àká; obìnrín dùn-ún bá sùn ju ọkùnrin lọ.
english_literal: It is palm oil that goes best with yams; it is a ladder that is best for climbing granaries; a woman is more pleasant to make love to than a man.
interpretation_gold: Certain things are fit for certain purposes; not anything will do anytime.
deepseek_translation: Oil is what is used to eat yam; cloth is what is used to cover the body; a woman is sweeter to sleep with than a man.
claude_translation: Palm oil is what makes yam delicious; a ladder is what makes it possible to climb a palm tree; a woman is sweeter to sleep with than a man.
gemini_translation: Palm oil is what makes yam edible; a ladder is what makes a barn climbable; a woman is more pleasant to sleep with than a man.
mistral_translation: It is palm oil that makes yam tasty; it is the wrapper that makes the load climb the shoulder; a woman is sweeter when she sleeps than a man.
llama_translation: Palm oil is used to eat jẹṣu; a cloth is used to cover the body; a woman's beauty surpasses that of a man.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the natural and essential roles or preferences in life, emphasizing that certain things are inherently better suited for specific purposes.
claude_interpretation: Each thing has its proper complement or partner that makes it complete and fulfilling.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb uses three distinct examples to emphasize that certain things are inherently better or more suitable for specific purposes.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the unique and irreplaceable value each person or thing brings to a situation, emphasizing that certain qualities or roles enhance outcomes in their own way.
llama_interpretation: A woman's inner qualities and character are more important than a man's physical appearance.

yoruba: Fi ìjà fún Ọlọ́run jà, fọwọ́ lérán.
english_literal: Leave the fighting to God, sit back and watch.
interpretation_gold: One should leave those who have injured one to God's judgement and punishment.
deepseek_translation: Leave the fight for God to fight, fold your arms.
claude_translation: Fight God's battle and wash your hands clean.
gemini_translation: Give the fight to God to fight, and cross your arms.
mistral_translation: Fight for God with fighting, but wash your hands with meat
llama_translation: Make war for God and run away
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb advises against taking matters into one's own hands and instead trusting in divine justice.
claude_interpretation: When you fight for a righteous cause or defend what is morally right, you remain blameless and pure in your actions.
gemini_interpretation: It is best to entrust difficult situations to a higher power and remain calm, rather than engaging in conflict yourself.
mistral_interpretation: Do not hypocritically claim to serve God while engaging in unethical or harmful actions.
llama_interpretation: One should not take credit for a task that requires divine intervention or assistance.

yoruba: Fimí-pamọ́-kí-npa-ọ́ làrùn ńjẹ́.
english_literal: Hide-me-and-I-will-kill-you is the name a disease answers to.
interpretation_gold: A concealed disease is a deadly thing.
deepseek_translation: The one who keeps silent about their pain is the one who suffers.
claude_translation: It is the hidden-and-kill-you type that the stomach eats
gemini_translation: Hide me so I can hide you is what sickness is called.
mistral_translation: Hide-me-so-that-I-will-not-die is what the sick person says
llama_translation: It is the one who is not at home that the wind blows on
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that withholding one's troubles leads to prolonged suffering, emphasizing the importance of speaking up about one's problems.
claude_interpretation: Hidden or internal problems are often more dangerous than obvious ones because they cause harm without being detected.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the reciprocal and often hidden nature of illness, where symptoms may be concealed while the disease itself progresses and affects the individual.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the desperate measures people take to avoid death or difficult situations, even when such efforts are futile or unrealistic.
llama_interpretation: One who is not in their comfort zone or familiar environment is more vulnerable to challenges.

yoruba: “Gba ọmọ fún mi kí nrèdí”; bí ìdí ò bá ṣe-é re ká gbọ́mọ fọ́lọ́mọ.
english_literal: “Hold my child for me so I may wiggle my buttocks”; if one cannot wiggle one's buttocks one should return the child to its mother.
interpretation_gold: One should not place oneself in difficulty in order to help others out of difficulty.
deepseek_translation: "Take a child for me to tie the waist"; if the waist is not suitable, we reject the child.
claude_translation: Take the child for me so I can defecate; if the buttocks cannot be wiped clean, let us throw the child away
gemini_translation: “Take the child for me to dance”; if the dancing is not possible, let us take the child from the child.
mistral_translation: Take a child for me so I can nurse; if the reason is not genuine, we will hear the child crying for its mother
llama_translation: Take my child for me to raise; if the head is not good, the child will not be good
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises careful evaluation before accepting responsibilities or commitments.
claude_interpretation: One should not make hasty decisions or abandon responsibilities when facing temporary difficulties that can be resolved.
gemini_interpretation: One should not make promises or commitments that cannot be fulfilled, and if a task becomes impossible, it is better to retract the offer than to fail.
mistral_interpretation: One should not take on responsibilities without a sincere or valid reason, as it will lead to complications.
llama_interpretation: A child's upbringing and character are shaped by the values and behavior of their caregivers.

yoruba: Ìgbọ̀nwọ́ ti kékeré yọké.
english_literal: The elbow develops a hump right from its youth.
interpretation_gold: Said of a precocious person.
deepseek_translation: The young squirrel climbs up.
claude_translation: The elbow has removed itself from being small.
gemini_translation: The elbow, though small, protrudes.
mistral_translation: The wisdom of a child surpasses that of an elder.
llama_translation: The forest that is small is the one that is cleared.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that even the young or inexperienced can achieve great things with determination.
claude_interpretation: Someone who was once humble or insignificant has now become proud or arrogant due to their changed circumstances.
gemini_interpretation: Even something seemingly insignificant can be prominent or have a noticeable impact.
mistral_interpretation: Age does not always guarantee superior knowledge or judgment; wisdom can come from unexpected sources.
llama_interpretation: Even the most daunting tasks can be accomplished when broken down into smaller, manageable parts.

yoruba: Ìgbín ìbá má mọ̀-ọ́ jẹ̀ kò tó okòó.
english_literal: Had the snail been careless in its foraging it would not “have grown large enough to” be worth twenty cowries.
interpretation_gold: With caution one can offset the effects of any handicap.
deepseek_translation: The snail that will not know hunger is not up to a yam heap.
claude_translation: If the snail did not know how to eat, it would not be as big as a cob of corn.
gemini_translation: If the snail knew how to eat, it wouldn't be worth twenty cowries.
mistral_translation: If a snail had not known its way, it would not have reached the farm.
llama_translation: The snail shell does not know the way to the farm, yet it gets there
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one must endure hardship to appreciate abundance.
claude_interpretation: Everyone has natural abilities and instincts that enable them to survive and thrive in their own way.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb suggests that if something or someone were more capable or valuable, it would not be easily obtainable or cheap.
mistral_interpretation: Consistent effort and familiarity with one's path lead to success.
llama_interpretation: Even the slow and seemingly unaware can achieve their goals with persistence and determination.

yoruba: Iṣú ta iṣu ò ta, ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ńwúṣu lébè.
english_literal: Whether the yams are large or not, it is one by one that one extracts them from the heap.
interpretation_gold: There is no task that is so small or insignificant that it does not deserve care and attention.
deepseek_translation: Yam sells, yam does not sell, each one is dug from the same soil.
claude_translation: Whether yam sells or doesn't sell, we still peel them one by one at the edge.
gemini_translation: Whether the yam sprouts or not, it is one by one that we harvest the yam from the mound.
mistral_translation: Whether the yam is peeled or not, each hoe gets blunted in the process
llama_translation: Yam does not meet yam, it is the farmer that makes them meet on the farm.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that despite differences in success or fortune, everyone shares the same origin and should be treated equally.
claude_interpretation: Regardless of external circumstances or outcomes, we must continue doing our work methodically and consistently.
gemini_interpretation: Regardless of the outcome, tasks are often completed step by step, and each effort contributes to the final result.
mistral_interpretation: Every task, regardless of its difficulty, requires effort and wears down the tools or people involved.
llama_interpretation: It takes effort and initiative to bring people or things together.

yoruba: Ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ àmúyọ, a kì í sin kádìí tán.
english_literal: One does not string decorative beads all around one's waist.
interpretation_gold: One should not deploy all one's resources at once.
deepseek_translation: A coral bead that charms, we do not kneel completely for.
claude_translation: Beads that bring joy, one does not bury them completely.
gemini_translation: A bead that is easily removed, one does not bury it completely.
mistral_translation: Beads of mucus, one does not string them until they are completely dry
llama_translation: The wall of the compound is not a place to lean on
deepseek_interpretation: Do not overly submit to or be deceived by outward beauty or charm.
claude_interpretation: Valuable things that bring happiness should be preserved and not completely discarded or wasted.
gemini_interpretation: Do not invest fully in something that is easily lost or temporary.
mistral_interpretation: Do not rush into action or decision-making before the situation is fully clear or resolved
llama_interpretation: One should not rely solely on external support or protection, but rather take personal responsibility.

yoruba: Ìwò-o ọlọgbọ́n ò jọ ti aṣiwèrè.
english_literal: The way a wise person looks at things is different from the way an imbecile does.
interpretation_gold: A wise person considers matter in a more rational way than an imbecile does.
deepseek_translation: The eyes of the elderly are not the same as those of the young.
claude_translation: The behavior of a wise person is not like that of a fool.
gemini_translation: The gaze of a wise person is not like that of a foolish person.
mistral_translation: The gaze of the wise does not equal that of the fool
llama_translation: The parrot's beauty is not in its feathers
deepseek_interpretation: Experience gives the elderly wisdom that the young lack.
claude_interpretation: Wisdom and foolishness manifest in distinctly different behaviors and actions.
gemini_interpretation: A wise person perceives and understands things differently and more profoundly than a foolish person.
mistral_interpretation: The perspectives or judgments of a wise person and a foolish one are fundamentally different and cannot be compared
llama_interpretation: True beauty or worth is not measured by external appearance.

yoruba: Ilẹ̀ nìjòkò ńjókòó de ìdí.
english_literal: It is on the ground that the stool sits to await the buttocks.
interpretation_gold: One should maintain one's place and not, for example, go out of the house to receive a visitor.
deepseek_translation: The ground is where the buttocks sit to reach the waist.
claude_translation: The ground is where the buttocks sits to wait for the bottom
gemini_translation: The ground is where the buttocks sit.
mistral_translation: It is the ground that sits that reaches the buttocks
llama_translation: The house that is being built is built at the foundation.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of humility and recognizing one's roots or foundation.
claude_interpretation: One must be patient and wait for the right time, as all things eventually settle into their proper place.
gemini_interpretation: One must acknowledge and accept their natural place or limitations.
mistral_interpretation: One must be patient and prepared to achieve success or receive what is due.
llama_interpretation: A strong foundation is crucial for a successful endeavor.

yoruba: Iná tó ńlérí omi á kù sọnù.
english_literal: The fire that challenges water will die off.
interpretation_gold: It is foolhardy to take on a power one is no match for.
deepseek_translation: The fire that boasts of water will eventually burn out.
claude_translation: Fire that is threatening water will surely be extinguished.
gemini_translation: The fire that boasts against water will be extinguished.
mistral_translation: The fire that promises water will eventually disappear
llama_translation: Fire that is burning in the water will not be quenched
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against arrogance and overconfidence, especially when one's strengths are dependent on others.
claude_interpretation: Those who challenge forces greater than themselves will ultimately face defeat.
gemini_interpretation: Those who boast or challenge a superior force will ultimately fail.
mistral_interpretation: Empty promises or deceptive assurances will not last and will ultimately fail
llama_interpretation: A problem or challenge that is deeply ingrained or hidden will be difficult to resolve.

yoruba: Ìtórò tó so lóko tí kò fẹ̀hìntì, afẹ́fẹ́ oko ní ńtú u.
english_literal: The lemon plant that grows in the bush and does not support itself against something will be uprooted by the forest breeze.
interpretation_gold: A weak person who has no support will fall victim to puny forces.
deepseek_translation: The cornstalk that stands tall in the farm without bending, the wind of the farm will break it.
claude_translation: The cotton that grows in the farm that doesn't want to be ginned, the farm wind will scatter it.
gemini_translation: A yam tendril that sprouts in the farm and has no support, the farm wind will unravel it.
mistral_translation: The weed that grows in the farm without being uprooted, the farm wind scatters it
llama_translation: The farmer who cultivates the farm without resting, the farm will surely reward him.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches humility and flexibility, warning that stubbornness leads to downfall.
claude_interpretation: Those who refuse to fulfill their purpose or resist necessary processes will eventually be destroyed by natural forces or circumstances beyond their control.
gemini_interpretation: Without proper support and guidance, an individual or endeavor is vulnerable to external forces and likely to fail.
mistral_interpretation: Problems or bad habits left unaddressed will eventually spread and cause greater harm
llama_interpretation: Hard work and perseverance will ultimately yield positive results.

yoruba: Ibi tí oyín gbé ńhó, tí àdó ńhó, ìfun ò dákẹ́ lásán.
english_literal: As the bees hum and the small calabash containing charms hums, the intestine does not keep silent.
interpretation_gold: No matter what other people's preoccupations are, one should not ignore one's own problems.
deepseek_translation: Where the snail is crawling, the tortoise is crawling, the intestines do not stay still.
claude_translation: Where honey is sweet and palm wine is sweet, the stomach does not just keep quiet.
gemini_translation: Where the bee is buzzing, where the calabash is buzzing, the intestines do not keep quiet for nothing.
mistral_translation: Where honey is being scooped and where palm oil is being scooped, the intestines do not stay quiet for nothing.
llama_translation: Where honey is being eaten, and corn is being eaten, the fly does not stay away from the market
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against complacency, emphasizing that even seemingly slow or steady progress requires constant effort and vigilance.
claude_interpretation: When good things are abundant and available, it is natural for people to desire and partake of them.
gemini_interpretation: Significant events or activities often have underlying causes or consequences that are not immediately apparent.
mistral_interpretation: When people see opportunities for gain or enjoyment, they will naturally express excitement or desire without restraint.
llama_interpretation: Where there is abundance and joy, people are naturally drawn to it.

yoruba: Ibi tí a ti ńjẹun bí ikun bí ikun, a kì í sọ̀rọ̀ bíi kẹ̀lẹ̀bẹ̀ bíi kẹ̀lẹ̀bẹ̀ níbẹ̀.
english_literal: Where one is eating food like mucus, one should not bring up matters like phlegm.
interpretation_gold: One must be careful not to bring up matters that are too sensitive for present company.
deepseek_translation: Where we eat like an elephant like an elephant, we do not whisper like a mouse like a mouse there.
claude_translation: Where one eats quietly like a squirrel, one does not talk noisily like a parrot there
gemini_translation: Where one eats like a stomach, one does not speak like a gossip.
mistral_translation: Where one eats like a glutton, one does not speak like a frog (i.e., croak loudly or carelessly).
llama_translation: The place where we eat and drink like elephant, we don't talk like a parrot there.
deepseek_interpretation: One should act boldly in situations where boldness is expected and not timidly.
claude_interpretation: One should show respect and restraint in places where they receive benefits or hospitality.
gemini_interpretation: When in a place of abundance or privilege, one should not engage in petty or ungrateful talk.
mistral_interpretation: In a place where you benefit or are well-fed, you should behave with restraint and not draw unnecessary attention to yourself.
llama_interpretation: One should be mindful of their speech and behavior in a place where they have been shown hospitality.

yoruba: Ibi tí a bá ńgbé la ti ńgbàwìn; à-rà-àì-san ni ò sunwọ̀n.
english_literal: One's home is a legitimate place to buy things on credit; what is bad is avoiding payment.
interpretation_gold: There is nothing wrong in seeking favors from those close to one; what is bad is not returning favors.
deepseek_translation: Where we live is where we gather dew; sickness is not good.
claude_translation: Where we live is where we seek respect; buying without paying is not proper.
gemini_translation: It is where we live that we borrow; it is not good to borrow and not repay.
mistral_translation: Wherever we live is where we sweep; a cheap item is not worth repairing
llama_translation: Where we live is where we make our farm; it is the one that is not far that we cultivate.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that one should appreciate and make the best of their current situation, as health is more valuable than any material gain.
claude_interpretation: One must earn respect in their community through proper conduct, and taking things without giving fair compensation is inappropriate behavior.
gemini_interpretation: One should always repay their debts, especially within their community, to maintain good standing and avoid negative consequences.
mistral_interpretation: One should adapt to and maintain their current environment, as some things are not worth the effort to fix or improve.
llama_interpretation: One should focus on utilizing the resources and opportunities available in their immediate environment.

yoruba: Igbá tó gbédè là ḿpè lóṣùwọ̀n.
english_literal: It is a calabash that understands one's language that one describes as a measure.
interpretation_gold: One places one's confidence only in those of the same mind with one.
deepseek_translation: The calabash that is deep is the one I call heavy.
claude_translation: The calabash that carries palm wine is what we call a wine gourd.
gemini_translation: It is the calabash that understands the language that is called a measure.
mistral_translation: It is the calabash that is whole that we use to measure salt.
llama_translation: The calabash that is broken is the one that is used to scoop water
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that true value or worth is often found in depth and substance rather than superficial appearances.
claude_interpretation: A person's function or role defines their identity and how they are recognized by others.
gemini_interpretation: Only those who understand and are capable of a task are entrusted with it.
mistral_interpretation: Only those who are complete and capable should be entrusted with important tasks.
llama_interpretation: A person who has experienced hardship or failure is often the one who is best equipped to help others in similar situations.

yoruba: Ibi tí òjò-ó ti ńpa igún bọ̀-ọ́ jìnnà; ta ní rán igún níṣẹ́?
english_literal: The vulture has endured the drenching rain from a great distance, but who sent the vulture on an errand?
interpretation_gold: If one's choices land one in difficulty, one should not blame others.
deepseek_translation: Where the rain is beating the vulture is far; who sent the vulture on an errand?
claude_translation: The place where rain beats the vulture is far away; who sent the vulture on an errand?
gemini_translation: The place where rain beats the vulture is far away; who sent the vulture on an errand?
mistral_translation: The place where the rain has been beating the vulture, it is far away; who sent the vulture on an errand?
llama_translation: Where the rain is beating the vulture's nest, can we ask the vulture to come down?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb criticizes those who interfere in matters that do not concern them, emphasizing the importance of minding one's own business.
claude_interpretation: People often suffer consequences in distant places due to their own choices and actions, not because others forced them into those situations.
gemini_interpretation: One should not interfere in the affairs of others, especially when they are facing difficulties that are a result of their own choices.
mistral_interpretation: One should not blame others for misfortunes that are a result of their own actions or nature.
llama_interpretation: One should not expect someone to take action or make a decision when they are already in a difficult or precarious situation.

yoruba: Ìlọ-ọ́ ya, oníbodè Atàdí; wọ́n kó o nílé, wọ́n gbà á lóbìnrin, ọ̀pẹ̀lẹ̀ tó ní òun ó fi wádìí ọ̀ràn, ajá gbé e, ọmọ ẹ̀ tó lé ajá láti gba ọ̀pẹ̀lẹ̀, ó yí sí kàǹga; oníbodè Atàdí wá dáhùn ó ní, “Ìlọ-ọ́ yá.”
english_literal: It is time to get out of here, the gatekeeper of Atadi; his home was burglarized, his wife was taken from him, the divining string he was going to use to investigate matters was snatched by a dog, his son who ran after the dog to retrieve the divining string fell into a well; the gatekeeper of Atadi then spoke up and said, “It is time to get out of here.”
interpretation_gold: When a place becomes too hot for a person, he/she should know it is time to get out.
deepseek_translation: The house is open, the gatekeeper Atadi; they took him home, they gave him a wife, the tortoise said he would investigate the matter, the dog carried it, the child was not enough to carry the tortoise, he turned to the fence; the gatekeeper Atadi responded, 'The house is open.'
claude_translation: Ilo-o ya, gatekeeper of Atadi; they captured him at home, they took his wife, the divination chain that said it would investigate the matter, a dog carried it away, his child who chased the dog to retrieve the divination chain fell into a ditch; the gatekeeper of Atadi then responded saying, 'Ilo-o ya.'
gemini_translation: The journey is swift, Atadi's gatekeeper; they gathered him at home, they took his wife, the divining chain he said he would use to investigate the matter, a dog carried it away, his child who chased the dog to retrieve the divining chain, fell into a well; Atadi's gatekeeper then replied, saying, 'The journey is swift.'
mistral_translation: The rope is broken, gatekeeper of Atadi; they took it home, they used it to marry a wife, the divination chain that claimed it would unravel matters, a dog took it, a child who could chase the dog to retrieve the chain, turned into a fool; the gatekeeper of Atadi replied, 'The rope is broken.'
llama_translation: The wall is broken, the owner of Atadi's house; they took it home, they took it as a wife, the calabash that it used to carry water, the dog took it, the child that is smaller than the dog took the calabash, it broke into pieces; the owner of Atadi's house came to console him, saying, 'The wall is broken.'
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against unnecessary interference or meddling in matters that do not concern you, as it can lead to complications.
claude_interpretation: When misfortunes pile up one after another, sometimes all one can do is accept fate with resignation.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb illustrates how a series of unfortunate events can quickly escalate and compound, leading to a disastrous outcome.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb teaches that once a situation has deteriorated beyond repair, no amount of explanation or past significance can restore it.
llama_interpretation: One should not be surprised or grieve over the inevitable or the consequences of one's own actions.

yoruba: Ìyàwó ṣe ọ̀ràn kan tán; ọkọ ẹ̀-ẹ́ ṣe ọ̀ràn-an nkò-jẹ-mọ́.
english_literal: The wife has done the unpardonable; her husband has adopted an I-will-not-eat-any-longer attitude.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who have caused unpardonable offence.
deepseek_translation: The wife is a complete plan; the husband is a plan that is not clear.
claude_translation: The wife did one thing; her husband did something that cannot be compared to it.
gemini_translation: The wife committed one offense; her husband committed an offense of 'I will not eat anymore.'
mistral_translation: A wife has finished one matter; her husband is still dealing with the same matter without knowing it.
llama_translation: The wife has one secret; the husband has a secret that is not to be told to me.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the contrast between the perceived reliability of a wife's plans and the uncertainty often associated with a husband's plans in Yoruba culture.
claude_interpretation: A husband's actions or mistakes can be far more serious or consequential than his wife's.
gemini_interpretation: A small offense can lead to an overreaction or disproportionate response from another person.
mistral_interpretation: It highlights how one person may remain unaware of a situation that another has already resolved or moved past.
llama_interpretation: A husband and wife should keep each other's secrets.

yoruba: Ìloro là ńwọ̀ ká tó wọlé.
english_literal: One enters the porch first before one enters the house.
interpretation_gold: Everything in its proper order.
deepseek_translation: It is outside we look before entering the house.
claude_translation: We wash our feet before entering the house
gemini_translation: It is the outside that one looks at before entering the house.
mistral_translation: It is the hallway we look at before entering the house
llama_translation: The drum that is beaten at home is the one that is heard outside.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises careful observation and assessment of a situation before taking action.
claude_interpretation: Proper preparation and cleanliness are necessary before engaging in important matters or entering sacred spaces.
gemini_interpretation: One should observe and assess a situation or person from the outside before fully engaging or committing.
mistral_interpretation: One should carefully observe or assess a situation before fully committing to it
llama_interpretation: A person's actions at home will ultimately reflect on their reputation outside.

yoruba: Ìgbín ìbá má mọ̀-ọ́ jẹ̀ ìbá ti kú síjù.
english_literal: Had the snail been careless in its foraging it would have died in the bush.
interpretation_gold: However disadvantaged one might be, one could still thrive if one took life easy.
deepseek_translation: If the snail had known excessive dancing would kill it, it would have danced less.
claude_translation: If the snail had not known how to eat, it would have died long ago.
gemini_translation: If the snail knew how to eat, it would have died in the forest.
mistral_translation: If the snail had not known, it would have eaten the snail that died excessively
llama_translation: The snail shell does not know the death of the snail in the forest.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against overindulgence or excessiveness, as it can lead to harm or downfall.
claude_interpretation: Everyone has natural instincts or abilities that help them survive and succeed in life.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb suggests that sometimes a lack of certain abilities or knowledge can be a form of protection or survival.
mistral_interpretation: Overconfidence or ignorance can lead one into avoidable danger or loss
llama_interpretation: One may not be aware of the problems or challenges faced by others in their private lives.

yoruba: Ibi tí òjò-ó bá ọjọ́ ní ńpa á sí.
english_literal: Wherever the rain catches up with the day, there it drenches it.
interpretation_gold: One should do what one has to do as the opportunities present themselves.
deepseek_translation: Wherever rain meets dew is where it beats it.
claude_translation: Where rain meets the day is where it beats it to
gemini_translation: Where the rain meets the day, it falls there.
mistral_translation: Wherever the rain chooses to fall heavily, that is where it will beat down on.
llama_translation: The place where the rain meets the sun is where it is being beaten.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that conflicts or challenges arise where opposing forces or interests meet.
claude_interpretation: Problems or challenges will affect you wherever they find you, regardless of your circumstances or location.
gemini_interpretation: Circumstances dictate the outcome of events.
mistral_interpretation: One must accept and endure the challenges or misfortunes that come their way, as they are often beyond personal control.
llama_interpretation: Harmony and balance are necessary for progress and growth.

yoruba: Ijó ní ḿbọ́ṣọ, ìjà ní ḿbọ́ ẹ̀wù.
english_literal: It is dance that strips one of one's cloth; it is a fight that takes off one's shirt.
interpretation_gold: Different situations call for different responses.
deepseek_translation: Dancing is how clothes tear, fighting is how clothes get stained.
claude_translation: Dancing spoils clothes, fighting spoils garments.
gemini_translation: Dancing wears out clothes, fighting wears out garments.
mistral_translation: Dancing is what wears out the wrapper, fighting is what wears out the cloth.
llama_translation: Dance is in the drum, fight is in the sword
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that engaging in frivolous or aggressive behavior leads to unnecessary consequences.
claude_interpretation: Every activity has its consequences and costs that must be accepted.
gemini_interpretation: Both excessive dancing and fighting lead to negative consequences and damage.
mistral_interpretation: Excessive or careless actions, even enjoyable ones, can lead to unintended damage or loss.
llama_interpretation: The means or tool used often determines the outcome or nature of an action.

yoruba: Ibi tí a ti gùn, ibẹ̀ la ti ńrọ̀.
english_literal: Where one began one's climb, there one effects one's descent.
interpretation_gold: One must not shift the problems originating in one context to another, unrelated context.
deepseek_translation: Where we have climbed is where we are descending.
claude_translation: Where we climbed from, that is where we descend to
gemini_translation: Where we climbed from, there we descend.
mistral_translation: Where we have climbed, there we are descending
llama_translation: The place where we have been seated, that is where we are looking.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that one must face the consequences of their actions.
claude_interpretation: We must return to our origins or starting point, emphasizing the importance of remembering where we came from.
gemini_interpretation: One must always remember their origins and the path they took to reach their current position.
mistral_interpretation: The consequences or outcomes of one's actions will eventually catch up with them, often in the same place or situation where those actions originated.
llama_interpretation: One should focus on the present situation rather than dwelling on past experiences.

yoruba: Ìpàṣán tí a fi na ìyálé ḿbẹ láàjà fún ìyàwó.
english_literal: The whip used on the senior wife is resting on the rafters waiting for the new wife.
interpretation_gold: One should not assume that the misfortune that befell those who went before one will pass one over.
deepseek_translation: The whip used to flog the senior wife is still kept in the rafters for the new wife.
claude_translation: The cane used to beat the senior wife is hanging in the corridor for the junior wife to see
gemini_translation: The cane used to beat the senior wife is in the attic for the junior wife.
mistral_translation: The whip used to beat the senior wife is kept in the kitchen for the junior wife
llama_translation: The slap with which we hit the senior wife is a warning to the junior wife
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that past actions or consequences can serve as a lesson or warning for future situations.
claude_interpretation: What happens to one person serves as a warning or lesson for others in similar situations.
gemini_interpretation: The consequences faced by one person for their actions will eventually befall another who commits similar transgressions.
mistral_interpretation: The suffering or mistreatment experienced by one person may be used as a warning or threat to control another
llama_interpretation: The actions taken against one person can serve as a warning or lesson to others.

yoruba: Ibi tí à ńgbé là ńṣe; bí a bá dé ìlú adẹ́tẹ̀ à di ìkúùkù.
english_literal: One should live according to the customs and fashions of the place one finds oneself in; if one lands in the city of lepers, one should make a fist, i.e., conceal one's fingers.
interpretation_gold: While in Rome, do as the Romans do.
deepseek_translation: Where we live is where we act; if we get to the land of the cripple, we become lame.
claude_translation: Where we live is where we act; if we reach the land of the crown-wearers, we become subjects
gemini_translation: Where we live is where we act; if we arrive in the town of lepers, we become hunchbacked.
mistral_translation: Where we live is where we act; if we reach the land of the leper, we become like a bunch of decaying matter.
llama_translation: Where we live is where we make our home; when we get to the city of the crown, it becomes a place of noise.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one's behavior is influenced by their environment and circumstances.
claude_interpretation: One must adapt their behavior to match the customs and expectations of whatever environment or community they find themselves in.
gemini_interpretation: One must adapt their behavior and appearance to the customs and environment of their surroundings.
mistral_interpretation: One's environment influences behavior, and associating with corrupt or harmful people can lead to moral decay.
llama_interpretation: One's true character is revealed when they are in a position of power or authority.

yoruba: Ibi tí o máa sùn lo tẹ́ ọmọ sí.
english_literal: It is precisely where you will eventually have to sleep that you have laid down your child to sleep.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person deceiving himself or herself, in the futile hope that a transparent ruse will work to his/her advantage.
deepseek_translation: Where you will sleep is where you lay the child.
claude_translation: Where you will sleep is where you lay the child.
gemini_translation: Where you will sleep is where you spread the mat for the child.
mistral_translation: Where you will sleep is where you lay your child down
llama_translation: The place where one is not awake is where one is carried to as a child.
deepseek_interpretation: Prepare for the future by making necessary arrangements in advance.
claude_interpretation: You must take responsibility for the consequences of your actions and decisions.
gemini_interpretation: One should prepare for the future or for others in a way that also benefits oneself.
mistral_interpretation: Your actions or choices determine the environment or future you create for your dependents.
llama_interpretation: One is often taken care of or protected in times of vulnerability or weakness.

yoruba: Igbá là ńpa, a kì í pa àwo.
english_literal: It is a calabash that one cuts decorative patterns on; one does not cut patterns on china plates.
interpretation_gold: What is appropriate treatment for one thing may be inappropriate for another.
deepseek_translation: We break the calabash, we do not break the plate.
claude_translation: We break the calabash, we do not break the plate.
gemini_translation: It is a calabash that one breaks, not a plate.
mistral_translation: It is the calabash that we break, we do not break the plate.
llama_translation: The calabash is what is used to fetch, one does not fetch the calabash.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises handling situations with care, choosing what to sacrifice wisely.
claude_interpretation: We should be careful to distinguish between what is expendable and what is valuable, treating precious things with appropriate care.
gemini_interpretation: Some things are inherently fragile and meant to be broken or discarded, while others are more durable and valued, thus requiring different treatment.
mistral_interpretation: One should address issues with those who can handle criticism or correction without taking offense.
llama_interpretation: One should not confuse the means with the end or the tool with the goal.

yoruba: Ibi tí a gbé epo sí a kì í sọ òkò síbẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not throw rocks at the place where one has one's palm-oil stored.
interpretation_gold: One should always protect one's base or where one's best interests lie.
deepseek_translation: Where palm oil is placed, one does not place a stone there.
claude_translation: Where we keep palm oil, we do not throw stones there
gemini_translation: Where palm oil is kept, one does not throw stones there.
mistral_translation: Where one puts oil, one does not point a finger there.
llama_translation: The place where we put the palm oil is not where we put the yam.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not spoil a good thing or situation with unnecessary harshness.
claude_interpretation: One should not harm or destroy the source of their livelihood or benefit.
gemini_interpretation: One should avoid actions that could damage or waste something valuable.
mistral_interpretation: One should not criticize or blame a place where they have contributed to the problem.
llama_interpretation: Different things require different approaches or treatments.

yoruba: Iná èsìsì kì í jóni lẹ́ẹ̀mejì.
english_literal: The fire of the stinging tragia plant does not burn a person twice.
interpretation_gold: One should learn a lesson from the first bad experience.
deepseek_translation: A sudden fire does not burn one twice.
claude_translation: The fire of a cooking stove does not burn someone twice.
gemini_translation: The fire of the nettle does not burn one twice.
mistral_translation: A sudden fire does not burn two places at once
llama_translation: A small fire does not burn two people
deepseek_interpretation: One learns from a sudden misfortune and avoids its recurrence.
claude_interpretation: A wise person learns from their first painful experience and avoids repeating the same mistake.
gemini_interpretation: One learns from a painful experience and avoids repeating the same mistake.
mistral_interpretation: A misfortune or crisis rarely affects multiple people or places simultaneously, emphasizing the unpredictability of trouble.
llama_interpretation: A small problem or issue should not affect multiple people.

yoruba: Ìyàwó sọ ọ̀rọ̀ kan tán: ó ní ìyálé òun a-bẹnu-funfun-bí-ègbodò.
english_literal: The junior wife has said what will be her last; she said the senior wife's mouth is as white as the new yam.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who have done the unthinkable.
deepseek_translation: The bride says one word: she has a mother-in-law whose mouth is as white as an egbo bird.
claude_translation: The new wife said one thing: she said her senior wife has a mouth as white as a heron.
gemini_translation: The junior wife finished saying something: she said her senior wife has a mouth as white as egbo (cornmeal).
mistral_translation: A wife finishes telling a story: she says her mother-in-law has a mouth as white as the egbodo tuber (i.e., speaks only sweet words).
llama_translation: The wife says one thing: she says her mother-in-law is as white as a snail shell.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that even a seemingly innocent remark can reveal deeper tensions or hidden truths in relationships.
claude_interpretation: This warns against making disparaging comments about others, as the new wife is criticizing her senior wife's appearance or speech in a derogatory manner.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes someone who speaks without thinking or is prone to gossip, as a 'white mouth' implies a lack of substance or discretion in their words.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the irony of a wife praising her mother-in-law’s kindness only after resolving a conflict, suggesting that harmony is often temporary or insincere.
llama_interpretation: A person may say something pleasant to your face, but mean the opposite.

yoruba: Ìgbà ara là ḿbúra.
english_literal: One swears when it is time to swear.
interpretation_gold: Everything in its proper time.
deepseek_translation: Time is what takes an oath.
claude_translation: It is one's own time that one swears by
gemini_translation: It is when one is in a hurry that one swears an oath.
mistral_translation: It is in times of personal crisis that one swears an oath.
llama_translation: The time of the body is the time of the cloth
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that time is the ultimate witness to truth and will reveal all things in due course.
claude_interpretation: People make promises or commitments based on their own circumstances and timing, not others'.
gemini_interpretation: People tend to make hasty promises or commitments when under pressure or in a rush.
mistral_interpretation: People often make promises or commitments when they are in desperate or difficult situations.
llama_interpretation: One's circumstances or situation determines one's appearance or behavior.

yoruba: Ìṣeǹṣe ewúrẹ́, kágùntàn fiyè síi.
english_literal: The fate that has befallen the goat, the sheep should bear in mind.
interpretation_gold: One should learn from the fates of others.
deepseek_translation: The goat's mistake, the sheep takes warning.
claude_translation: The goat's misbehavior should not make the sheep jealous of it
gemini_translation: The goat's behavior, let the sheep pay attention to it.
mistral_translation: The goat's effort, the sheep gets the feathers
llama_translation: The goat's beard is not long, yet it is tangled in the bush
deepseek_interpretation: Learn from the mistakes of others to avoid similar consequences.
claude_interpretation: One should not envy or desire the wrongdoings of others, even if they seem to benefit from their bad behavior.
gemini_interpretation: One should learn from the mistakes or experiences of others to avoid similar pitfalls.
mistral_interpretation: One person's hard work or sacrifice often benefits someone else who did not contribute.
llama_interpretation: Even the smallest or seemingly insignificant things can get entangled in complex problems.

yoruba: Ìgbà òjò ńlọ, ìgbà ẹ̀rùn ńlọ, a ní ká dí isà eku kó le; ìgbà wo la óò tó wá peku náà?
english_literal: The rainy season passes, the dry season passes, and the suggestion is that the rat's burrow be sealed up tight; when will the time be ripe to kill the rat?
interpretation_gold: One must do what needs to be done while there is still time, rather than resort to transparent temporizing ruses.
deepseek_translation: The rainy season is passing, the dry season is passing, we say let us set the rat trap; when will we ever get to catch the rat?
claude_translation: The rainy season is going, the dry season is going, we say let's block the rat's hole so it cannot escape; when will we have time to catch the rat?
gemini_translation: The rainy season is going, the dry season is going, and we are told to block the rat's hole tightly; when will we then call the rat?
mistral_translation: When it is raining, when it is dry season, we say let us block the rat's hole; when exactly will we have time to catch the rat?
llama_translation: When rain is going, when sun is going, we say let us put the rat's tail in the house; when will it be the turn of the rat itself?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against procrastination and indecisiveness, emphasizing that opportunities are fleeting.
claude_interpretation: Constant procrastination and endless preparation without action will result in missing opportunities entirely.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to prepare for a task or problem when the opportune time has passed, making the effort pointless.
mistral_interpretation: It highlights the futility of preparing for a problem without taking direct action to solve it.
llama_interpretation: One should not wait for the worst-case scenario to take action, but rather prepare for it while dealing with lesser problems.

yoruba: Ìdí òwò ni òwòó gbé tà.
english_literal: It is at its home base that a company or trade prospers.
interpretation_gold: One would be wise to protect one's base.
deepseek_translation: The buttocks are what the buttocks use to sell.
claude_translation: It is from the bottom that money is sold.
gemini_translation: The base of the trade is where the trade is sold.
mistral_translation: It is the reason for the money that the money is used to trade
llama_translation: The palm tree is what the palm frond leans on.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that one must use their inherent qualities or resources to achieve success.
claude_interpretation: Success and wealth are built from humble beginnings and small foundations.
gemini_interpretation: The foundation or origin of a venture determines its success or failure.
mistral_interpretation: Every action or resource is best utilized when its original purpose or intention is understood and followed
llama_interpretation: One should always acknowledge and respect their source or origin.

yoruba: Ikúdú pa ẹṣin à ńyọ̀; ó ḿbọ̀ wá pa ọmọ èèyàn.
english_literal: An abandoned well kills a horse and we rejoice; it will in time kill a human being.
interpretation_gold: One should take other people's misfortunes as a reminder that one also is not immune to such misfortunes.
deepseek_translation: The pit that kills the horse is laughing; it is coming to kill the human child.
claude_translation: The disease that killed the horse, we rejoiced; it is coming to kill human beings.
gemini_translation: Death kills a horse, we rejoice; it is coming to kill a human being.
mistral_translation: The saddle killed the horse in joy; it will later come to kill a human child.
llama_translation: The forest is clearing the path for the horse to pass; it is not the horse that clears the path for humans to pass.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that misfortune affecting others today may befall you tomorrow if precautions are not taken.
claude_interpretation: We should not celebrate others' misfortunes because the same calamity may befall us.
gemini_interpretation: One should not rejoice at the misfortune of others, as a similar or worse fate may eventually befall them.
mistral_interpretation: What brings temporary joy or benefit may eventually lead to greater harm or destruction.
llama_interpretation: Those in power or authority often receive preferential treatment, while the needs of ordinary people are neglected.

yoruba: Ìbéèrè kì í jẹ́ kí ẹni ó ṣìnà; ẹni tí kò lè béèrè ní ńnpọ́n ara ẹ̀ lójú.
english_literal: Asking “directions” keeps one from losing one's way; the person who refuses to ask is responsible for his/her own difficulties.
interpretation_gold: One should not be too obstinate or too proud to seek help when one needs it.
deepseek_translation: Asking questions does not make one lose the way; it is the one who cannot ask questions that wanders aimlessly.
claude_translation: Asking questions does not make one go astray; the person who cannot ask questions is the one who embarrasses themselves.
gemini_translation: Asking questions does not allow one to go astray; it is the one who cannot ask questions that troubles themselves.
mistral_translation: Asking questions does not make one get lost; the one who cannot ask questions is the one who stumbles over themselves in plain sight.
llama_translation: A person who cannot endure hardship will not be able to endure wealth; a person who cannot bear hardship is a slave to his stomach.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance to avoid confusion or mistakes.
claude_interpretation: It is better to ask questions when uncertain than to remain ignorant and make mistakes that bring shame.
gemini_interpretation: Seeking clarification prevents errors, while a refusal to ask questions leads to self-inflicted difficulties.
mistral_interpretation: Seeking knowledge through inquiry prevents mistakes, while ignorance leads to avoidable errors.
llama_interpretation: One must be able to endure hardship in order to truly appreciate and manage wealth.

yoruba: Isó inú ẹ̀kú, à-rá-mọ́ra.
english_literal: The fart within a masquerader's shroud “is” something to be endured.
interpretation_gold: The insult one cannot escape from, one has to endure.
deepseek_translation: The inside of the grave is tight.
claude_translation: The stomach of a rat, we-see-ourselves.
gemini_translation: The excrement inside the civet cat, we meet it with closeness.
mistral_translation: The rat's internal secret, only the one who shares its nest knows.
llama_translation: The inside of the rat is not seen, yet it is known.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that death is inevitable and inescapable, urging people to live wisely.
claude_interpretation: We should be content with what we have and not be greedy, as even a small rat's stomach can teach us about moderation.
gemini_interpretation: One must accept and deal with the inherent flaws or unpleasant aspects of something or someone they are closely associated with.
mistral_interpretation: Only those closely involved in a matter truly understand its hidden details or complexities.
llama_interpretation: One's true nature or character will eventually be revealed.

yoruba: Ilé olóńjẹ là ńdẹ̀bìtì àyà sí.
english_literal: It is in the home of a person who has food that one sets one's chest like a trap.
interpretation_gold: People usually position themselves where they imagine there is something to gain.
deepseek_translation: It is the house of the eater that one prepares the chest for.
claude_translation: It is to the house of the food seller that we take our heart's debt.
gemini_translation: It is at the house of the one who has food that one leans one's chest.
mistral_translation: It is the house of the food owner that we point to when we are in need of courage.
llama_translation: The house of the eater is where the visitor breaks his/her teeth
deepseek_interpretation: One prepares for challenges where they expect to receive support or benefit.
claude_interpretation: We naturally gravitate toward those who provide for our needs and show them loyalty.
gemini_interpretation: People naturally gravitate towards those who can provide for their needs.
mistral_interpretation: One often turns to those who are well-resourced or capable for support in times of difficulty.
llama_interpretation: One should be cautious of the intentions of those who appear to be generous or welcoming.

yoruba: Ìyàwó mi ò sunwọ̀; nítorí ọmọ ni mo ṣe fẹ́ ẹ; ẹni mélòó la ó wìí fún tán?
english_literal: “My wife is not good looking, but I married her for the sake of children”; to how many people will one give that explanation?
interpretation_gold: One should not embark on the endless and futile task of justifying one's decisions to people.
deepseek_translation: My wife is not beautiful; it is because of children that I married her; how many people will we inform?
claude_translation: My wife is not beautiful; it is because of children that I married her; how many people shall we tell this to?
gemini_translation: My wife is not beautiful; it is because of children that I married her; how many people will one tell everything to?
mistral_translation: My wife does not cook; because I married her for her child; how many people will we tell this to?
llama_translation: My wife is not sleeping; because I have a child I love; who else will wake up for?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes valuing substance (like having children) over superficial qualities (like beauty).
claude_interpretation: Some truths are better kept private as sharing them widely can cause unnecessary harm or embarrassment.
gemini_interpretation: One should not air all their grievances or private matters publicly, as some things are best kept to oneself.
mistral_interpretation: One should accept and manage personal choices or situations privately without unnecessary public disclosure.
llama_interpretation: A parent's love and responsibility for their child is unparalleled and requires selfless sacrifice.

yoruba: Igúnnugún ò torí abẹ párí.
english_literal: The vulture did not go bald for fear of the razor.
interpretation_gold: One's actions are not determined by one's fear of any person.
deepseek_translation: The vulture does not lack feathers.
claude_translation: The vulture does not end because of a razor.
gemini_translation: The vulture does not shave its head because of a razor.
mistral_translation: The vulture does not perish because of a blunt knife
