mistral_interpretation: A person who benefits from external help or privilege should not boast or act arrogantly, as their success is not solely their own effort.
llama_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should appreciate and be content with the blessings they have.

yoruba: Orin tí ò ṣoro-ó dá kì í ṣòro-ó gbè; bí ó bá ní “héééé,” à ní “háááá.”
english_literal: A song that is not difficult to lead is not difficult to follow; if the leader sings “haaaay,” one responds “haaaah.”
interpretation_gold: One expends on a task only the amount of effort commensurate with it.
deepseek_translation: A song that is not difficult to sing is not difficult to carry; if it says 'héééé,' we say 'háááá.'
claude_translation: A song that is not difficult to start is not difficult to carry; if it has 'héééé,' we respond with 'háááá.'
gemini_translation: A song that is not difficult to compose is not difficult to sing; if it says “heeee,” we say “haaaa.”
mistral_translation: A song that is not difficult to sing does not become difficult to sing; if it has 'heee,' it will have 'haaaa.'
llama_translation: A song that does not make you dance will not make you dance; if it says 'héééé,' you will say 'háááá.'
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that tasks which appear easy require little effort or thought to accomplish.
claude_interpretation: Things that are easy to begin are usually easy to continue, and participation becomes natural when you understand the pattern.
gemini_interpretation: Simple tasks or situations are easy to respond to and manage.
mistral_interpretation: A task that appears simple at first will reveal its true challenges as you attempt it.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the idea that people tend to respond in kind to the energy or attitude they receive.

yoruba: O sá fún ikú, o bọ́ sí àkọ̀ idà.
english_literal: You run from death and seek refuge in a scabbard.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person who has got himself/herself in a worse predicament from the one he/she was fleeing from.
deepseek_translation: He ran from death, but ran into the sheath of the sword.
claude_translation: He ran from death and fell into a sword's sheath
gemini_translation: He ran from death, he fell into a sword sheath.
mistral_translation: You ran from death, you stumbled into the sheath of a sword
llama_translation: He made a sacrifice for death, and it reached the left side of the sword.
deepseek_interpretation: Avoiding one danger only to encounter a worse one.
claude_interpretation: Trying to escape one danger often leads to encountering an even greater one.
gemini_interpretation: Attempting to escape one danger can lead one directly into another, equally perilous situation.
mistral_interpretation: Avoiding one danger may lead you into an even greater one
llama_interpretation: One's actions can have unintended and far-reaching consequences.

yoruba: Onígẹ̀gẹ́ fìlẹ̀kẹ̀ dọ́pọ̀; adámú fi sàárà san ẹgbẹ̀ta.
english_literal: The goitered person sets a low price on beads; the person with a blocked nose repays six thousand cowries with alms.
interpretation_gold: One usually sets little value on what one cannot use.
deepseek_translation: The bald-headed one wears a wig; the hairy one shaves his head.
claude_translation: The banana seller exchanges banana for coins; the groundnut seller uses small change to pay for thirty kobo worth.
gemini_translation: The one who wears beads uses them to replace a debt; the one who wears a cap uses it to pay six hundred cowries.
mistral_translation: The lazy person strings beads to sell; the restless one pays double the price for a gourd.
llama_translation: The tortoise's shell is not complete; Adamu uses a rag to cover his buttocks.
deepseek_interpretation: People often desire what they do not have while neglecting what they possess.
claude_interpretation: Small consistent transactions and careful money management can accumulate into significant amounts over time.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the resourcefulness and adaptability of individuals in using available assets to resolve financial obligations, even if unconventional.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights how laziness and impatience both lead to unnecessary waste or loss.
llama_interpretation: One uses available resources to cover up one's shortcomings or inadequacies.

yoruba: Ogún kì í pọ̀ ká pín fún aládùúgbò.
english_literal: The inheritance is never so abundant that one shares it with neighbors.
interpretation_gold: However abundantly one is blessed one should manage one's resources wisely.
deepseek_translation: Twenty is not too many to share with a neighbor.
claude_translation: Twenty cannot be many enough to share with neighbors
gemini_translation: War does not become so much that it is shared with a neighbor.
mistral_translation: Twenty does not gather together to be shared with a neighbor.
llama_translation: War does not allow one to choose a companion
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of generosity and community support, suggesting that no amount is too large to share with those around you.
claude_interpretation: No matter how much you have, it's never enough to satisfy everyone who expects to benefit from your resources.
gemini_interpretation: One's personal troubles or burdens are not meant to be shared or distributed among others, especially those not directly involved.
mistral_interpretation: People should not expect others to share their resources when they have enough for themselves.
llama_interpretation: In times of crisis, one may have to accept help from anyone, regardless of their character or background.

yoruba: Olóògùn ní ńṣe bí a-láigbọ́-mọ̀ràn; bí ogun ó bàá wọ̀lú ọlọgbọ́n là ńfọ̀rọ̀ lọ̀.
english_literal: The medicine man behaves like a person impervious to wise counsel; if war threatens a town the person to consult for counsel is the sage.
interpretation_gold: Trust rather in wisdom than in magical charms.
deepseek_translation: The medicine man behaves like one who lacks wisdom; when war comes to town, the wise man is the one who runs.
claude_translation: The medicine man acts like one who doesn't listen to advice; when war enters the town, it is to the wise person we run for counsel.
gemini_translation: The herbalist acts like one who does not know; if war is to enter the town, it is with the wise that one consults.
mistral_translation: The medicine owner acts as if he is ignorant; when war enters a wise person's town, we seek refuge with him.
llama_translation: The herbalist treats as one who has not seen the forest; if the medicine does not kill the herbalist, it is the one he will use to treat others.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against underestimating the wise, as they know when to act or retreat for survival.
claude_interpretation: Those who ignore good advice in peaceful times will be sought after for wisdom when crisis strikes.
gemini_interpretation: Even experts may feign ignorance to gather information, and in times of crisis, it is crucial to seek counsel from the truly knowledgeable.
mistral_interpretation: True wisdom or expertise is often hidden until the moment of need, when it becomes indispensable.
llama_interpretation: A person who has not experienced a situation firsthand may not fully understand its challenges.

yoruba: Olé tó jí kàkàkí, níbo ni yó ti fọn ọ́n?
english_literal: A thief who stole a bugle, where will he blow it?
interpretation_gold: One should not waste one's efforts chasing something one can never use.
deepseek_translation: The thief who wakes the trumpeter, where will he blow the trumpet?
claude_translation: A thief who steals a trumpet, where will he blow it?
gemini_translation: A thief who stole a trumpet, where will he blow it?
mistral_translation: The thief who wakes up to the sound of a trumpet, where will he have hidden his loot?
llama_translation: A thief who steals a hen, where has he hidden it?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that actions meant to expose others may ultimately reveal one's own misdeeds.
claude_interpretation: Some stolen goods are too conspicuous or distinctive to use without revealing the theft.
gemini_interpretation: One should consider the consequences and practicality of their actions, especially when those actions are illicit or inappropriate.
mistral_interpretation: A person who acts recklessly or arrogantly will eventually expose their own wrongdoing.
llama_interpretation: This proverb teaches that every action has consequences and one's misdeeds will eventually be exposed.

yoruba: Odó iyán ò jẹ́ gún ẹ̀lú; odó ẹ̀lú ò jẹ́ gúnyán; àtẹ tá-a fi ńpàtẹ ìlẹ̀kẹ̀, a ò jẹ́ fi pàtẹ ọ̀rúnlá.
english_literal: The mortar used for pounding yams will not do for pounding indigo leaves; the mortar for pounding indigo leaves will not do for yams; the tray on which beads are displayed for sale will not do for displaying dried okro.
interpretation_gold: Each object has its proper uses.
deepseek_translation: The mortar for pounding yam cannot be used to pound ẹ̀lú; the mortar for pounding ẹ̀lú cannot be used to pound yam; the grinding stone used for grinding beads cannot be used to grind ọ̀rúnlá.
claude_translation: The mortar for pounding yam is not suitable for pounding elu; the mortar for elu is not suitable for pounding yam; the flat stone used for flattening beads cannot be used to flatten Orunmila.
gemini_translation: The yam pounder cannot pound indigo; the indigo pounder cannot pound yam; the tray used for displaying beads, we cannot use it to display kola nuts.
mistral_translation: The mortar for pounding yam does not climb the hill; the mortar of the hill does not pound yam; the mat we use to string beads on the ground, we do not use to string the ọ̀rúnlá beads.
llama_translation: The river of yam does not flow to the town; the river of the town does not flow to the yam; we use the river to wash the feet, we do not use it to wash the head.
deepseek_interpretation: Each tool has its specific purpose and should not be misused for tasks it wasn't designed for.
claude_interpretation: Different tools are designed for specific purposes, and sacred things require appropriate reverence and cannot be treated with ordinary implements.
gemini_interpretation: Each tool or person has a specific purpose or role, and it is inappropriate to use them for tasks they are not suited for.
mistral_interpretation: Every tool or method has its proper context or use, and one should not force what is unsuitable for a particular situation.
llama_interpretation: One should prioritize and respect the proper order and hierarchy of things.

yoruba: Òjòwú ò já gèlè; kooro ló lè já.
english_literal: The jealous woman does not snatch her head gear off; all she can do is threaten a fight.
interpretation_gold: Some people are all mouth and no action.
deepseek_translation: The scarf did not tear into a headtie; it tore into strips.
claude_translation: Jealousy cannot tear a headtie; only a sharp object can tear it.
gemini_translation: The jealous person does not tie a headtie; it is the bald person who can tie it.
mistral_translation: The rain does not remove the headtie; it is the wind that can remove it.
llama_translation: The rain does not beat the drum; it is the thunder that beats the drum.
deepseek_interpretation: The outcome of a situation may not be as expected, but it still serves a purpose.
claude_interpretation: Mere envy or ill-will cannot destroy something solid or well-established; only direct action or real force can cause damage.
gemini_interpretation: Those who are envious or critical of others often lack the ability or opportunity to achieve what they criticize.
mistral_interpretation: External challenges alone cannot ruin one's dignity or status; it is one's own actions or carelessness that lead to downfall.
llama_interpretation: Power and authority are not the same as the ability to take action or make things happen.

yoruba: Ó ńti ilé bọ̀ kò ra ẹ̀gbẹ; ó dé oko tán ó ní ẹ̀gbẹ ni oníkú ẹ̀kọ.
english_literal: Leaving the home he did not purchase dried meat; after arriving on the farm he says dried meat is the indispensable thing to eat corn loaf with.
interpretation_gold: One should make provisions against one's future needs.
deepseek_translation: He who destroys his house does not buy a mat; he gets to the farm and says the mat belongs to the deceased farmer.
claude_translation: He was coming from home and didn't buy palm wine; when he arrived at the farm he said palm wine is what the corn seller has.
gemini_translation: He was coming from home and did not buy a side dish; when he got to the farm, he said the side dish is the owner of the eko (corn pudding).
mistral_translation: He was plastering the house and did not buy a fan; when he got to the farm, he said a fan is for the owner of the hoe
llama_translation: He who doesn't learn at home doesn't learn in the farm; he gets to the farm and says learning is the death of a farmer.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against destroying what you have, as you may later regret and falsely claim ownership of what remains.
claude_interpretation: People often make excuses or blame others for their own lack of preparation or foresight.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb criticizes someone who is unprepared or lazy and then blames others or circumstances for their shortcomings.
mistral_interpretation: People often neglect what they truly need until they are in a situation where it becomes essential.
llama_interpretation: One who fails to learn from their family and upbringing will struggle to learn and adapt in other environments.

yoruba: Olóúnjẹ-ẹ́ tó-ó bá kú.
english_literal: Someone who has food is worth dying with.
interpretation_gold: Food is a good enough reason to cast one's lot with another person's.
deepseek_translation: The owner of food is the one who dies.
claude_translation: The food owner who will die.
gemini_translation: The one who owns food will die.
mistral_translation: The owner of the food that is about to die.
llama_translation: The one who eats alone will die alone
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that those who possess resources are often the ones who face the consequences or responsibilities.
claude_interpretation: Everyone, regardless of their wealth or possessions, will eventually face death.
gemini_interpretation: Even the wealthy and powerful are subject to mortality.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against being overly possessive or greedy, as death can take everything away.
llama_interpretation: Selfishness and isolation can lead to one's downfall.

yoruba: Onígbèsè tí ńpa àpatà ẹyẹ́lé.
english_literal: Habitual debtor who butchers a pigeon for sale.
interpretation_gold: The debtor is desperate, because there is not much to a pigeon, and few people eat pigeons anyway.
deepseek_translation: The hunter who kills pigeons with a club.
claude_translation: A debtor who is killing the dove's rock/stone
gemini_translation: A debtor who kills a pigeon for sacrifice.
mistral_translation: The debtor who kills a pigeon on a rock
llama_translation: The one who is lazy will be beaten by the ant.
deepseek_interpretation: It criticizes unnecessary force or overkill in achieving a goal.
claude_interpretation: A person who destroys their own place of refuge or safety while trying to escape their problems will ultimately harm themselves.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to incur more debt or waste resources when already in debt, as it exacerbates the problem.
mistral_interpretation: A person in debt should not live extravagantly or waste resources they do not truly possess.
llama_interpretation: Hard work and diligence are essential to avoid being surpassed by others.

yoruba: Owó la fi ńlògbà; ọgbọ́n la fi ńgbélé ayé.
english_literal: It is with money that we secure pleasures; it is with wisdom that one secures a good life.
interpretation_gold: Riches are desirable, but wisdom is more valuable.
deepseek_translation: Money is used to grow old; wisdom is used to live on earth.
claude_translation: It is with money that we buy respect; it is with wisdom that we sustain life in the world.
gemini_translation: Money is used to cultivate a farm; wisdom is used to live life.
mistral_translation: We use money to build a fence; we use wisdom to navigate the world
llama_translation: Money is used to take care of the body; wisdom is used to navigate the world.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that while money is necessary for survival, wisdom is essential for a meaningful life.
claude_interpretation: While money can purchase temporary respect and status, it is wisdom that enables one to navigate and endure successfully in life.
gemini_interpretation: While resources are essential for practical endeavors, wisdom is paramount for navigating the complexities of life successfully.
mistral_interpretation: Wisdom is more valuable than wealth in overcoming life's challenges and earning respect
llama_interpretation: Wisdom is more valuable than wealth in navigating life's challenges.

yoruba: Ohun tí a ṣe nílé àna ẹni, “Ojú ńtì mí” kúrò níbẹ̀.
english_literal: What one does in the home of one's parents-in-law leaves no room for “I am bashful.”
interpretation_gold: One must not be reticent in doing whatever one must do.
deepseek_translation: What one does in the house of one's in-laws, 'My eyes are closed' is absent there.
claude_translation: What one does in one's in-laws' house, 'I am ashamed' should be removed from there.
gemini_translation: What is done in one's in-laws' house, "I am ashamed" is removed from there.
mistral_translation: What one does in a neighbor's house, 'My eyes are closed' does not remain there
llama_translation: What we do at home, 'my eyes are closed' will leave from there
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that one's actions are always observed, even when one thinks they are unnoticed.
claude_interpretation: One should act confidently and without shame when visiting or living with in-laws, as hesitation or embarrassment can create awkwardness in family relationships.
gemini_interpretation: One should not feel shame or embarrassment when performing duties or actions in their in-laws' home, as it is a place of acceptance and belonging.
mistral_interpretation: Actions taken in secrecy or without accountability will eventually be exposed or have consequences.
llama_interpretation: One's secrets will eventually be exposed if they are not careful about their actions at home.

yoruba: Owó ní ńpa ọjà ọ̀mọ̀ràn.
english_literal: It is money that brings a knowing person's trading to a conclusion.
interpretation_gold: A wise trader knows how to use his money to make his offer successful.
deepseek_translation: Money is what kills the wise person.
claude_translation: Money is what kills the market of the wise person.
gemini_translation: Money kills the market of the wise.
mistral_translation: Money is what kills the market of the wise child.
llama_translation: Money is the one that kills the market of children
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that greed or excessive pursuit of wealth can lead even the wisest to ruin.
claude_interpretation: Even wise people can make poor decisions when money is involved, as financial considerations can cloud good judgment.
gemini_interpretation: Even the most intelligent and skilled individuals can be hindered or rendered ineffective if they lack the necessary financial resources.
mistral_interpretation: Excessive wealth or greed can undermine the value of wisdom and good judgment.
llama_interpretation: Wealth and material possessions can be a corrupting influence on the young.

yoruba: Ó di kan-nu-rin kan-nu-rin, agogo Ògúntólú.
english_literal: All one hears is noise without pattern, like that of Oguntolu's bell.
interpretation_gold: The statements being made are senseless.
deepseek_translation: It becomes step by step, the clock of Oguntolu.
claude_translation: It has become kan-nu-rin kan-nu-rin, Oguntolu's bell.
gemini_translation: It becomes 'one-in-the-mouth, one-in-the-mouth,' the bell of Oguntolu.
mistral_translation: It has become one who walks stealthily, the bell of Ògúntólú
llama_translation: It has become a single step, a single step, the drum of Ògúntólú.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of patience and gradual progress in achieving success.
claude_interpretation: Something that was once valuable or functional has become worn out, damaged, or reduced to making only meaningless sounds.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes a situation where something is done repeatedly and persistently, like the continuous ringing of a bell.
mistral_interpretation: A person who acts deceptively or unpredictably will eventually reveal their true nature, just as a bell betrays the presence of its wearer.
llama_interpretation: A task or journey that was once difficult has become easy and manageable.

yoruba: Ojú kì í ti eégún kó má mọ̀nà ìgbàlẹ̀.
english_literal: A masquerader is never so shamed that he cannot find his way to the secret grove.
interpretation_gold: One cannot become so shamed abroad that one cannot return to the embrace of one's home.
deepseek_translation: The eye does not see the masquerade and not know the way to the shrine.
claude_translation: The eyes of a masquerader do not close without knowing the way home
gemini_translation: The masquerade does not get ashamed and not know the path to the grove.
mistral_translation: The eyes that have seen a masquerade should not lose the way to the grove
llama_translation: The eyes do not see the masquerade and still know the shrine.
deepseek_interpretation: One cannot encounter a problem without recognizing its source or solution.
claude_interpretation: No matter how far one ventures or how involved one becomes in activities, one should always know their way back to safety or their origins.
gemini_interpretation: Even in difficult or embarrassing situations, one should not forget their fundamental knowledge or responsibilities.
mistral_interpretation: Once you have witnessed something significant, you should not forget the lessons or experiences gained from it
llama_interpretation: One cannot know the true nature of something without experiencing it directly.

yoruba: O kò bá òkun máwo, o ò bá ọ̀sà mulẹ̀; abẹ́rẹ́ ẹ-ẹ́ bọ́ sódò o ní o ó yọ ọ́.
english_literal: You made no secret pact with the lagoon and you entered into no covenant with the ocean; yet when your needle dropped into the stream you proposed to retrieve it.
interpretation_gold: Unless one has extraordinary means one should not attempt the impossible.
deepseek_translation: You did not measure the depth of the ocean, you did not measure the depth of the lagoon; the needle that pricks you is the one that will remove it.
claude_translation: You don't touch the ocean with your hands, you don't touch the deity with your feet; when a needle falls into the river, you say you will retrieve it.
gemini_translation: You did not consult the sea, you did not make a pact with the lagoon; your needle fell into the river and you say you will retrieve it.
mistral_translation: If you do not meet the ocean at the shore, you will not meet the lagoon at its source; the needle you throw into the stream is what you will use to retrieve it.
llama_translation: He didn't meet the sea and ask for a passage, he didn't meet the god of the sea and ask for a place to stay; the one who is carrying a calabash on his head is the one who will ask for a rope to tie it.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that one must face the consequences of their actions, as the same source of a problem often holds its solution.
claude_interpretation: It warns against making impossible promises or attempting tasks that are clearly beyond one's capabilities.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to embark on a difficult task without proper preparation or consideration of the challenges involved.
mistral_interpretation: One must face the consequences of their actions, as what they put into a situation will determine what they get out of it.
llama_interpretation: One should be prepared for the consequences of one's actions and not expect others to bail them out.

yoruba: Ohun tí a ni la fi ńkẹ́ ọmọ ẹni.
english_literal: It is what one has that one uses to spoil one's child.
interpretation_gold: One should not go beyond one's means simply to make a good impression on others.
deepseek_translation: What we have is what we use to call our child.
claude_translation: It is what one has that one uses to teach one's child.
gemini_translation: It is what one has that one uses to pamper one's child.
mistral_translation: What we have is what we use to spoil our own child
llama_translation: What we have is what we use to take care of someone's child.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means people use what is available or familiar to them in naming or addressing their children.
claude_interpretation: Parents can only pass on to their children the knowledge, values, and resources they themselves possess.
gemini_interpretation: One should only provide for their children within their means, not beyond them.
mistral_interpretation: People often misuse their own resources or privileges to harm those closest to them, such as family.
llama_interpretation: One should take care of others' children with the same resources they have.

yoruba: Ohun tó ní òun óò ṣeni lẹ́rú, tó wá ṣeni níwọ̀fà, ká gbà á.
english_literal: If whatever promised to make one a slave only makes one a pawn, one should accept one's fate.
interpretation_gold: One should gratefully accept a fate that turns out more merciful than what could have been.
deepseek_translation: What says it will not enslave someone, then goes ahead to enslave them subtly, we should accept it.
claude_translation: Something that says it will not make one a slave, but comes to make one a servant, let us accept it.
gemini_translation: That which says it will enslave one, but then makes one a pawn, let's accept it.
mistral_translation: The thing that claims it will carry a load, which then claims it has a pawn, let us accept it
llama_translation: What has its own owner at home, comes to the market to beg, let it be taken.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against deceptive promises or actions that ultimately lead to control or subjugation.
claude_interpretation: It is better to accept a lesser burden or compromise than to risk facing a much worse situation.
gemini_interpretation: It is wise to accept a less severe outcome when a worse one was anticipated or threatened.
mistral_interpretation: Accept help or responsibility from someone only after verifying their capability, not their empty promises
llama_interpretation: One who has the means to take care of themselves should not beg from others.

yoruba: O rojọ́ láàárọ̀ o ò jàre, ó dalẹ́ o ní kọ́ba dúró gbọ́ tẹnu ẹ; ohun tó o wí láàárọ̀ náà kọ́ lo máa wí lálẹ́?
english_literal: You state your case in the morning and you are not vindicated, and at nightfall you plead with the king to delay a bit and listen to what you have to say; isn't what you have to say in the evening the same thing you said in the morning?
interpretation_gold: Repeated stating will not make a bad case a good one.
deepseek_translation: You refused to fight in the morning, now in the evening you say the king should wait to hear you; what you said in the morning, will you not say it in the evening?
claude_translation: It rained in the morning and you didn't dance, it stopped in the evening and you want the king to stand and listen to you; is what you will say in the evening not the same thing you would have said in the morning?
gemini_translation: You complained in the morning and were not justified, it is evening and you say the king should stop and listen to your words; is it not what you said in the morning that you will say in the evening?
mistral_translation: You said it in the morning and it was not fought, in the evening you say you will wait to hear it from your mouth; what you said in the morning, will it not be said in the evening?
llama_translation: The one who is crying in the morning, will he not cry in the evening too? What he said in the morning, will he not say in the evening?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against procrastination and indecision, emphasizing that delaying action often leads to missed opportunities.
claude_interpretation: One should seize opportunities when they arise rather than waiting until it's too late to demand attention for the same matter.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb advises against repeating the same ineffective arguments or complaints, especially when they have already been dismissed.
mistral_interpretation: A promise or statement made earlier should not be retracted or denied later, as consistency is valued.
llama_interpretation: Consistency is expected in one's words and actions.

yoruba: Ohùn àgbà: bí kò ta ìgún, a ta èbù.
english_literal: An elder's voice: if it does not yield yams ready for pounding (for food), it will yield yam seedlings ready for planting.
interpretation_gold: There is some value in whatever comes out of an elder's mouth.
deepseek_translation: The elder's voice: if it does not sell the vulture, it sells the kite.
claude_translation: The voice of an elder: if it doesn't sell vulture, it sells dust.
gemini_translation: The voice of an elder: if it does not hit the heel, it hits the ankle.
mistral_translation: The voice of the elder: if the vulture does not sell, the kite will sell
llama_translation: The elder's word: if the vulture is not available, we use the kite.
deepseek_interpretation: An elder's advice is valuable and will always be useful in some way, even if not in the expected manner.
claude_interpretation: An elder's words carry weight and influence - even when they seem to offer something worthless, people will still listen and respond.
gemini_interpretation: The words or advice of an elder, whether direct or indirect, will inevitably have an impact or consequence.
mistral_interpretation: The wisdom or advice of elders will always prove useful, even if its immediate value is not apparent.
llama_interpretation: One must adapt and make do with what is available when the preferred option is not accessible.

yoruba: Ojú la fi ḿmọ àísí epo; ẹnu la fi ḿmọ àìsíyọ̀; ọbẹ̀ tí ò bá lépo nínú òkèèrè la ti ḿmọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: It is with the eyes that one tells the absence of palm-oil; it is with the mouth that one determines the absence of salt; if a stew lacks oil, it is the eyes that will tell.
interpretation_gold: In some matters the evidence of the eyes is enough to tell one all one needs to know.
deepseek_translation: The eyes are used to recognize the absence of palm oil; the mouth is used to recognize the absence of salt; it is the soup that lacks palm oil that we recognize from afar.
claude_translation: It is with the eyes we know the absence of palm oil; it is with the mouth we know the absence of salt; soup that has no palm oil in it, we know it from afar.
gemini_translation: It is by sight that we know the absence of palm oil; it is by the mouth that we know the absence of salt; soup that has no palm oil, we know it from afar.
mistral_translation: It is with the eyes that one knows the absence of palm oil; it is with the mouth that one knows the absence of salt; the soup that lacks palm oil in the pot is what one has already known.
llama_translation: The eyes are used to search for palm oil; the mouth is used to search for what is not there; the knife that does not cut in the kitchen is used to cut in the forest.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that certain deficiencies or flaws are easily noticeable even from a distance, emphasizing the importance of maintaining good qualities to avoid public scrutiny.
claude_interpretation: Some deficiencies or shortcomings are immediately obvious and cannot be hidden from those who know what to look for.
gemini_interpretation: Deficiencies or problems are often evident through observable signs, even before direct experience.
mistral_interpretation: Observation and direct experience are the most reliable ways to recognize a deficiency or problem.
llama_interpretation: One should use the right tool or approach for the right situation.

yoruba: Ojú kì í ti àgbà lóru; jagun a lóṣòó góńgó.
english_literal: An elderly person does not become embarrassed under cover of darkness; the stalwart squats nonchalantly.
interpretation_gold: One can do whatever one pleased when no eyes are watching.
deepseek_translation: The eye does not grow old in the dark; the warrior does not carry a sheath for nothing.
claude_translation: The eyes do not shame an elder at night; a warrior will have tall spears tomorrow.
gemini_translation: The elder's eye does not get ashamed at night; the warrior has a prominent beard.
mistral_translation: The eyes do not stay awake at night for an elder; it is the warrior who stays awake in the watchtower
llama_translation: The eye does not reach the elder's head; it is the warrior that reaches the elder's head.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that experience and wisdom come with age and challenges, and one should always be prepared for what they are trained or destined to do.
claude_interpretation: An experienced person maintains their dignity and preparedness even in difficult times, knowing that better days and opportunities for action will come.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that experience and wisdom, like an elder's vision in the dark or a warrior's distinguishing beard, are inherently valuable and evident regardless of circumstances.
mistral_interpretation: Responsibility and vigilance are often shouldered by those who are capable and prepared, not necessarily by those who are older or in authority
llama_interpretation: Respect and authority are earned through bravery and strength, not just age.

yoruba: Owó kì í yéye kọ́mọ ó kú.
english_literal: If money is available in abundance, a child does not die.
interpretation_gold: One should spare no expenses to take care of one's children or one's affairs.
deepseek_translation: Money does not understand that its owner is dead.
claude_translation: Money does not become worthless because a child dies
gemini_translation: Money does not stop a child from dying.
mistral_translation: Money does not play around, or the child will die.
llama_translation: Money does not make a child die
deepseek_interpretation: Material wealth is meaningless after death, emphasizing the futility of prioritizing possessions over life.
claude_interpretation: Material wealth retains its value regardless of personal tragedies or emotional circumstances.
gemini_interpretation: Wealth cannot prevent the inevitable, such as death.
mistral_interpretation: Financial responsibility is crucial to prevent serious consequences for one's dependents.
llama_interpretation: Wealth is not a guarantee of a child's survival or well-being.

yoruba: Onígbá ní ńpe igbá ẹ̀ ní àíkàrágbá káyé tó fi kólẹ̀.
english_literal: It is the owner of the calabash who first called it a broken piece of gourd before the world used it for scooping dirt.
interpretation_gold: If one does not value what one has, other people will value it even less.
deepseek_translation: The owner of the calabash is the one who calls the calabash 'mine' without hesitation until it breaks.
claude_translation: The calabash owner calls his calabash 'the unbreakable one' until the day it falls and breaks.
gemini_translation: The owner of the calabash is the one who calls his calabash 'not strong enough' before the world takes it away.
mistral_translation: The owner of the calabash calls the calabash a worthless container that is used to cover things
llama_translation: The calabash seller calls the calabash a deceitful calabash, yet he uses it to carry his load.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of ownership and responsibility, suggesting that one should take care of what is theirs until it is no longer usable.
claude_interpretation: People often boast about their possessions or abilities until reality proves them wrong.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to publicly devalue your own possessions or abilities, as it invites others to exploit or dismiss them.
mistral_interpretation: People often undervalue or dismiss what they possess while admiring or desiring what others have.
llama_interpretation: One should not despise or devalue something just because of its flaws or imperfections, as it may still be useful.

yoruba: Ohun tí a bá pàdé ò jọ ohun tí a rí tẹ́lẹ̀.
english_literal: That which one comes upon is nothing to compare to what one has always had.
interpretation_gold: No new friend or find can be as valuable as that one has had for some time.
deepseek_translation: What we meet does not resemble what we saw before.
claude_translation: What we encounter is not the same as what we saw before
gemini_translation: What we meet is not like what we saw before.
mistral_translation: What we encounter is not the same as what we saw before
llama_translation: What we encounter in the morning is different from what we see in the evening
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that experiences are unique and should not be judged based on past encounters.
claude_interpretation: Reality often differs from our expectations or previous experiences, so we should be prepared for change and not assume things will remain the same.
gemini_interpretation: New experiences often differ from our expectations or previous knowledge.
mistral_interpretation: Life's experiences are unpredictable, and one should not assume the future will mirror the past.
llama_interpretation: Circumstances can change rapidly, so be prepared for unexpected developments.

yoruba: Obìnrin ò gbé ibi tó máa rọ̀ ọ́ lọ́rùn.
english_literal: A woman never remains where her well being rests.
interpretation_gold: Women seldom know until it is too late which home would best suit them.
deepseek_translation: A woman does not carry the place she will urinate on her neck.
claude_translation: A woman does not carry a load that will make her neck sore.
gemini_translation: A woman does not live where she will be comfortable.
mistral_translation: A woman does not carry the place she will cry to on her neck.
llama_translation: A woman does not stay in a place where she is not being pampered.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not prematurely reveal their plans or intentions.
claude_interpretation: People should not take on burdens or responsibilities beyond their capacity to handle comfortably.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb suggests that women often face challenges and discomfort in life, implying a societal expectation of resilience or a commentary on their often-difficult circumstances.
mistral_interpretation: One should not invite or create trouble that will later cause regret or suffering.
llama_interpretation: A woman deserves to be treated with care and respect in her relationship.

yoruba: Ó yẹ kí eégún mọ ẹni tó mú àgbò so.
english_literal: It is proper that the masquerader know who tethered the ram.
interpretation_gold: One should acknowledge those who have done one some favor.
deepseek_translation: The masquerade should know the person who ties the goat.
claude_translation: It is fitting for the masquerader to know who holds the rope
gemini_translation: It is proper for the masquerade to know who tied the ram.
mistral_translation: It is proper for the masquerade to know who tied the ram to it
llama_translation: It is not good for the masquerade to know who is behind the mask.
deepseek_interpretation: One should acknowledge and respect those who have helped or supported them.
claude_interpretation: Those in positions of power or performance should be aware of who controls or supports them behind the scenes.
gemini_interpretation: One should acknowledge and appreciate the source of their support or success.
mistral_interpretation: One should recognize and acknowledge those who support or enable their success or position.
llama_interpretation: Secrecy is essential in certain situations to maintain respect and avoid conflict.

yoruba: Orí tí yó jẹ igún kì í gbọ́; bí wọ́n fun ládìẹ kò níí gbà.
english_literal: The head that is destined to eat a vulture cannot be saved; if a chicken is offered to it it will refuse.
interpretation_gold: The person destined to suffer will manage to succumb to the suffering even in spite of efforts by others to save him/her.
deepseek_translation: A head that will become vulture's does not hear; if they give it chicken, it will not accept.
claude_translation: The head that will eat vulture does not refuse; if they give it to a fowl it will not accept.
gemini_translation: The head that will eat vulture does not hear; if they give it a chicken, it will not accept.
mistral_translation: The vulture's head that will be eaten does not listen; even if they cook it for the chicken, it will not accept
llama_translation: The head that is destined to wear a crown will not be rejected; even if they try to give it to a slave, it will not accept.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against stubbornness and refusing good advice or opportunities, as it leads to inevitable downfall.
claude_interpretation: People have different destinies and what is meant for one person may not be suitable for another.
gemini_interpretation: Some people are so set on a destructive path that they will reject good alternatives, even when offered.
mistral_interpretation: A person destined for misfortune will not heed warnings or change their fate, no matter how favorable the alternatives appear.
llama_interpretation: One's destiny and rightful status cannot be altered or taken away by external forces.

yoruba: Ooré pẹ́, aṣiwèrè-é gbàgbé.
english_literal: The favor is long past; the imbecile forgets.
interpretation_gold: Only an imbecile forgets a favor even long after it was done.
deepseek_translation: Friendship is long, madness is forgotten.
claude_translation: Friendship lasts long, but a foolish person forgets.
gemini_translation: Goodness lasts long, the foolish one forgets.
mistral_translation: The favor is great, the madman forgets it.
llama_translation: Friendship is sweet, but the test of it is bitter
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that true friendship endures even when one friend acts foolishly or makes mistakes.
claude_interpretation: True friendship endures over time, but foolish people fail to remember or value the kindness and loyalty shown to them.
gemini_interpretation: People with good intentions often have their kindness taken for granted or forgotten by those who are foolish or ungrateful.
mistral_interpretation: People often forget or take for granted the kindness shown to them when they are in a difficult situation.
llama_interpretation: True friendship is proven in difficult times.

yoruba: O rí ẹsẹ̀-ẹ wèrè o ò bù ú ṣoògùn; níbo lo ti máa rí tọlọgbọ́n?
english_literal: You see the footprint of an imbecile and you do not take soil from it to make a charm; where will you find the footprint of a wise person?
interpretation_gold: One should take advantage of the weak and vulnerable, because one will not be able to take advantage of the strong.
deepseek_translation: You see the footprint of the monkey but you do not see the footprint of the baboon; where then will you see that of the cat?
claude_translation: You see a madman's leg and you don't prepare medicine for it; where will you find a wise person's?
gemini_translation: You saw the footprints of a mad person and you did not use them for medicine; where then will you find those of a wise person?
mistral_translation: You see a madman's footprints but do not avoid the medicine; where will you find wisdom?
llama_translation: He sees the foot of a madman and doesn't take medicine; where will he see a herbalist?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against selective perception or hypocrisy, emphasizing that overlooking obvious faults while focusing on minor ones leads to flawed judgment.
claude_interpretation: One should take advantage of available opportunities to help or learn, as better chances may not come again.
gemini_interpretation: If you cannot take advantage of readily available opportunities, you will not be able to seize more difficult or rare ones.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb teaches that ignoring obvious warnings or signs of danger due to overconfidence can lead to foolish mistakes.
llama_interpretation: One should take preventive measures when they see signs of trouble or danger.

yoruba: O wà láyé, mo wà láàyè, ò ḿbi mí bí ọ̀rún ṣe rí.
english_literal: You are on earth “alive” and I am on earth, and yet you ask me what heaven is like.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person seeking information from someone in no better position to know than the seeker.
deepseek_translation: You exist on earth, I exist on earth, you don't know me like the sun knows.
claude_translation: You are alive, I am alive, it does not concern me how the sky looks
gemini_translation: You are alive, I am alive, you are asking me how the sky looks.
mistral_translation: I am in the world, I am in existence, I do not know how heaven looks
llama_translation: You are in the world, I am in the world, you don't know me as heaven knows me.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that mere coexistence does not guarantee deep understanding or familiarity between people.
claude_interpretation: As long as we are both well and alive, external circumstances or appearances don't matter to me.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to ask someone for information that is readily available to both parties.
mistral_interpretation: One should focus on the present reality rather than worrying about unknown or divine matters beyond human understanding.
llama_interpretation: No one truly knows another person's inner nature or character, not even those closest to them.

yoruba: O fẹ́ joyè o ní o-ò ní-í jà.
english_literal: You aspire to taking a chieftaincy title and you say you will not get into a fight.
interpretation_gold: It is self-deceit to wish for something without being prepared for the struggle it demands.
deepseek_translation: He wants the title but does not want to fight.
claude_translation: You want to become a chief but you say you will not fight.
gemini_translation: You want to be a chief, but you say you will not fight.
mistral_translation: You want to be a chief but you do not have the strength to fight.
llama_translation: He wants to eat and he has a mouth to eat with
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes those who desire honor or position without being willing to endure the necessary struggles or responsibilities.
claude_interpretation: Leadership requires courage and the willingness to face challenges and conflicts.
gemini_interpretation: Achieving a position of power or influence often requires overcoming challenges and engaging in struggles.
mistral_interpretation: Desiring a position of leadership or responsibility without the necessary ability or effort is futile.
llama_interpretation: One should be content with what they have and not covet what others have.

yoruba: Ohun tó fọ́ni lójú ló ńjúwe ọ̀nà fúnni.
english_literal: Whatever deprives one of one's sight is the same thing that shows one the way.
interpretation_gold: Misfortune teaches those its afflicts how to cope with it.
deepseek_translation: What passes in front of one's eyes is what shows one the way.
claude_translation: What breaks one's eye is what shows one the way
gemini_translation: What blinds one's eyes is what shows one the way.
mistral_translation: What blinds a person is what they use to look at the path for themselves.
llama_translation: What is on the head is what shows on the face, it is what shows on the road to the buttocks.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that personal experience and observation are the best guides in life.
claude_interpretation: Painful experiences or failures often teach us valuable lessons and guide us toward better paths in life.
gemini_interpretation: Difficult experiences or setbacks can often provide valuable lessons and guidance for the future.
mistral_interpretation: One's own flaws or biases often prevent them from seeing the right way forward.
llama_interpretation: One's true nature will eventually be revealed, no matter how hard they try to hide it.

yoruba: Olówe laláṣẹ̀ ọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: A person who knows proverbs has the last word in a dispute.
interpretation_gold: There is no authority like proverbial authority.
deepseek_translation: The owner of the knife is the owner of the yam.
claude_translation: The literate person is the commander of words
gemini_translation: The proverb-sayer is the one who gives authority to words.
mistral_translation: The owner of the broom is the one who sweeps the matter.
llama_translation: The owner of a house is the one who knows its corners.
deepseek_interpretation: The person in control of resources has the power to decide their use or distribution.
claude_interpretation: Education and literacy give one power and authority over language and communication.
gemini_interpretation: Proverbs carry significant weight and authority in Yoruba communication, often used to validate or conclude an argument.
mistral_interpretation: The person directly involved in a situation is the one responsible for resolving it.
llama_interpretation: One who is familiar with a situation or place is best suited to navigate its complexities.

yoruba: Ràdà-ràdà-á mọ ibi tí ó ńrè.
english_literal: The meandering person knows where he is headed.
interpretation_gold: A person may seem without a purpose, but he or she is engaged in some thing known to himself or herself.
deepseek_translation: The crab knows where it is crawling to.
claude_translation: The wanderer knows where he is going.
gemini_translation: The wanderer knows where he is going.
mistral_translation: The cutlass will eventually know where it is going
llama_translation: The one who is always running knows where he is going.
deepseek_interpretation: One's actions are guided by personal knowledge and intentions.
claude_interpretation: Someone who appears to be moving aimlessly actually has a clear purpose or destination in mind.
gemini_interpretation: Even someone who appears aimless may have a clear purpose or destination in mind.
mistral_interpretation: Every action or decision will ultimately reveal its consequences or purpose
llama_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of being focused and having a clear direction in life.

yoruba: Rírí tí a rí igún la fi ńta igún lọ́fà.
english_literal: It is because one sees the vulture that one shoots arrows at it.
interpretation_gold: If one does not make oneself available, one would not present a target for people's hostility.
deepseek_translation: The way we see the vulture is how we hunt the vulture.
claude_translation: It is by seeing how we have seen the vulture that we shoot arrows at the vulture
gemini_translation: It is by seeing the vulture that we shoot the vulture with an arrow.
mistral_translation: It is the manner in which we see the vulture that we use to shoot the vulture with an arrow
llama_translation: The noise that we make to scare away vultures is what we use to invite vultures.
deepseek_interpretation: One's approach to a situation depends on their perception of it.
claude_interpretation: We judge and treat others based on our past experiences and observations of their behavior.
gemini_interpretation: One must identify a problem or target before attempting to address or achieve it.
mistral_interpretation: One should approach a problem or person based on their observed behavior or nature, not assumptions.
llama_interpretation: One's actions can sometimes attract the very problem they are intended to prevent.

yoruba: Rà á ire, gà á ire; ìpéǹpéjú ni àlà-a fìlà.
english_literal: Press it well on the head; puff it out; the eyebrow is the limit for the cap.
interpretation_gold: One may be free to use one's possession as one pleases, but there are still some conventions one must observe.
deepseek_translation: Buy good, sell good; the turban is folded from the edge.
claude_translation: Buy it well, wear it well; patience is the ornament of a cap
gemini_translation: Buy good, wear good; the eyelid is the brim of the cap.
mistral_translation: Buy good fortune, sell good fortune; it is the excessive haste that spoils the cap.
llama_translation: Wealth is a blessing, poverty is a blessing; it is the heart that is the true garment.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches the importance of integrity and fairness in business dealings, suggesting that success comes from honest practices.
claude_interpretation: Quality investment and careful use require patience, as rushing leads to poor outcomes.
gemini_interpretation: What you invest in or put out is what you will receive or experience in return, just as the eyelid naturally serves as a protective brim for the eye.
mistral_interpretation: Overly rushing decisions or actions can ruin even the most promising opportunities.
llama_interpretation: One's true character is revealed by their attitude and behavior, regardless of their economic circumstances.

yoruba: Sọ̀rọ̀ kí ọlọ́rọ̀ gbọ́, àbùkù ní ńfi kanni.
english_literal: Spreading rumors into the ears of the subject of the rumor brings disgrace to one.
interpretation_gold: One should refrain from rumor mongering.
deepseek_translation: It is difficult for the rich to hear, the poor are the ones who use their ears.
claude_translation: Speak so that the wise person may hear, it is disgrace that one uses to kill oneself
gemini_translation: Speak so that the rich person hears, it is disgrace that it brings to one.
mistral_translation: Words that the wealthy person hears, the poor person uses to cover their shame
llama_translation: The noise that the drum makes, the calabash hears it and is afraid
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb suggests that wealthy people often ignore advice or warnings, while the poor are more attentive and receptive.
claude_interpretation: Speaking foolishly or inappropriately brings shame and destruction upon oneself, so one should speak wisely for intelligent people to listen.
gemini_interpretation: Speaking ill of a wealthy or powerful person can lead to negative consequences for the speaker.
mistral_interpretation: People often adopt the advice or criticisms meant for others to hide their own shortcomings.
llama_interpretation: One should be mindful of the consequences of their actions, as they can have a ripple effect on others.

yoruba: “Sìn mí ká relé àna,” ó wẹ̀wù ẹtù.
english_literal: “Go with me to my in-laws' home,” and he wore a garment made from rich hand-woven material.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person who attempts to steal other people's glory when he/she is supposed to be helping them.
deepseek_translation: “Help me down to the ground,” it burdens the ant.
claude_translation: Follow me let's go to the in-laws' house, he wore guinea fowl feathers
gemini_translation: “Accompany me to my in-laws’ house,” he wore a guinea fowl feather garment.
mistral_translation: “Lean on me to reach your hometown,” said the vulture to the antelope.
llama_translation: I am not going, it is the cloth that is going.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against imposing excessive demands on those who are already struggling.
claude_interpretation: One should dress appropriately and present themselves well when visiting important people or attending significant occasions.
gemini_interpretation: One should dress appropriately for the occasion, especially when seeking assistance or making a request.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb warns against trusting deceptive offers of help from those who may harm you.
llama_interpretation: One's appearance or attire can sometimes be more noticeable than the person themselves.

yoruba: Tábà tí ò dùn, ẹnu ò tà á.
english_literal: Snuff that is not pleasant, the mouth cannot not sell.
interpretation_gold: No amount of talk will make something unpleasant become pleasant.
deepseek_translation: The tobacco that is not sweet, the mouth does not chew it.
claude_translation: Tobacco that is not sweet, the mouth does not chew it.
gemini_translation: Tobacco that is not sweet, the mouth does not sell it.
mistral_translation: The tobacco that is not sweet, the mouth does not sell it.
llama_translation: A stubborn person does not know sweetness, the mouth does not taste it.
deepseek_interpretation: People avoid things that are unpleasant or unbeneficial.
claude_interpretation: People naturally avoid or reject things that do not bring them pleasure or benefit.
gemini_interpretation: People do not promote or praise things that are not good or beneficial.
mistral_interpretation: People naturally promote or endorse only what they find valuable or enjoyable.
llama_interpretation: Stubbornness can lead to missing out on life's pleasures and goodness.

yoruba: Tẹni ntẹni; bí àpọ́n bá sun iṣu a bù fọ́mọ-ọ ẹ̀.
english_literal: One's own is one's own; when a man without a wife roasts yams he cuts a piece for his child.
interpretation_gold: One makes do with what one has.
deepseek_translation: Everyone for themselves; if the apron burns the yam, it will throw the child away.
claude_translation: One person is one person; if a bachelor roasts yam, it breaks into pieces for his child
gemini_translation: What belongs to one belongs to one; if a bachelor roasts yam, he will give it to his child.
mistral_translation: Each person to their own; if a bag of yams sleeps, it will sprout shoots for its owner
llama_translation: We are all equal; if a calabash falls on a yam, it will not break the yam's child.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes self-preservation, suggesting that in dire situations, individuals prioritize their own survival over others.
claude_interpretation: Even someone without family responsibilities will naturally think of and provide for children when they have something good.
gemini_interpretation: People prioritize their own and their immediate family's needs and interests.
mistral_interpretation: Everyone reaps the consequences of their own actions or inactions, whether positive or negative.
llama_interpretation: Everyone has their own unique strength and resilience, and no one can be easily broken or intimidated by others.

yoruba: Ta ní jẹ́ jẹ ọṣẹ kó fògìrì fọṣọ?
english_literal: Who would eat soap and wash clothes with fermented beans?
interpretation_gold: Who would seek unease when ease is available?
deepseek_translation: Who is it that eats the yam and the peel falls off?
claude_translation: Who will eat soap so that foam can wash clothes?
gemini_translation: Who would eat soap and then use ogiri to wash clothes?
mistral_translation: Who will eat soap and then go about naked?
llama_translation: Who eats the soup of the deity and then insults the deity's priest?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb questions the possibility of benefiting from something without facing its consequences.
claude_interpretation: No one should sacrifice themselves or suffer harm just so others can benefit from the consequences of that sacrifice.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to use something valuable or beneficial in a way that is inappropriate or counterproductive.
mistral_interpretation: One should not act in a way that contradicts their own well-being or self-respect.
llama_interpretation: One should not disrespect those who have helped or supported them.

yoruba: Tinú ọ̀lẹ lọ̀lẹ ńjẹ; aṣiwèrè èèyàn ni ò mọ èrú tí yó gbà.
english_literal: The lazy person eats the products of his native wisdom; only a fool does not know what devious way will be fruitful.
interpretation_gold: If one lacks industry, one had better be resourceful.
deepseek_translation: The lazy person eats in anger; a foolish person does not know the load they will carry.
claude_translation: It is from the lazy person's stomach that the lazy person eats; it is a foolish person who does not know the suffering they will endure.
gemini_translation: It is from the lazy person's inside that laziness eats; it is a foolish person who does not know the load they will carry.
mistral_translation: The lazy person's stomach eats at night; it is a mad person who does not know the burden they will carry
llama_translation: The cold is not cold; it is the fear of the cold that we know when it bites.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against laziness and foolishness, emphasizing that irresponsible behavior leads to unnecessary hardship.
claude_interpretation: Lazy people will eventually face the consequences of their idleness through hunger and hardship, but only foolish people fail to recognize the suffering that awaits them due to their laziness.
gemini_interpretation: Laziness ultimately harms the lazy individual, and a wise person anticipates the consequences of their actions.
mistral_interpretation: A lazy person will suffer consequences later, just as a foolish person fails to anticipate the troubles ahead
llama_interpretation: Fear of a situation can be more debilitating than the situation itself.

yoruba: Tẹ̀tẹ́ ní ńṣíwájú eré sísa.
english_literal: A child's learning to walk comes before running.
interpretation_gold: One should observe some order in what one does.
deepseek_translation: Early is the one that goes ahead of the race.
claude_translation: Slowly is what leads ahead in the game of running
gemini_translation: Tete (a type of vegetable) precedes the running race.
mistral_translation: It is gradually that one progresses in a game of intelligence.
llama_translation: The tortoise precedes the lizard to the dance
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of starting early to achieve success.
claude_interpretation: Steady persistence and patience often lead to better results than rushing hastily.
gemini_interpretation: One must prepare adequately before embarking on a task or challenge.
mistral_interpretation: Success in complex endeavors requires patience, persistence, and step-by-step effort rather than rushing.
llama_interpretation: One must be prepared and take initiative to achieve success.

yoruba: Tìẹ́ sàn, tèmí sàn, lolókùnrùn méjì-í fi ńdìmú.
english_literal: “Your condition is better; My condition is better,” is what gets two invalids into a fight.
interpretation_gold: Fools will fight over the most stupid things.
deepseek_translation: The head is good, the mind is good, two deep wells are not drunk from.
claude_translation: Yours is good, mine is good, that's how two friends maintain their friendship
gemini_translation: Yours is good, mine is good, is how two sick people hold on to each other.
mistral_translation: Mine is good, yours is good, but it is the two small pieces of okra that are causing the dispute
llama_translation: The earth is wide, the sky is wide, two deaf people are arguing
deepseek_interpretation: Having multiple good options does not mean one should pursue them all at once.
claude_interpretation: Mutual respect and acknowledgment of each other's worth is essential for maintaining lasting friendships.
gemini_interpretation: People in similar unfortunate circumstances often find solace and support in each other.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights how minor or trivial matters often lead to unnecessary conflict between people.
llama_interpretation: It highlights the futility of arguing with someone who refuses to listen or understand.

yoruba: “Tèmi ò ṣòro,” tí kì í jẹ kọ́mọ alágbẹ̀dẹ ní idà.
english_literal: “Mine is not urgent.” which prevents the son of the blacksmith from owning a sword.
interpretation_gold: The person who always yields to others will never get anywhere.
deepseek_translation: "Mine is not difficult," says the blacksmith's child who does not eat iron.
claude_translation: Mine is not difficult, that which does not allow the blacksmith's child to learn sword-making.
gemini_translation: “Mine is not difficult,” is what prevents the blacksmith’s child from having a sword.
mistral_translation: “Mine is not difficult,” said the one who is not the child of a blacksmith with a sword.
llama_translation: My ear is not deaf, yet I do not hear the cry of the child in the womb.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against underestimating challenges one has not personally experienced.
claude_interpretation: People often avoid learning difficult skills by claiming they are easy, but their avoidance reveals the true difficulty.
gemini_interpretation: Overconfidence or a belief that one's own situation is easy can lead to a lack of preparedness or the failure to acquire necessary skills or tools.
mistral_interpretation: People often underestimate tasks they have not personally experienced or mastered.
llama_interpretation: One should not feign ignorance of a situation when they are actually aware of it.

yoruba: Tẹni ní ńjọni lójú; eèrà-á bímọ-ọ ẹ̀ ó sọ ọ́ ní òyírìgbí.
english_literal: One's own thing is what impresses one; the ant has a child and names it The-one-who-rolls-mightily-around.
interpretation_gold: One always tends to overestimate the worth of one's possession.
deepseek_translation: It is one's own that dances in the eye; the ant gives birth to its child and calls it tiny.
claude_translation: It is one's own person that disgraces one in public; an ant cannot give birth and call its child a cricket.
gemini_translation: What one has is what one resembles; the ant gives birth to its child and calls it 'òyírìgbí'.
mistral_translation: It is the owner who recognizes their own in the crowd; the ant's child will say it has a distinctive waistline.
llama_translation: The one who has a wound on his face; his child will not tell him it is ugly.
deepseek_interpretation: People naturally favor and cherish their own, often overlooking flaws or shortcomings.
claude_interpretation: People bring shame upon themselves through their own actions, just as one cannot produce something and falsely claim it to be what it is not.
gemini_interpretation: People tend to value and identify with what is their own, even if it seems insignificant to others.
mistral_interpretation: Only those closely familiar with something or someone can truly recognize their unique qualities or identity.
llama_interpretation: Family members are reluctant to criticize or correct their own relatives, even when it is necessary.

yoruba: Wò mí lójú, wò mí lẹ́ẹ̀kẹ́; ẹni a bá lọ sóde là ńwò lójú.
english_literal: Keep your eyes on my face, and keep your eyes on my cheeks; one keeps one's eyes on the person with whom one goes visiting.
interpretation_gold: People should not cultivate wandering eyes.
deepseek_translation: Look at me in the face, look at me on the cheek; it is the person we are going outside with that we look at in the face.
claude_translation: Look at me in the face, look at me in the back; it is the person we go out with that we look in the face
gemini_translation: Look at me in the eye, look at me on the cheek; it is the person we go out with that we look in the eye.
mistral_translation: Look at me in the face, look at me in the armpit; it is the one we go outside with that we look at in the face.
llama_translation: Look at me in the face, look at me on the leg; whoever goes outside will look at the face.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of trusting and valuing those who are truly present and supportive in one's life.
claude_interpretation: We should judge people by their character and actions when we interact with them closely, not by superficial appearances or what others say about them.
gemini_interpretation: One should give attention and respect to those they are closely associated with or depend on.
mistral_interpretation: People tend to respect and pay attention to those who are present or visible in public, rather than those who remain hidden or inactive.
llama_interpretation: One's true character is revealed in their actions outside of their home or familiar environment.

yoruba: Wèrè-é dùn-ún wò, kò ṣé-é bí lọ́mọ.
english_literal: An imbecile makes an entertaining spectacle, but one would not want one as one's child.
interpretation_gold: One might be tolerant of simplicity or irresponsibility in other people, but not in one's own relatives.
deepseek_translation: Madness is sweet to watch, but not good to have as a child.
claude_translation: Madness is sweet to watch, but it cannot be used to bear children
gemini_translation: Madness is pleasant to watch, but it is not pleasant to have as a child.
mistral_translation: The madman looks pleasant, but he is not like a child
llama_translation: A madman's dance is sweet to watch, but not to be imitated by a child.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against enjoying others' misfortunes, as similar troubles could befall you or your loved ones.
claude_interpretation: Entertainment or spectacle may be amusing to observe, but it has no productive value for serious life endeavors.
gemini_interpretation: It is easy to observe and be entertained by the flaws or misfortunes of others, but it is difficult and undesirable to experience them personally.
mistral_interpretation: Outward appearances can be deceptive; not everything that seems harmless or appealing is truly innocent or safe
llama_interpretation: One should not imitate the actions of someone who is not in their right mind, no matter how appealing they may seem.

yoruba: Wèrè-é yàtọ̀ sí wéré; wéré kì í ṣe wèrè; ìjá yàtọ̀ sí eré.
english_literal: Madness differs from the singing of Islamic songs; the singing of Islamic songs is not madness; fighting is different from playing.
interpretation_gold: One should not confuse jesting with quarrelling.
deepseek_translation: A madman is different from a playful person; a playful person is not a madman; a fight is different from a play.
claude_translation: Madness is different from being mad; being mad does not make one mad; fighting is different from playing
gemini_translation: Madness is different from haste; haste is not madness; a fight is different from a game.
mistral_translation: Madness is different from madness; madness is not madness; fighting is different from play
llama_translation: A madman is not a madman in his father's house; a madman is a madman in the market; a slave is not a slave in his father's house.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against mistaking playful or unserious behavior for genuine madness or conflict.
claude_interpretation: There are important distinctions between similar-seeming things, and one should not confuse temporary states with permanent conditions or serious matters with trivial ones.
gemini_interpretation: It is important to distinguish between similar-sounding or appearing concepts, as their true nature and implications can be vastly different.
mistral_interpretation: Not all unusual or disruptive behavior is the same—some actions may appear similar but have different underlying causes or intentions.
llama_interpretation: One's true character is revealed outside of their comfort zone or familiar environment.

yoruba: Wàrà-wàrà là ńyọ oró iná.
english_literal: When one is on fire one's reaction is extremely agile.
interpretation_gold: One should not delay in exacting vengeance for a wrong.
deepseek_translation: It is slowly that one removes the thorn of fire.
claude_translation: It is gently that we remove the thorn of fire
gemini_translation: Quickly, quickly is how one extracts the venom of a snake.
mistral_translation: It is quickly that we drink the juice of the fire plant.
llama_translation: The scattered ones are the ones that fill the basket of firewood.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb advises patience and caution when dealing with difficult or dangerous situations.
claude_interpretation: Delicate or dangerous situations require careful, patient handling rather than forceful or hasty approaches.
gemini_interpretation: Swift action is required to address urgent and dangerous situations effectively.
mistral_interpretation: Hasty actions often lead to unnecessary trouble or suffering.
llama_interpretation: Unity and cooperation are essential for achieving a common goal.

yoruba: Wéré-wéré lọmọdé ḿbọ oko èèsì.
english_literal: A child's journey home from a nettle bush is fast indeed.
interpretation_gold: Painful problems enforce quick attention.
deepseek_translation: Little by little, the child carries the ant's nest.
claude_translation: It is playfully that a child enters a farm of thorns
gemini_translation: Quickly, quickly is how a child comes from the farm of the yam beetle.
mistral_translation: It is in a hurry that a child goes to the farm of recklessness.
llama_translation: The foolish child goes to the farm with a calabash.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that persistence and gradual effort lead to achieving significant goals.
claude_interpretation: Children often get into dangerous situations because they act without understanding the consequences of their actions.
gemini_interpretation: Children are quick to abandon tasks that are difficult or unpleasant.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb warns against hasty or impulsive actions, as they often lead to mistakes or regret.
llama_interpretation: One should not send an inexperienced or unprepared person on an important task.

yoruba: Wọ́n ní, “Afọ́jú, o ò tanná alẹ́.” Ó ní àtọ̀sán àtòru, èwo lòún rí níbẹ?
english_literal: People said, “Blind man, you did not light a lamp.” He asked, night or day, which one would his eyes register?
interpretation_gold: One should not waste one's efforts in procuring things one cannot use.
deepseek_translation: They said, "Blind one, you do not light the evening lamp." He said morning and night, what do you see there?
claude_translation: They said, 'Blind person, you did not light the evening lamp.' He said, 'Day and night, what difference does he see there?'
gemini_translation: They said, "Blind person, you did not light a lamp at night." He replied, "Day and night, which one do I see there?"
mistral_translation: They said, 'Blind person, you do not light the lamp at night.' He said, 'Daytime and nighttime, which one do I see in?'
llama_translation: They said, 'Afoju, you don't know the night.' He said, 'I know the dawn, what do I need to know the night for?'
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes hypocrisy by pointing out the inconsistency in someone's actions or words.
claude_interpretation: People should not be criticized for failing to do things that are meaningless or impossible for them given their circumstances.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the futility of expecting someone to perform a task that is inherently impossible or irrelevant to their condition.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the futility of expecting someone to perform a task they are inherently incapable of due to their limitations.
llama_interpretation: One who has experienced the dawn of a situation can infer the nature of the preceding night.

yoruba: Wọ́n ní, “Afọ́jú, ọmo-ọ̀ ẹ-ẹ́ pẹran.” Ó ní kò dá òun lójú, àfi bí òún bá tọ́ ọ wò.
english_literal: They said to the blind man, “Blind man, you son has killed a game.” He responds that he cannot believe them until he has tasted the meat.
interpretation_gold: Always insist on proof positive.
deepseek_translation: They said, 'Blind person, your child is missing.' He replied that it does not concern him, unless he sees the child himself.
claude_translation: They said, 'Blind person, your child killed an animal.' He said it doesn't concern him, unless he touches it to confirm.
gemini_translation: They said, 'Blind man, your child has killed an animal.' He said he wasn't sure, unless he touched it.
mistral_translation: They said, 'Blind person, your child is a goat.' He replied, 'It does not matter to me, as long as I can see it.'
llama_translation: They said, 'Afoju, the child of the one who is not at home is troublesome.' He said he did not look at him, unless he had grown up to look at him.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of personal verification and not relying solely on others' words.
claude_interpretation: One should not accept claims or accusations without personal verification, even when they involve matters close to you.
gemini_interpretation: One should not rely solely on hearsay or external reports, but rather seek personal verification or experience to confirm the truth.
mistral_interpretation: A person should not be concerned with others' mockery if they are confident in their own judgment or situation.
llama_interpretation: One should not pay attention to a child's misbehavior until they have matured and can be held accountable.

yoruba: “Wo ọmọ-ọ̀ mi dè mí”: ó ńlo kíjìpá mẹ́ta gbó; mélòó ni ọlọ́mọ-ọ́ máa lò gbó?
english_literal: “Look after the child for me”: she wears three durable hand-loom wrappers to tatters; how many would the mother of the child herself wear out?
interpretation_gold: The caretaker should not use up all his own resources for the benefit of his/her employer.
deepseek_translation: "Look at my child supporting me": he is walking with three walking sticks; how many will the child use to walk?
claude_translation: "Look, my child has grown up": he is using three bundles of firewood to cook; how many bundles will the parent use to cook?
gemini_translation: “Watch my child for me”: he uses three pieces of thick cloth to cover himself; how many will the child's owner use to cover himself?
mistral_translation: “Look at my child for me”: he is going to tie three knots; how many knots will the parent of the child use?
llama_translation: My child saw me: he is going to cut three yams; how many yams will my child cut?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against overburdening or exploiting the younger generation, as it may leave them without resources for their own future.
claude_interpretation: If a child already consumes so much, the parent who raised them will naturally need even more resources.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the tendency for people to be more protective or cautious of things that belong to others than they are of their own.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights that parents naturally bear greater responsibility and effort for their children than others would.
llama_interpretation: A child will imitate and possibly surpass their parent's actions.

yoruba: Wolé-wolé kì í wolé agbọ́n láì tẹ́.
english_literal: The sanitary inspector does not inspect a wasp's home without coming to grief.
interpretation_gold: One should be cautious in performing one's duties.
deepseek_translation: Slowly-slowly does not enter the wasp's nest without being stung.
claude_translation: Enter-enter does not enter the wise person's house without stepping carefully
gemini_translation: A house inspector does not inspect a beehive without being stung.
mistral_translation: A stealthy person does not enter a beehive without getting stung
llama_translation: The one who enters the house first does not enter the parlor first.
deepseek_interpretation: Caution is necessary even when proceeding carefully in dangerous situations.
claude_interpretation: A wise person does not allow just anyone to enter their private space or affairs without proper consideration and caution.
gemini_interpretation: One cannot engage with a dangerous or difficult situation without facing its inherent risks or consequences.
