mistral_interpretation: Caution and preparation are necessary when dealing with risky or delicate situations
llama_interpretation: One's initial success or advantage does not guarantee ultimate success or recognition.

yoruba: Ọgbọ́n ọlọgbọ́n ò jẹ́ ká pe àgbà ní wèrè.
english_literal: Other people's wisdom saves the elder from being called a lunatic.
interpretation_gold: The person who can learn from others will avoid a lot of embarrassment.
deepseek_translation: The wisdom of the wise does not allow us to call an elder a fool.
claude_translation: The wisdom of a wise person does not allow us to call an elder a fool
gemini_translation: The wisdom of the wise prevents us from calling an elder a fool.
mistral_translation: The wisdom of the wise does not allow us to call an elder a fool
llama_translation: The elder who is wise is not called an elder because of madness
deepseek_interpretation: Respect for elders is paramount, and their wisdom should not be dismissed lightly.
claude_interpretation: True wisdom teaches us to respect our elders and avoid insulting them, regardless of circumstances.
gemini_interpretation: Respect for elders and their accumulated wisdom prevents younger generations from dismissing their perspectives, even when they seem unconventional.
mistral_interpretation: Respect for elders demands that we overlook their mistakes rather than openly criticize them
llama_interpretation: Wisdom and good judgment are essential qualities of a respected elder.

yoruba: Ọlọ́jà kì í wípé kọ́jà ó tú.
english_literal: The owner of the market never wishes the market to be disrupted.
interpretation_gold: People always want the best outcome for their ventures.
deepseek_translation: The market does not say it is not passable, it just is.
claude_translation: A trader does not say that trade has scattered/failed.
gemini_translation: A market seller does not say that the market should scatter.
mistral_translation: The owner of the market does not say the market should close.
llama_translation: The owner of the house does not say the house is old.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that challenges or obstacles do not announce themselves; they simply exist and must be faced.
claude_interpretation: People do not speak negatively about their own livelihood or source of income.
gemini_interpretation: People do not intentionally wish for the failure or disruption of their own source of livelihood or well-being.
mistral_interpretation: A leader or person in authority should not abandon their responsibilities or neglect their duties.
llama_interpretation: One should not speak negatively about their own family or heritage.

yoruba: Ẹní gbọ́n juni lọ ní ńtẹni nÍfá.
english_literal: It is someone wiser than one who consults the oracle for one.
interpretation_gold: One receives advice only from those qualified to offer it.
deepseek_translation: The person who is wiser than another is the one who consults Ifa.
claude_translation: The one who is wiser goes ahead and consults Ifa for the person
gemini_translation: He who is wiser than us is the one who initiates us into Ifá.
mistral_translation: The one who hears the wisdom of the elders is the one who owns Ifá (divination wisdom).
llama_translation: The person who is skilled in Ifá is the one who knows the secrets of the forest
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of seeking wisdom and guidance from Ifa, the Yoruba divination system, as a mark of true intelligence.
claude_interpretation: A wise person takes initiative to seek spiritual guidance or solutions on behalf of others who may not know how to help themselves.
gemini_interpretation: One should seek guidance and knowledge from those who are more experienced and knowledgeable.
mistral_interpretation: Respecting and learning from elders grants access to profound knowledge and guidance.
llama_interpretation: True wisdom and knowledge come from those who have mastered the ancient traditions and mysteries.

yoruba: Ẹni àìgbọ́n pa ló pọ̀; ẹni ọgbọ́n pa ò tó ǹkan.
english_literal: People killed by folly are innumerable; people killed by wisdom are few.
interpretation_gold: Few things kill more surely than folly.
deepseek_translation: The number of foolish people killed is many; the number of wise people killed is not much.
claude_translation: Those who lack wisdom kill many; those who wisdom kills are not much.
gemini_translation: Those killed by foolishness are many; those killed by wisdom are few.
mistral_translation: The one without wisdom kills many; the one with wisdom does not kill enough things.
llama_translation: The one who does not hear dies; the one who hears does not die.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that foolish actions often lead to greater harm or consequences compared to wise actions.
claude_interpretation: Foolish actions cause widespread harm and destruction, while wisdom rarely leads to negative consequences.
gemini_interpretation: Foolish decisions and actions lead to more negative consequences than wise ones.
mistral_interpretation: A foolish person causes widespread harm, while even a wise person may not be able to prevent all problems.
llama_interpretation: Listening to advice or warnings can save one from harm or death.

yoruba: Ẹni tó máa tẹ́ òkú ọ̀pọ̀lọ́, yó nìí ilé ògbóni tirẹ̀ lọ́tọ̀.
english_literal: Whoever wishes to lay a dead toad in state will have to build his own cult shrine separately.
interpretation_gold: Whoever wishes to do the absurd should not expect the cooperation or approval of others.
deepseek_translation: The person who will bury a dead frog will have his own wisdom house outside.
claude_translation: The person who will step on many frogs will have their own ogboni house destroyed.
gemini_translation: He who will bury a toad will have his own private Ogboni house.
mistral_translation: Whoever will step on a toad's corpse will surely enter his own Ogboni lodge in a similar manner
llama_translation: The person who is going to die on the road, his spirit is already in the house of the elders.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that those who engage in foolish or unnecessary tasks will face the consequences of their actions.
claude_interpretation: Those who harm or disrespect many others will eventually face consequences that destroy their own position of honor or authority.
gemini_interpretation: Undertaking a difficult or unusual task requires special preparation and resources.
mistral_interpretation: One will face consequences or retribution in the same way they have treated others
llama_interpretation: One's fate is predetermined and cannot be changed.

yoruba: Ọsán gbé ojú ọrun le kókó; bó bá wọ odò, a di ọ̀-rọ̀-pọ̀jọ̀-pọ̀jọ̀.
english_literal: The bow-string is taut while it remains on the bow; dipped into the river it becomes very soft indeed.
interpretation_gold: One thrives on one's home ground where conditions are ideal; in hostile territory one becomes helpless.
deepseek_translation: The sun carries the face of heaven lightly; when it enters the river, it becomes a water beetle.
claude_translation: The sun makes the sky bright and clear; when it enters the river, it becomes scattered and fragmented.
gemini_translation: The sun hardens the sky; if it enters the river, it becomes soft and mushy.
mistral_translation: The orange peels the sky's face; if it enters the river, it becomes wrinkled and shrunken.
llama_translation: The moon rises with its face to the sky, but when it enters the river, it becomes rippled.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should adapt to circumstances with humility and flexibility, as even the mighty sun appears small when reflected in water.
claude_interpretation: Things that appear strong and unified can become weak and divided when they enter an unfamiliar or hostile environment.
gemini_interpretation: Circumstances dictate the nature and behavior of things, as what is firm in one environment may become pliable in another.
mistral_interpretation: A person who appears impressive in one setting may lose their dignity or influence in another.
llama_interpretation: Even the most serene and composed person can become disturbed or flustered when faced with challenging circumstances.

yoruba: Ọ̀bẹ ńwólé ara ẹ̀ ó ní òún ḿba àkọ̀ jẹ́.
english_literal: The knife is destroying its own home, it says it is ruining the sheath.
interpretation_gold: Said of people whose actions will hurt them more than they will hurt other people.
deepseek_translation: The knife enters its own sheath and says it does not associate with the scabbard.
claude_translation: The knife that enters its own body says it is eating with the handle
gemini_translation: The knife is entering its sheath and says it is spoiling the sheath.
mistral_translation: The knife is cutting into its own handle, yet it claims it is sharpening the hoe
llama_translation: Soup is entering the body, it is the stomach that knows it is hot
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb criticizes hypocrisy, pointing out when someone denies their obvious connections or dependencies.
claude_interpretation: Self-destructive behavior is often rationalized or justified by those who engage in it.
gemini_interpretation: One should not blame others for their own actions or natural consequences.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against self-destructive actions while blaming others for the harm caused.
llama_interpretation: One's inner self knows one's true feelings or condition, even if outward appearances suggest otherwise.

yoruba: Ọmọdé kì í ní ina níle kí tòde má jòó o.
english_literal: A child does not have fire at home and therefore escape being burned by the fire abroad.
interpretation_gold: Being secure and well respected in one's home does not save one from vicissitudes outside the home.
deepseek_translation: A child does not have fire at home and go outside to feel cold.
claude_translation: A child does not have fire at home and go outside to warm themselves.
gemini_translation: A child does not have fire at home and the outside is not burning.
mistral_translation: A child does not have fire in the house and ask a neighbor to lend some.
llama_translation: A child does not have fire in the house and still go to warm up outside
deepseek_interpretation: One should appreciate and utilize the resources available to them rather than seeking elsewhere.
claude_interpretation: One should utilize the resources and opportunities available at home before seeking them elsewhere.
gemini_interpretation: One should not neglect their immediate responsibilities or problems while focusing on external matters.
mistral_interpretation: It advises against neglecting one's own resources while seeking help from others.
llama_interpretation: One should utilize the resources available at home before seeking external help.

yoruba: Ẹni tó bá ní igbà-á lò, bí igbà-á bá já, kó dúró so ó.
english_literal: If one must use a tree-climbing rope and it breaks, one must pause to repair it.
interpretation_gold: One must make the time to attend to chores that must be performed.
deepseek_translation: Whoever has a calabash should use it, if the calabash breaks, let them stand and mend it.
claude_translation: One who has a calabash to use, if the calabash breaks, let him stand and cry for it
gemini_translation: He who has a rope to use, if the rope breaks, he should wait to tie it.
mistral_translation: Whoever has their own time, if the time breaks, let them stand and say it
llama_translation: Whoever has a calabash, when the calabash breaks, he will not stay there
deepseek_interpretation: One should make use of what they have and take responsibility for repairing or replacing it if it gets damaged.
claude_interpretation: When you lose something valuable that you depended on, it's natural and acceptable to grieve the loss.
gemini_interpretation: One should be prepared to mend and maintain their resources if they wish to continue using them effectively.
mistral_interpretation: One should take responsibility for their own actions or circumstances when things go wrong.
llama_interpretation: One should be prepared to move on when a situation or relationship becomes unworkable.

yoruba: Ẹni tó bá fi ojù àná wòkú, ẹbọra a bọ́ ọ láṣọ.
english_literal: Whoever looks at the dead with yesterday's eyes will be stripped naked by the spirits.
interpretation_gold: One behaves towards people according to the heights they have attained, not according to the way they used to be.
deepseek_translation: The person who looks at a corpse with yesterday's eyes, the ghost will dress them in clothes.
claude_translation: One who looks at a corpse with yesterday's eyes, spirits will clothe them in cloth.
gemini_translation: He who looks at a corpse with yesterday's eyes, the spirit will strip him naked.
mistral_translation: Whoever looks at the corpse with yesterday's eyes will have their clothes covered with dust from the spirit world
llama_translation: Whoever uses their eyes to look at death, the deity will clothe them in a shroud.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against dwelling on past misfortunes, as it can lead to further harm or misfortune.
claude_interpretation: Those who dwell on past sorrows or refuse to accept present realities will be consumed by spiritual consequences or misfortune.
gemini_interpretation: One must adapt their perspective to new realities, as clinging to old ways in changed circumstances can lead to severe consequences.
mistral_interpretation: One should not judge current situations based solely on past experiences, as circumstances change and require fresh perspectives.
llama_interpretation: One who recklessly courts danger will ultimately meet with disaster.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a wífún kó gbọ́; ẹni tí kò gbọ́, tara-a rẹ̀ ni yó dà.
english_literal: Let the person one advises heed one; the heedless person places himself at risk.
interpretation_gold: Those who refuse instruction lay the foundation for their own ruin.
deepseek_translation: The person who is warned listens; the person who does not listen, it is their own body that will suffer.
claude_translation: The person who is told to listen should listen; the person who does not listen will test it on themselves.
gemini_translation: The one who is told should listen; the one who does not listen, it is their own business that will be ruined.
mistral_translation: The one we anointed will hear; the one who does not hear will destroy their own body.
llama_translation: The person we are calling is not hearing; the person who is not hearing, it is his ear that is at fault.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that ignoring advice leads to personal consequences.
claude_interpretation: Those who refuse to heed good advice will learn through their own painful experience.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of heeding advice, as ignoring it will ultimately lead to personal detriment.
mistral_interpretation: Those who heed advice will benefit, while those who ignore it will suffer the consequences.
llama_interpretation: One is responsible for their own lack of understanding or awareness.
